description: Make Printyx print shop management SaaS enterprise-grade, professional, and production-ready. Platform: React 18 + TypeScript + Express + PostgreSQL (Drizzle ORM) + Supabase. Architecture: multi-tenant 4-tier hierarchy (Platform > Company > Regional > Location), 8-level RBAC, 213 pages, 127 route files, 91 services, 51 schema files. Quality checks: npm run check (typecheck), npm run test (unit tests), npm run lint (eslint), npm run build (vite build).

userStories.title: Set up Drizzle migration system replacing db:push
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need proper database migrations instead of db:push so schema changes are versioned, auditable, and safely deployable to production without data loss.
acceptanceCriteria: Configure drizzle-kit to generate migration SQL files in a drizzle/migrations/ directory
drizzle-kit migrate applies pending migrations in order
Add npm scripts: db:generate, db:migrate, db:migrate:status
Create an initial baseline migration from the current schema in shared/schema.ts
Add a migration lockfile pattern to prevent concurrent migrations in production
Update the Database section in CLAUDE.md with new migration workflow replacing db:push references
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently using db:push which is not safe for production. Drizzle supports generate+migrate workflow. Main schema: shared/schema.ts (293KB) with 43 additional files in shared/*-schema.ts. Forecasting DB config: drizzle.forecasting.config.ts. See drizzle.config.ts for current setup.

userStories.title: Fix a cluster of type-safety bugs in server/shared core files
userStories.description: As a maintainer, several core server + shared-schema files contain real type-safety bugs that tsc flags (and that mask runtime defects). Fix the highest-value cluster: the structured logger silently DROPPED the error/meta argument when called message-first (errors never reached the logs in prod); an async method was typed boolean instead of Promise<boolean>; two Zod schemas were malformed (marginAnalysisReport was a raw object so z.infer produced an error type; insertCalculatorSessionSchema refined a non-existent email column); a self-referencing FK was untyped; and Set iteration needed downlevelIteration.
acceptanceCriteria: Logger calls of the form log.error("msg", errOrMeta) converted to pino object-first form so the error/meta is actually logged (fixes silent log-data-drop) and types pass — apiErrorHandler, error-sanitizer, company-id-generator, websocket-service (7 sites)
websocket-service.isRealTimeReport typed Promise<boolean> (was async ...: boolean — a real bug)
marginAnalysisReport wrapped in z.object so z.infer<MarginAnalysisReport> resolves (was an error type)
Bogus email refinement removed from insertCalculatorSessionSchema (email is on calculatorLeads, not calculatorSessions)
platform-crm self-referencing reportsToId FK typed via AnyPgColumn
user-lifecycle transferDetails index signature widened to number | undefined to match optional members
schema.ts totalPaid decimal default corrected to string (.default("0")) matching every other decimal default in the file
downlevelIteration enabled + illustrative *.example.ts excluded from typecheck scope
All targeted tsc errors in these specific files resolved (verified: 0 remaining) with no new errors introduced in them
NOTE: this does NOT make npm run check globally green — see QUALITY-002 (6176 pre-existing errors repo-wide)
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-06-25 (QUALITY-001). Scope corrected mid-flight: an earlier `npm run check | tail` had hidden the true error count — the full tsc run shows 6176 pre-existing errors repo-wide (5013 server/shared + 1163 client), so this codebase has never typechecked clean and global-green is a large separate effort (tracked as QUALITY-002). This story fixes the highest-value correctness cluster I found and VERIFIES those specific errors are gone (grep of the fresh tsc log shows 0 remaining in websocket-service.ts, utils/apiErrorHandler.ts, error-sanitizer.ts, company-id-generator.ts, platform-crm-schema.ts, print-cost-calculator-schema.ts, product-pricing-schema.ts, user-lifecycle-schema.ts, schema.ts:2685). Most valuable fixes: (1) the structured logger silently dropped the 2nd arg on message-first calls, so caught errors never reached logs in prod — now logged via {err}; (2) marginAnalysisReport z.infer was broken; (3) isRealTimeReport async-return-type bug. Changes are non-additive (relaxing tsconfig + type-correcting code). Build (vite/esbuild) was never gated on tsc so this changes no shipped behavior except the corrected/improved logging.

BATCH 13 (2026-06-26): server-wide req.session.user typing — the single highest-leverage root cause remaining. ENV NOTE: this container shipped with an EMPTY node_modules (no typescript/@types/node/vite), so npx tsc resolved a stray GLOBAL TS 6.0.2 and reported a bogus ~2 errors (deprecation-only) off a stale incremental cache. Ran `npm ci` to restore the pinned local TS 5.6.3 (the CI toolchain): TRUE count was 3577 baseline -> 3507 after upstream merges. ALWAYS verify node_modules is populated before trusting a tsc count. ROOT CAUSE: 500 TS2339 across 19 files all = "Property 'user' does not exist on type 'Session & Partial<SessionData>'". Two access patterns: direct (req.session.user.tenantId, 5 files: apollo/email-marketing/field-service/lease/signature) and destructured (const user = req.session?.user; 11 files: advanced-billing/automated-billing/customer-success/geofence-alerts/gps-tracking/lead-scoring/manufacturer-order/mfa/mileage/route-optimization/workflow-automation). LATENT RUNTIME BUG FOUND: nothing populates req.session.user — session login (auth-routes.ts) sets FLAT req.session.userId/req.session.tenantId, and these 19 routers mount with NO auth middleware, so every `if (!req.session.user?.tenantId)` guard always 401s at runtime. FIX (type-only, zero runtime risk — chosen over a login-flow change that's security-sensitive and unverifiable with the broken build): new server/types/express-session.d.ts declaring `interface SessionData { user?: {...} }`. Made id+tenantId REQUIRED string (auth-critical, always set together when a user exists) so `if (!user)` guards narrow them to string for downstream storage calls — keeping them optional left 209 string|undefined TS2345/TS2322. role/roleLevel/role_level/email/firstName/fullName/twoFactorEnabled/twoFactorSecret optional (every field the route layer reads; types confirmed from usage e.g. role.toLowerCase(), roleLevel||...||1). Removing the any-poisoning (req.session.user TS2339 -> any propagated through {...data, tenantId:any}) re-typed 6 pre-existing field-service errors any->string (same locations, NOT new) and surfaced ONE new: mfa-routes.ts(813) user.email string|undefined into sendEmailOtp(email:string) — fixed faithfully with a `if (!user.email) return 400` guard (can't email-OTP without an email; also narrows). VERIFIED: ratchet 3507 -> 3017 (-490); `comm` on file+line+col+code shows ZERO genuinely-new error locations. Baseline tightened 3577 -> 3017. Documented latent always-401 bug for a follow-up story (populate req.session.user at login OR migrate the 19 routes to getUserId/getTenantId helpers). prettier clean; server/ eslint-ignored. Build still pre-existing-broken (@sentry/react absent). passes STAYS false (tsc not yet green; cumulative 6176 -> 3017, -51%).

DELIBERATELY NOT DELETED, each with a reason rather than a guess: server/routes-intelligent-alerts.ts (2 errors) — unregistered router, but its IntelligentAlertsService has a real unit suite (server/tests/unit/intelligent-alerts.test.ts), so register-vs-delete is a product call, not a typecheck fix; the demo/seed cluster server/{auth-setup,role-seeder,initialize-roles,setup-demo-data}.ts (3 errors total) — unreachable from every entry point, but they are hand-invoked ops tooling (tsx server/setup-demo-data.ts), and deleting operator tooling because a graph walk cannot see a human typing it is the wrong inference. SEPARATELY, A DOC BUG THIS SURFACED: CLAUDE.md's auth-middleware table says requireAuth may be imported from './auth-setup'. Nothing in the repo does — the only importer of auth-setup.ts is the dead setup-demo-data.ts. The table entry is stale; left in place because correcting it is a CLAUDE.md edit, not this batch. VERIFICATION: tsc 1083->1067; TS2307 count UNCHANGED at 4 (no dangling imports created by the deletions); ESLint 11994->11916 (-78), baseline tightened; check:nav green (42 known, 321 routes); unit suite byte-identical to the clean tree (26 files / 10 tests failing BOTH before and after — they need a live DB this container lacks, so they are pre-existing, not regressions). PRE-EXISTING FAILURE FOUND ON CLEAN MAIN, NOT CAUSED HERE AND NOT FIXED HERE: npm run check:routes FAILS on an untouched checkout of main — 1 new ambiguous-ownership route (/api/custom-fields, both Express + edge and not proxied) and 3 new missing-edge routes that will 404 in PROD (/api/ai-employees, /api/email-sequences, /api/web-forms). Confirmed by stashing this batch and re-running: byte-identical output. Worth its own story. I did NOT run --update-baseline on docs/route-ownership-baseline.json even though this batch resolved one domain, because doing so would silently absorb those four upstream regressions into the baseline. | BATCH 13 (ESignatureIntegration.tsx, 22 errs -> 0; ratchet 1046 -> 1024) - a PHANTOM-SHAPE page whose WRITE path was fully broken, which the error count alone did not reveal. CLAUDE.md already flagged this file under EDGE-005e as 'built against a MOCK camelCase shape... that data-contract rewrite is a separate story'; that was half right. A previous pass (PA-036) had already added a mapSignatureRequest normalizer, so the READ path rendered - but it hardcoded every phantom field to empty (documentUrl:'', remindersSent:0, contractValue:undefined, signers:[]), which quietly turned three UI blocks into permanent dead space rather than fixing them. THE REAL BUG WAS THE CREATE FORM: supabase/functions/signatures/handlers/requests.ts requires request_number + title + provider on POST, and the form sent documentName/documentType/contractValue/contractDuration/expirationDays - NONE of the three - so every submit 400'd with VALIDATION_ERROR. Fixed by rebinding to real columns: documentName->title; documentType->provider (its options were document categories like 'service_agreement' for which the table has NO column - provider is the only categorical column and is what analytics groups by); businessRecordId->customerId; added emailSubject; expirationDays converted client-side to an absolute expiresAt (the column is a timestamp, not a day count). request_number is now generated IN THE HANDLER when absent - it is NOT NULL and unique per tenant, so no client can safely invent one and there was no field for it. DELETED (no backing column, per the BATCH-7 rule): contractValue + contractDuration form inputs and the card's 'Value' tile (which always read N/A). REPLACED WITH REAL COLUMNS instead of deleting, where the table had an equivalent: the Value tile now shows signers_completed of total_signers, and the reminder line now reports reminder_enabled/reminder_days instead of a remindersSent count that does not exist. customerName is resolved against the customer list the page ALREADY loads, keyed by customer_id - deliberately client-side, because signature_requests.customer_id could reference either `customers` or `business_records` (the COP-B00 contradiction) and a wrong backend join would be worse than a lookup. TWO REUSABLE LESSONS: (1) a normalizer that maps phantom fields to empty constants SILENCES the type errors and hides the defect - check whether the mapper is inventing blanks before trusting a page that 'renders fine'; (2) tsc error count measures the READ path only - the create/update path of a phantom-shape page can be 100% broken while contributing ZERO errors, so always diff the form's submitted keys against what the handler accepts. | BATCH 14 (EnhancedOnboardingForm.tsx, 12 errs -> 0; ratchet 1024 -> 1012) - THE HEADLINE IS THAT TWO OF THESE 12 ERRORS WERE A HARD CRASH, not a type nit. TS2448/TS2454 'Block-scoped variable form used before its declaration' at the top of the component: a useEffect prefilling from URL params sat 45 lines ABOVE the useForm() call, and a dependency array is evaluated DURING RENDER, so `[form]` threw ReferenceError: Cannot access 'form' before initialization on every mount and the page white-screened. Both /onboarding/new and /onboarding/enhanced are live routes and WarehouseOperations.tsx:840 links into the second with ?orderId=... - exactly the flow that prefill exists for. Fixed by moving the effect below the declaration. TAKEAWAY: treat TS2448/TS2454 as a RUNTIME BUG REPORT, not a lint - they are among the few tsc codes that guarantee a throw, so grep the remaining baseline for them before picking a batch by error count. SECOND REAL BUG, zero-error-adjacent: the Review step's Network Configuration panel read networkConfig.customerNumber, networkConfig.dhcpEnabled and networkConfig.defaultGateway - NONE of which exist on that zod object (the real fields are ipAssignment/gateway/dnsServers, and customerNumber lives on customerData). The panel printed 'Not specified' for 3 of 4 rows no matter what the user typed. Rebound to the real fields. Same class as BATCH 13's dead UI: a phantom READ through form.watch() is silent, because watch() returns undefined rather than erroring. THIRD: equipmentItems useState inferred its element type from the initial literal, where `replacedEquipment: {}` inferred as `{}` - so every item.replacedEquipment?.oldMake read was TS2339 and the nested objects had no shape at all. Fixed by typing the state as EnhancedOnboardingFormData['equipment'][number] (derive the element type from the schema, do not re-declare it). Plus two mechanical fixes: `as const` cannot be applied to a CONDITIONAL expression (TS1355) - put it on each literal branch; and new Date(form.watch(x)) where x is z.string().optional() needs a guard, since new Date(undefined) matches no overload. | BATCH 14b - ACTED ON THE BATCH-14 LESSON IMMEDIATELY, and it paid: swept the whole remaining baseline for the tsc codes that GUARANTEE A RUNTIME THROW rather than describing a type mismatch (TS2448 used-before-declaration, TS2454 used-before-assigned, TS2304 cannot-find-name, TS2552 cannot-find-name-did-you-mean) instead of picking the next file by error count. Outside the already-known predictive-service-dispatch phantom-table file this found exactly two, and BOTH were endpoints that threw on every single call: (1) POST /api/contract-renewal/proposals/:id/send destructured `sendVia` from req.body but wrote the SHORTHAND `sentVia,` into the drizzle .set() - an undeclared identifier, so sending a renewal proposal was a guaranteed ReferenceError. The column is sentVia, the body field is sendVia; now mapped explicitly. A shorthand property whose name differs by one letter from the in-scope variable is invisible in review - worth grepping for. (2) The conversion-funnel query in routes-signup-crm.ts wrote `const count = await db.select({ count: count() })...` - the local shadowed drizzle's imported count() aggregate AND was referenced inside its own initializer, throwing 'Cannot access count before initialization' and failing the whole endpoint. Renamed to `rows`. SAME SHADOWING SHAPE AS THE BATCH-14 CRASH, different mechanism, so it is a recurring pattern in this codebase, not a one-off. Ratchet 1012 -> 1009. REMAINING guaranteed-throw errors are ONLY the ~60 TS2304s in routes-predictive-service-dispatch.ts (serviceCallsEnhanced / equipmentMetrics / technicianResourcesEnhanced / equipment), which reference tables in NO schema or migration - CLAUDE.md already records that as needing new schema tables + a migration, not an import fix, so it stays deferred. RECOMMENDATION: make this sweep a permanent gate. These four codes should be a HARD ZERO (excluding that one deferred file), not part of a counted ratchet - they are bug reports, and letting them sit inside a 1009-error budget is what hid three live crashes. | HARD GATE SHIPPED 2026-08-19 (acting on the BATCH-14b recommendation rather than leaving it as a note): scripts/check-throwing-types.mjs + npm run check:throwing-types, wired into ci.yml. TS2304/TS2552/TS2448/TS2454 are now gated at ZERO instead of being counted by the check-types ratchet. Rationale, which is the reusable part: a ratchet is right for type debt but WRONG for these four codes, because they do not describe a mismatch - they guarantee a ReferenceError the first time the line runs. Three live crashes were found in one sweep precisely because a 1000+ error budget gave them somewhere to hide. Exclusions live in the script as a Map from file -> the reason it cannot be fixed by editing that file alone, so a reviewer can check the reason; there is exactly ONE today. MUTATION-TESTED against the two REAL crashes it exists to catch (not a synthetic case): reintroducing the signup-crm `const count` that shadowed drizzle's count() inside its own initializer, and the contract-renewal `sentVia,` shorthand one letter off from `sendVia`, each exit 1 at the right line; restoring passes.

The activity timeline can leverage existing deal activities API (GET /api/deals-management/deals/:id/activities). Associated records use existing relationship data. Reference: CRM_Layout.md 'Deal record page layout' section: 'Header: name, stage/pipeline, quick actions. Left: editable property groups. Center: timeline with filters and compose inputs. Right: pluggable cards for associated entities.'

userStories.title: Build board options and in-context configuration UIs
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need a 'Board options' menu on the pipeline board that lets me configure card content, column display, and board settings without leaving the board view, matching HubSpot's in-context configuration pattern.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Board options' button in top-right of board view opens a dropdown menu with: Edit Cards, Edit Columns, Board Settings

'Edit Cards' opens a right-side slide-over panel (CardConfigPanel.tsx): list of available properties with drag handles for reorder, toggle to show/hide each property on cards, tag display toggle, card style selector (compact/standard/detailed), 'Apply for myself' vs 'Apply for everyone' radio
'Edit Columns' panel: toggle visibility of pipeline stages as columns, reorder columns, configure column total display (sum/count/weighted/average/none), column color customization
'Board Settings' panel: default sort within columns (newest first, highest value, closest close date), card limit per column before 'Show more' button, auto-refresh interval
Changes preview live on the board as user configures
Save button applies changes and persists to board_card_configs table (CRM-004) and saved_views boardConfig (CRM-001)
Cancel button reverts all preview changes
Admin-level changes (Apply for everyone) show a confirmation: 'This will change the board for all team members using this view'
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: This story provides the configuration UIs for CRM-004 (card configs). HubSpot has two levels: global admin setup (Objects > Deals > Pipelines in settings) and in-context configuration (Edit board, Card setup) for power users. This story focuses on the in-context configuration. The global admin setup is handled by the existing PipelineConfiguration.tsx page. Reference: CRM_Layout.md 'Deal card design and customization' and 'Practical build strategy' step 5.

userStories.title: Apply unified CRM index pattern to contacts, companies, and all object types
userStories.description: As a platform user, I need contacts, companies, and other CRM object types to use the same unified index/board/record page patterns as deals, so the entire CRM feels consistent and professional like HubSpot where every object type shares the same UX.
acceptanceCriteria: CrmIndexShell from CRM-002 accepts objectType as a generic parameter and renders appropriate columns/fields per type
Contacts page (/contacts) uses CrmIndexShell with objectType='contacts': table view with inline editing, filter bar with contact-specific quick filters (company, email domain, last contacted)
Companies page (/companies) uses CrmIndexShell with objectType='companies': table view with inline editing, filter bar with company-specific quick filters (industry, size, territory)
Leads page (/leads) uses CrmIndexShell with objectType='leads' including board view with lead stages
Each object type defines its own: available properties for card config, default saved views, quick filter fields, default table columns
Create a shared object type registry: client/src/lib/crm-object-registry.ts that maps each objectType to its config (fields, filters, views, board support, record layout)
Board view is only available for object types that have pipelines (deals, leads, opportunities); contacts and companies show table view only with option to group by a field
Saved views are scoped per objectType - deal views don't show in contacts
Record detail pages for contacts and companies use RecordPageLayout from CRM-008 with object-specific layout configs
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: HubSpot's core UX principle: 'Contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and custom objects all share the same basic index + board + record patterns.' This story generalizes the deals-specific work from CRM-002 through CRM-009 into a generic object view system. The object registry pattern lets each type define its behavior. Existing pages to refactor: Contacts.tsx, CustomersPage.tsx, CompanyContacts.tsx, ProspectsPage.tsx. Reference: CRM_Layout.md 'Custom objects and extensible UI' section.

userStories.title: Complete frontend route permission guards for all 261 pages
userStories.description: As a security auditor, I need every frontend route to enforce permission checks so users cannot access pages by typing URLs directly, closing the ~180-page gap in navigation-permissions.ts coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all 261 routes in client/src/App.tsx against client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts
Add permission entries for every page missing from navigationPermissions map
Group missing pages by module: dashboards, equipment, billing, reports, admin, settings, integrations
Create a ProtectedRoute wrapper component that checks navigationPermissions before rendering
Wrap all lazy-loaded routes in App.tsx with ProtectedRoute
Unauthenticated users redirected to /login; authenticated users without permission see a 403 page with 'Request Access' link
Create a simple /unauthorized page component explaining the user lacks permission
Verify platform admin (level 8) can access all pages
Verify location-level user (level 1) is blocked from admin pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently only ~80 of 261 pages have permission rules in navigation-permissions.ts. Pages like /gpt5-dashboard, /social-media-generator, /autopilot-*, many admin pages lack guards. Users can bypass sidebar role filtering by navigating directly to URLs. The sidebar hides items but doesn't prevent access. Key files: client/src/App.tsx (261 routes), client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts (~80 entries), client/src/components/layout/RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx.

userStories.title: Standardize auth middleware imports across all 156 route files
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single consistent auth middleware pattern across all route files so security behavior is uniform and auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all server/routes-*.ts and server/routes/*.ts files for auth middleware usage
Replace all inline requireAuth definitions with centralized imports
Standardize on: import { requireSupabaseAuth as requireAuth } from './middleware/supabase-auth' for JWT auth
Ensure every route file uses getUserId(req) and getTenantId(req) from utils/auth-helpers instead of direct req.user access
Remove any duplicate middleware definitions found in individual route files
Create a lint rule or code comment convention documenting the standard pattern
Verify no route files define their own auth middleware inline
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Found ~8-10 different auth middleware patterns across route files. Some define requireAuth inline, some import from replitAuth, some from supabase-auth. This inconsistency makes security auditing difficult. CLAUDE.md documents the correct patterns but they aren't consistently followed.

userStories.title: Add granular RBAC permission checks to all CRUD and sensitive endpoints
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need every API endpoint that modifies data to enforce granular RBAC permissions (not just authentication) so users can only perform actions their role allows.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE endpoints across route files for requirePermission usage
Add requirePermission middleware to all data-modifying endpoints that currently only use requireAuth
DELETE endpoints require appropriate .delete permission (e.g., sales.lead.delete_own, admin.record.delete_all)
Bulk operation endpoints (/api/*/bulk-update, /api/*/bulk-delete) require elevated permissions (scope: _all or _team)
Settings/configuration endpoints require admin-level permissions
Export endpoints require appropriate .export permission
Document the complete permission matrix: endpoint → required permissions in a permissions-matrix.ts file
Add tests verifying permission denial returns 403 with descriptive message
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Many endpoints currently only check requireAuth (is the user logged in?) but not requirePermission (does the user have the right role/permission?). Bulk operations and DELETE routes are the highest risk. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts has full support for granular permissions but adoption is incomplete.

userStories.title: Eliminate legacy string-role checks and unify on enhanced RBAC system
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the codebase to use a single RBAC system instead of mixing legacy string role checks ('admin', 'root_admin') with the enhanced RBAC permission system.
acceptanceCriteria: Find all instances of legacy role string comparisons (role === 'admin', role === 'root_admin', role === 'manager', etc.) in server/ directory
Replace each with equivalent enhanced RBAC permission checks using requirePermission or hasPermission
Map legacy roles to their enhanced RBAC equivalents and document the mapping
Remove or deprecate the legacy role-to-permission mapping functions that bridge old and new systems
Update the roles seeder (npm run seed:rbac) to ensure all enhanced roles have complete permission sets
Verify platform admin bypass still works correctly through enhanced RBAC (level 8 auto-grants)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Two role systems exist: 'roles' table (frontend via PostgREST) and 'enhanced_roles' (backend RBAC). Legacy string checks create duplicate logic paths that are hard to audit. The enhanced RBAC system is complete and should be the single source of truth.

userStories.title: Add role-based UI element visibility throughout frontend
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I should only see buttons, menu items, and form fields that my role permits so the UI isn't cluttered with actions I can't perform.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a usePermission(permissionKey) hook that checks the current user's permissions client-side
Create a <PermissionGate permission='sales.quote.approve_standard'> wrapper component that conditionally renders children
Hide 'Delete' buttons for users without delete permissions on each entity
Hide 'Approve' buttons on quotes/orders for users below approval threshold
Hide 'Export' buttons for users without export permissions
Hide admin-only actions (user management, role assignment, tenant settings) for non-admin roles
Disable (don't hide) edit fields on records the user can view but not modify (e.g., view_own without edit_own)
Apply PermissionGate to at least: LeadsManagement, QuotesManagement, Invoices, Customers, Orders, and all Admin pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently the sidebar hides navigation items by role, but within pages all action buttons render regardless of permission. Users see 'Delete' and 'Approve' buttons that return 403 when clicked. This creates a frustrating UX. The backend already enforces permissions - the frontend just needs to match.

userStories.title: Add global search with Cmd/Ctrl+K shortcut and universal results
userStories.description: As any user, I need a global search bar accessible from anywhere in the app so I can quickly find leads, customers, quotes, orders, invoices, and contacts without navigating through menus.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a search icon/bar to the top header area, always visible on all pages
Cmd/Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut opens a search dialog overlay (command palette style)
Search queries hit GET /api/universal-search with debounced input (300ms)
Results grouped by entity type: Leads, Customers, Contacts, Quotes, Orders, Invoices, Equipment
Each result shows: entity icon, name/number, key detail (e.g., company for contact, amount for quote), and entity type badge
Clicking a result navigates to the detail page for that entity
Recent searches stored in localStorage (last 10)
Empty state shows quick-access shortcuts: 'New Lead', 'New Quote', 'New Customer'
Search works on mobile with full-width overlay
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Backend endpoint GET /api/universal-search already exists. Frontend has no global search UI - users must navigate to specific modules to search. A command palette (Cmd+K) pattern is standard in modern SaaS apps. Use shadcn/ui Dialog + Command components.

userStories.title: Add breadcrumb navigation to all detail and nested pages
userStories.description: As a user navigating deep into the app, I need breadcrumbs showing my current location so I can understand context and navigate back without using the browser back button.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a reusable Breadcrumb component in client/src/components/ui/breadcrumb.tsx
Breadcrumb renders: Home > Section > Subsection > Current Page with clickable links except the last item
Add breadcrumbs to all detail pages: LeadDetail, CustomerDetail, QuoteView, OrderDetail, InvoiceDetail, EquipmentDetail, ContractDetail
Add breadcrumbs to all nested pages that are 2+ levels deep from the sidebar
Breadcrumb data derived from route path and page title (not hardcoded per page)
Create a useBreadcrumbs() hook that auto-generates breadcrumbs from the current Wouter route
Mobile: breadcrumbs truncate with ellipsis for middle items, always showing first and last
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Detail pages like LeadDetail, CustomerDetail, QuoteView are dead-ends - no visible back navigation. Users who land on a detail page via URL have no context of where they are in the app hierarchy. Breadcrumbs are the standard solution.

userStories.title: Redesign dashboard landing page with role-appropriate widgets and quick actions
userStories.description: As a user logging in, I need my dashboard to immediately show me the most important information for my role with actionable widgets so I can start working without navigating elsewhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard renders different widget sets based on user role level
Sales reps (levels 1-3): My Open Leads count, My Pipeline Value, Quotes Expiring This Week, Tasks Due Today, Recent Activity feed
Managers (levels 4-6): Team Pipeline Summary, Revenue This Month vs Target, Top Deals to Close, Team Activity, Overdue Tasks
Executives (levels 7-8): Company Revenue Dashboard, Pipeline Health, Win/Loss Ratio, Customer Acquisition, MRR/ARR metrics
Each widget is clickable and navigates to the relevant full page
Quick action buttons at top: 'New Lead', 'New Quote', 'Log Activity' (role-appropriate)
Recent items section showing last 5 records the user viewed/edited
Dashboard loads in under 2 seconds with skeleton placeholders during data fetch
Widgets use TanStack Query with stale-while-revalidate for fast subsequent loads
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Current dashboard exists but doesn't provide role-appropriate guidance. A good landing page reduces time-to-first-action. Dashboard widget customization (US-059) exists as a story but this focuses on sensible defaults per role. Leverage existing KPI endpoints and analytics services.

userStories.title: Standardize form patterns with consistent validation, errors, and submit states
userStories.description: As a user filling out forms, I need consistent behavior across all create/edit dialogs so I can predict how forms work regardless of which entity I'm creating.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a StandardFormDialog component wrapping shadcn Dialog + React Hook Form + Zod validation
All form dialogs show: title, scrollable form body, Cancel + Submit buttons in footer
Submit button shows loading spinner and disables during submission
Field-level validation errors appear below the field in red text immediately on blur
Form-level errors (API errors) appear as a banner at the top of the form
Required fields marked with red asterisk
Tab order follows visual layout (top-to-bottom, left-to-right)
Escape key closes dialog with unsaved changes confirmation if form is dirty
Apply StandardFormDialog pattern to at least: Create Lead, Create Quote, Create Customer, Create Invoice, Create Contact
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently forms vary widely: some use Dialog, some inline, validation display is inconsistent, submit button states differ. React Hook Form + Zod are already used but the outer chrome (dialog, error display, button states) needs standardization. This is about UX consistency, not rewriting form logic.

userStories.title: Add consistent empty states, loading skeletons, and error states to all list pages
userStories.description: As a user, I need clear visual feedback when pages are loading, when there's no data, and when something goes wrong so I always know the system's status.
acceptanceCriteria: Create reusable EmptyState component with: icon, title, description, and optional CTA button
Create reusable ErrorState component with: error icon, message, retry button, and support link
All list pages (leads, customers, quotes, invoices, orders, contacts, equipment) use TableSkeleton during initial load
Empty state shows entity-specific messaging: 'No leads yet. Create your first lead to get started.' with 'Create Lead' button
Error state shows: 'Failed to load leads. Please try again.' with Retry button that re-fetches
Distinguish between empty search results ('No leads match your filters') and empty table ('No leads yet')
Loading skeletons match the approximate shape of the real content (table rows, card grids)
Apply to at least 10 major list pages across Sales, Service, Billing, and Equipment hubs
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: US-025 covers standardizing loading/empty states but focuses on top pages. This extends coverage comprehensively. Some pages show blank white space during loading or when empty. TableSkeleton component exists but isn't used everywhere. Error states are especially important for mobile users on flaky connections.

userStories.title: Unify snake_case to camelCase data transformation with centralized entity mappers
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single transformation layer between API responses (snake_case) and frontend state (camelCase) so every page doesn't duplicate 50+ lines of field mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: Create client/src/lib/entity-mappers.ts with typed mapper functions for each entity: mapLead, mapCustomer, mapQuote, mapInvoice, mapOrder, mapContact, mapEquipment
Each mapper converts snake_case API fields to camelCase TypeScript interfaces with correct types
Each mapper provides sensible defaults for nullable fields (empty string for text, 0 for numbers, null for optional relations)
Create a generic mapResponse<T>(response, mapper) utility that handles both single and array responses
Integrate mappers into apiRequest or create entity-specific query hooks that auto-transform
Refactor at least 8 major pages (Leads, Customers, Quotes, Invoices, Orders, Contacts, Contracts, Equipment) to use centralized mappers
Remove duplicate inline transformation code from refactored pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Every page currently does manual field mapping like: invoiceNumber: item.invoiceNumber || item.invoice_number || ''. This creates 50+ lines of duplicate transformation per page, is error-prone, and makes it hard to add new fields. A centralized mapper eliminates this entirely.

userStories.title: Implement optimistic mutations for inline edits and status changes
userStories.description: As a user editing records, I need the UI to update immediately when I make changes rather than waiting for the server round-trip so the app feels fast and responsive.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a useOptimisticMutation hook that wraps TanStack Query's useMutation with optimistic cache updates
On mutation: immediately update the query cache with the expected new value
On success: merge the server response into the cache (server is source of truth for computed fields)
On error: roll back the optimistic update, show error toast, restore previous state
Apply to inline cell edits in table views (status changes, field updates)
Apply to drag-and-drop stage changes on pipeline boards
Apply to toggle operations (active/inactive, pin/unpin, archive/unarchive)
Show a subtle 'Saving...' indicator near the edited field during the API call
Batch rapid edits: if user edits multiple fields within 500ms, debounce into a single PATCH request
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently pages use queryClient.invalidateQueries() which does a full refetch after every mutation. This causes visible loading flicker and feels slow, especially on mobile. useOptimisticMutations hook already exists in the codebase but isn't widely adopted. This story expands adoption.

userStories.title: Add contextual help tooltips and onboarding hints for key workflows
userStories.description: As a new user, I need contextual help throughout the app explaining what features do and how to use them so I can be productive without external training.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a HelpTooltip component that shows an info icon with hover/click tooltip explaining the feature
Add HelpTooltips to: pipeline stages (what each stage means), quote statuses, invoice generation, lead scoring, RBAC roles, report builder
Create a first-time-user checklist that appears on the dashboard: 'Getting Started' card with steps like 'Create your first lead', 'Set up your pipeline', 'Invite a team member'
Checklist progress persists in user preferences (mark steps complete)
Add 'What's this?' links on complex pages (Reports Builder, Pipeline Configuration, RBAC Settings) linking to relevant knowledge base articles
Tooltips are dismissible and users can toggle 'Show help tips' in user preferences
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: US-055 covers guided onboarding wizard for new tenants. This story focuses on persistent contextual help throughout the app, not just initial setup. Knowledge base system exists (npm run kb commands). Help tooltips reduce support burden and improve feature discovery.

userStories.title: Enhance Quotes page with expiration warnings, version history, and send workflow
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need to see which quotes are about to expire, view previous versions of a quote, and send quotes directly to customers via email so I can manage the proposal process end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Expiring Soon' badge (orange) on quotes where validUntil is within 7 days
Add 'Expired' badge (red) on quotes past validUntil date
Add a sortable 'Days Until Expiry' column to the quotes table
Create a quote version history panel: show previous versions with date, author, and change summary
Store quote versions in a quote_versions table: id, quoteId, versionNumber, snapshotData (jsonb), createdBy, createdAt, changeNotes
Auto-create a version snapshot when a quote is updated (on PUT /api/proposals/:id)
Add 'Send Quote' button that opens a dialog with: recipient email (pre-filled from contact), subject line, message body, PDF attachment toggle
Sending a quote changes status from 'draft' to 'sent' and logs an activity
Email uses existing email-service.ts with a professional quote email template
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Quotes page has status workflow but no expiration warnings (validUntil field exists but isn't visually flagged). No versioning visible - important for audit trails and negotiations. No send workflow - status changes to 'sent' manually but no email is triggered. These are core sales workflow gaps.

userStories.title: Enhance Invoices page with aging analysis, payment reminders, and AR dashboard
userStories.description: As a billing manager, I need to see invoice aging buckets (current, 30/60/90+ days), send automated payment reminders, and view accounts receivable metrics so I can manage cash flow effectively.
acceptanceCriteria: Add aging summary cards at top of invoices page: Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 90+ Days with total amounts
Color-code overdue invoices in the table: yellow (1-30 days), orange (31-60), red (61+)
Add 'Send Reminder' button on overdue invoices that sends a payment reminder email with invoice details and payment link
Create GET /api/invoices/aging-summary endpoint returning bucket totals filtered by tenantId
Add AR metrics dashboard section: total outstanding, average days to payment, collection rate this month
Add date preset filters: 'Overdue', 'Due This Week', 'Due This Month' as quick filter chips
Generate dialog adds presets: 'Current Month', 'Previous Month', 'Current Quarter' for date range
Payment recording shows remaining balance and supports partial payments with running balance
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Invoice page has generation and payment recording but lacks aging analysis - a critical billing function. No automated reminders. Generate dialog requires manual date range with no presets. Partial payment tracking unclear. These are core billing workflow gaps for any print shop.

userStories.title: Enhance Leads page with lead scoring display, territory visualization, and activity timeline
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need to see lead scores, territory assignments, and recent interaction history directly on the leads list so I can prioritize outreach and manage my team's pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Lead Score' column to leads table showing numerical score with color indicator (green: hot, yellow: warm, red: cold)
Lead score calculated from: recency of last activity, number of interactions, deal value, engagement metrics
Create GET /api/leads/:id/score endpoint or compute client-side from existing lead data
Add territory assignment badge on each lead showing the assigned territory name
Add 'Assigned Rep' column showing the sales rep avatar + name with click to reassign (for managers)
Quick-view panel: clicking a lead row expands an inline detail panel showing last 5 activities without leaving the list
Add 'Last Contacted' column with relative time ('3 days ago', 'Never')
Add quick filter: 'Uncontacted Leads' (no activities), 'Hot Leads' (score > threshold)

Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Schema has ownerId, assignedSalesRep, territory fields on businessRecords. leadAssignmentHistory, salesTerritories, repCapacity tables exist in lead-assignment-schema.ts. Lead scoring service may exist but isn't surfaced in the UI. Activity data available via deals activities API.

userStories.title: Enhance Customers page with health score, contract summary, and hierarchy view
userStories.description: As an account manager, I need to see customer health scores, active contract summaries, and parent-child company relationships so I can manage accounts proactively.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'Health Score' column: computed from recent activity, open support tickets, contract renewal proximity, payment history
Health score shown as colored dot: green (healthy), yellow (at risk), red (churning)
Add 'Active Contracts' count column linking to the customer's contracts list
Add 'Annual Contract Value' (ACV) column summing active contract values
Add 'Contract Renewal' column showing nearest renewal date with warning for renewals within 30 days
Add company hierarchy view toggle: tree visualization showing parent company → child locations/divisions
Customer detail page shows: contract timeline, equipment deployed, open quotes, recent invoices in organized tabs
Add 'At Risk' quick filter showing customers with declining health scores or upcoming renewals
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Customer page has 6 filter dimensions but lacks business intelligence. No health scoring, no contract context, no hierarchy view. For a print shop management platform, seeing equipment deployed and contract status per customer is essential for account management.

userStories.title: Enhance Orders page with fulfillment tracking, status timeline, and delivery management
userStories.description: As an operations manager, I need to track order fulfillment stages, see status change history, and manage delivery scheduling so orders move smoothly from confirmed to delivered.
acceptanceCriteria: Add visual fulfillment pipeline at top of orders page: Confirmed → In Production → Quality Check → Ready to Ship → Shipped → Delivered with counts per stage
Clicking a pipeline stage filters the table to that stage
Add status timeline on order detail: vertical timeline showing every status change with timestamp, user, and notes
Add 'Estimated Delivery' column with color coding: on time (green), at risk (yellow), late (red)
Add delivery scheduling: assign delivery date, driver/courier, and tracking number
Add 'Flag for Review' action that marks an order for manager attention with a reason
Bulk action: 'Mark as Shipped' for selected orders with tracking number input
Add notification to customer when order status changes to 'Shipped' or 'Delivered'
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Orders are a core workflow for a print shop. The page likely exists but needs fulfillment-specific UX. Print shops need to track production stages, delivery logistics, and customer communication. This turns the orders page from a simple list into a fulfillment management tool.

userStories.title: Enhance Service/Dispatch page with technician availability, map view, and SLA tracking
userStories.description: As a service dispatcher, I need to see technician availability, view service calls on a map, and track SLA compliance so I can efficiently schedule and monitor field service work.
acceptanceCriteria: Add technician availability panel: list of technicians with today's schedule, current status (available, en route, on site, off duty)
Add map view toggle showing service call locations as pins with status colors (open: blue, in progress: yellow, overdue: red)
Map uses existing Leaflet integration with cluster markers for dense areas
Add SLA timer on each service ticket: shows time remaining before SLA breach with visual countdown
SLA breached tickets highlighted in red with 'SLA Breached' badge
Drag-and-drop assignment: drag a service call to a technician's schedule slot to assign
Add 'Optimize Route' button that suggests efficient ordering of a technician's daily calls
Service metrics cards at top: Open Tickets, Average Response Time, SLA Compliance %, Technicians Active
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Service Hub has Dispatch, Technicians, Meter Readings pages. Leaflet is installed (with --legacy-peer-deps). For a print/copier shop, service dispatch is a core revenue function. Technicians service equipment on-site and SLA tracking is contractually important.

userStories.title: Add real-time collaboration indicators and conflict prevention
userStories.description: As a team member, I need to see when others are viewing or editing the same record so we don't overwrite each other's changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Show presence indicators on record detail pages: avatars of other users currently viewing the same record

userStories.title: Add unified activity timeline component for all entity detail pages
userStories.description: As a user viewing any record, I need a chronological activity timeline showing all interactions, changes, and related events so I have full context without clicking through multiple tabs.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a reusable ActivityTimeline component in client/src/components/ui/activity-timeline.tsx
Timeline shows: notes, emails, calls, status changes, field changes, related record events (quote created for lead, invoice generated for order)
Each entry shows: icon by type, user avatar, description, relative timestamp, and expandable detail
Filter tabs at top of timeline: All, Notes, Emails, Calls, Changes, System
'Add Note' quick action at top of timeline with rich text input
Field change entries show: 'Status changed from Draft to Sent by Jane 2 hours ago' with old → new values
Timeline supports infinite scroll with 'Load older' trigger
Integrate into LeadDetail, CustomerDetail, QuoteView, OrderDetail, InvoiceDetail, ContractDetail, EquipmentDetail pages
Create GET /api/:entityType/:id/timeline endpoint aggregating activities from multiple sources
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: CRM-008 covers activity timeline for the CRM layout engine, but this is a standalone reusable component that can be adopted incrementally across all detail pages, not just CRM objects. Activity data exists via /api/deals-management/deals/:id/activities and similar endpoints. This is one of the most impactful UX improvements for daily users.

userStories.title: Enforce role-based route protection for all unguarded CRM, admin, and finance pages
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I need every page in the application to enforce minimum role permissions so that sales reps cannot access admin functions, company admins cannot reach root/platform admin pages, and finance pages are restricted to finance roles, preventing unauthorized access through direct URL navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all routes in client/src/App.tsx and identify every Route that renders a component directly without ProtectedRoute wrapping

Apply ProtectedRoute to all CRM routes (/crm/deals, /crm/leads, /crm/contacts, /crm/companies, /leads, /customers, /deals, /opportunities) with permissions: ['sales.lead.view_own', 'sales.lead.view_team', 'sales.customer.view_own']
Apply ProtectedRoute to sales management routes (/quotes, /quotes/new, /quotes/:id, /proposal-builder, /quote-proposal-generation) with permissions: ['sales.quote.view_own', 'sales.quote.view_team']
Apply ProtectedRoute to finance routes (/advanced-billing, /commission-management) with permissions: ['finance.billing.view', 'finance.reports.view'] and minLevel: 3
Apply ProtectedRoute to operations routes (/purchase-orders, /warehouse-operations, /equipment-lifecycle, /product-hub) with permissions: ['operations.inventory.view', 'service.equipment.view']
Apply ProtectedRoute to analytics/reporting routes (/sales-performance-analytics, /sales-command-center, /service-analytics) with permissions: ['reporting.sales.view'] and minLevel: 3
Routes using AdminRouteGuard (minLevel 7) must remain on: /admin-command-center, /root-admin-signups-crm, /root-admin/seo and all /admin/* paths
Routes using platformOnly must remain on: /admin-hub, /root-admin-dashboard, /admin/tenant-management, /admin/platform-analytics, /admin/database-management, /admin/mobile-logs, /admin/audit-logs
All routes that previously had no guard must now show the AccessDenied component for users without the required permissions — NOT a blank page or 404
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: CRITICAL security story. Current App.tsx audit shows most routes at /crm/*, /quotes/*, /customers, /leads, /purchase-orders, /warehouse-operations, /commission-management, and /sales-command-center render components directly with no ProtectedRoute wrapper. A sales rep can navigate directly to /advanced-billing or /commission-management via URL. The RouteGuard and ProtectedRoute components already exist in client/src/components/auth/ — this story is purely applying them consistently. Reference: client/src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx and client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts for the permission map.

userStories.title: Build role-aware sidebar navigation that hides sections users cannot access
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I should only see navigation items I have permission to use so the interface is not cluttered with links to pages I cannot access, and admin users should see their additional sections without sales users being aware those sections exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Read client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts — every SECTION_PERMISSIONS and ITEM_PERMISSIONS entry must be enforced in the sidebar render logic
Modify the sidebar component (client/src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx or equivalent) to call usePermissions() and filter sections before rendering
Platform-only sections (platform-admin-hub, tenant-org-management, user-access-management, system-operations, platform-features) must be completely invisible (not just disabled) to non-platform users
Sections with requiredPermissions (service, products, reporting, finance) are hidden if the user has none of the listed permissions
Sections with minLevel are hidden if the user's role level is below the minimum
alwaysVisible sections (dashboard, tasks, ai-hub, knowledge-base, settings, crm) remain visible to all authenticated users
When a section is hidden, its children items are also hidden — no orphaned links
Add a hook useVisibleNavItems() in client/src/hooks/ that returns the filtered navigation tree using navigation-permissions.ts rules
Navigation rendering must not show loading flicker — permissions should be read synchronously from the usePermissions() hook cache
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: navigation-permissions.ts already maps all sections and items to permissions. The sidebar currently renders all items regardless of role. This story wires the existing permission map to the sidebar render. usePermissions() hook exists at client/src/hooks/usePermissions.ts and returns isPlatformUser, level, hasAnyPermission, hasAllPermissions synchronously from cached data. The sidebar component is at client/src/components/layout/ — identify the correct file and apply the filter there.

userStories.title: Implement role-scoped API data filtering so reps only see their own records
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need records to be automatically scoped to what each user is authorized to see at the API level — reps see only their own leads and quotes, managers see their team's, directors see their region's — so data isolation is enforced on the server, not just the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Review server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts — ensure buildScopedQuery() is applied to all GET list endpoints for: /api/leads, /api/customers, /api/proposals, /api/deals-management/deals, /api/contacts

Scope tiers must map to role levels: roleLevel 1-2 (own records: userId match), roleLevel 3-4 (team records: teamId match), roleLevel 5-6 (regional records: regionId match), roleLevel 7+ (company-wide: tenantId only)
Platform admins (roleLevel 8, isPlatformAdmin=true) bypass all scoping and see all tenants
Each scoped endpoint must read the user's roleLevel, teamId, regionId from the JWT/session via getUserId() and getTenantId() helpers
Create a server/middleware/scope-middleware.ts helper: applyScopeFilter(req, baseQuery, table) that injects the correct WHERE clause based on role
Scoped endpoints return only records the user is authorized to see — a rep calling GET /api/leads must not receive another rep's leads
Add integration test in server/tests/integration/ verifying scope isolation: rep A cannot see rep B's leads, manager sees both, director sees all in region
Existing admin-level endpoints that intentionally return all records (platform admin routes) must document this explicitly with a comment
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: hierarchical-query-builder.ts exists at server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts but is not applied consistently across all list endpoints. Currently most endpoints only filter by tenantId which means any authenticated user in the tenant sees all records. This is correct for admins but wrong for reps. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts provides EnhancedUserContext with roleLevel, teamId, regionId, territoryScope — use these for scoping. This is a data security story, not just UI.

userStories.title: Add role-specific dashboard views that surface relevant KPIs and actions per role
userStories.description: As a sales rep, when I log in I should see a dashboard focused on my leads, my quotes, and my tasks — not company-wide revenue charts. As a manager, I should see my team's pipeline. As an executive, I see company-wide KPIs. The dashboard should present the right information for each role automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify the main Dashboard page (client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx or equivalent) to detect the user's roleLevel from usePermissions() and render the appropriate view
roleLevel 1-2 (Individual Contributor / Team Lead): Show 'My Pipeline' widgets — My Open Leads count, My Active Quotes with total value, My Upcoming Tasks (next 7 days), My Recent Activity feed
roleLevel 3-4 (Supervisor / Manager): Show team widgets — Team Pipeline Summary by stage, Team Quota Attainment %, Top Performing Reps (ranked by deals closed this month), Team Activity Feed
roleLevel 5-6 (Regional / Company Director): Show regional widgets — Regional Revenue vs Target, Pipeline by Stage (all teams in region), Deals at Risk (no activity > 14 days), Conversion Rate trend
roleLevel 7-8 (Executive / Platform Admin): Show company-wide KPIs — Total Revenue MTD/YTD, MRR, NRR, Customer Count, ARR Forecast, Churn Rate
Each dashboard tier must use the existing KpiSummaryBar component with role-appropriate metrics
Quick action buttons on each tier: Rep → 'New Lead', 'New Quote'; Manager → 'Review Pipeline', 'Team Assignments'; Director → 'Reports', 'Forecast'; Admin → 'Admin Hub', 'System Settings'
Dashboard does not redirect or change URL — same route / but renders different components based on role
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently the Dashboard at / renders a single view for all roles. KpiSummaryBar component exists at client/src/components/dashboard/KpiSummaryBar.tsx and accepts configurable metrics. This is a high-impact UX improvement — reps currently see company-wide charts that aren't actionable for them. usePermissions() returns level and role tier. The API scoping from RBAC-003 means the data returned is already role-scoped, so the dashboard widgets can use the same endpoints and get role-appropriate data.

userStories.title: Implement contextual 'Quick Actions' button strip on all entity detail pages
userStories.description: As a sales rep, when I'm on a customer, lead, or deal detail page I should see a clearly visible strip of the most common actions for that record's current state — not buried in dropdown menus — so I can act immediately without hunting through nested menus.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a reusable QuickActionsBar component in client/src/components/ui/quick-actions-bar.tsx that accepts: entityType, entityId, currentStatus, and an actions array
Actions are state-aware: the available actions change based on the record's current status field

Lead quick actions by status: New → ['Qualify', 'Schedule Call', 'Create Quote', 'Disqualify']; Contacted → ['Log Call', 'Create Quote', 'Schedule Follow-up']; Qualified → ['Create Quote', 'Convert to Customer']; Won → ['Create Quote', 'View Customer']; Lost → ['Reopen', 'Archive']
Customer quick actions: ['New Quote', 'Log Activity', 'Schedule Service', 'Create Invoice', 'Add Contact']
Deal quick actions by stage: Early stages → ['Update Stage', 'Create Quote']; Late stages → ['Generate Contract', 'Mark Won', 'Mark Lost']
Each action button shows an icon + label, uses appropriate variant (primary for main CTA, outline for secondary)
Actions that navigate away use wouter's useLocation to navigate with pre-populated query params (e.g., 'New Quote' navigates to /quotes/new?businessRecordId=xxx&companyName=xxx&contactId=xxx)
Actions that open dialogs (Log Activity, Schedule Follow-up) use sheet/dialog from shadcn/ui — no full page navigation required
Integrate QuickActionsBar into CustomerDetail.tsx at the top of the page, below the header
Integrate QuickActionsBar into the lead and deal detail pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently all actions on detail pages are in dropdown kebab menus or tab-buried buttons. HubSpot puts primary actions (Email, Call, Create Note, Schedule Meeting) directly in the header. This story solves the 'buried actions' problem. The navigation with query params is the precursor to QP-001 (auto-populating quotes from customer context). Each action button should respect RBAC — if the user lacks sales.quote.create_own permission, hide the 'New Quote' button rather than show an error after clicking.

userStories.title: Build a streamlined inline edit mode for record detail fields to reduce edit-page navigation
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I should be able to click any field on a customer or lead detail page to edit it inline and save without navigating to a separate edit form, matching how modern CRMs allow fast field updates during a call or meeting.
acceptanceCriteria: Create an InlineEditField component in client/src/components/ui/inline-edit-field.tsx supporting field types: text, textarea, select, date, phone, email, currency, number
Clicking a field value on a detail page replaces it with an input in edit mode; pressing Enter or clicking outside saves; pressing Escape cancels
On save, fire a PATCH /api/:entityType/:id request with only the changed field (partial update)
Show a brief success indicator (checkmark for 1.5s) on save; show an error toast if the request fails, and revert the field to its previous value
Apply InlineEditField to CustomerDetail.tsx for fields: companyName, phone, email, website, address, industry, accountStatus, assignedUserId
Apply InlineEditField to lead detail pages for fields: firstName, lastName, email, phone, company, status, source, assignedUserId
Respect RBAC: if the user lacks the write permission for the entity (e.g., sales.customer.edit_own), fields render as read-only text — no click-to-edit affordance shown
assignedUserId field uses a searchable user select dropdown populated from GET /api/users?tenantId=xxx
Changes made via inline edit must invalidate the relevant TanStack Query cache key so other components on the page reflect the update
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently CustomerDetail.tsx and lead detail pages require navigating to a separate edit form or opening a modal to change any field. This is a 3-click workflow that inline editing reduces to 1 click. PATCH endpoints already exist for customers and leads (server/routes-*.ts). The InlineEditField component pattern is common in CRMs — refer to HubSpot's click-to-edit behavior. TanStack Query invalidation: use queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['/api/customers', id] }) after a successful PATCH.

userStories.title: Add global keyboard shortcuts and command palette for power-user navigation
userStories.description: As a power user, I need keyboard shortcuts and a command palette (Cmd+K) to quickly navigate to any page, create a new record, or perform common actions without using the mouse, so I can work faster during high-volume sales periods.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement a CommandPalette component in client/src/components/ui/command-palette.tsx using shadcn/ui Command (cmdk) component
Open with Cmd+K (Mac) / Ctrl+K (Windows/Linux) from anywhere in the app; close with Escape

Command palette sections: Navigate (links to all main pages), Create New (New Lead, New Quote, New Customer, New Contact, New Deal), Recent (last 5 visited records from localStorage), Actions (current page actions if applicable)
Navigation commands: 'Go to Dashboard', 'Go to Leads', 'Go to Quotes', 'Go to Customers', 'Go to Deals', 'Go to Reports', etc.
Fuzzy search filters all commands in real time as the user types
Create New commands navigate to the appropriate creation page or open a quick-create sheet
Keyboard shortcuts outside the palette: N+L = New Lead, N+Q = New Quote, N+C = New Customer (sequential key combos, not simultaneous)
Add a small keyboard shortcut hint badge in the sidebar nav items and action buttons where shortcuts exist
Command palette respects RBAC — only shows commands for pages/actions the user has permission to access (use usePermissions() to filter)
Register the command palette at the App root level (App.tsx) so it works on all pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: cmdk is already available via shadcn/ui Command component. This is a high-delight feature for sales reps who work at volume. The command palette should be lazy-loaded and not impact initial page load. Sequential key combos (N then L) are simpler to implement than chords and avoid conflicts with browser shortcuts. The RBAC filter is important — showing 'Go to Admin Hub' to a rep who cannot access it creates confusion.

userStories.title: Enable quote creation pre-seeded with customer and contact data from the record context
userStories.description: As a sales rep, when I click 'New Quote' from a customer or lead detail page, the quote builder should automatically fill in the company name, primary contact, billing address, and any existing equipment so I don't have to re-enter information I'm already looking at.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify the 'New Quote' navigation action on CustomerDetail.tsx to navigate to /quotes/new?businessRecordId={id}&companyName={encodeURIComponent(name)}&contactId={primaryContactId}&contactName={encodeURIComponent(contactName)}
Modify QuoteBuilderPage.tsx to read URL search params (businessRecordId, companyName, contactId, contactName) on mount using useSearch() from wouter
If businessRecordId param is present, pre-populate the quote's customer/company fields and skip the customer search step in the quote wizard
If contactId param is present, pre-populate the primary contact field on the quote

If businessRecordId is present, automatically fetch GET /api/customers/{businessRecordId}/equipment to pre-populate an 'Existing Equipment' section in the quote as reference line items (not billed — informational context)
After auto-population, the sales rep lands directly on the product/line items step of the quote builder, not the customer selection step
Show a contextual banner in the quote builder: 'Creating quote for [Company Name] — customer details pre-filled. Edit if needed.'
The 'New Quote' button on CustomerDetail.tsx must only be visible to users with sales.quote.create_own or sales.quote.create_team permission
The same pre-seeding must work from the lead detail page: navigate with businessRecordId of the lead record
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently /quotes/new opens a blank QuoteBuilderPage. The customer, contact, and company fields must be filled manually even when navigating from a customer record. URL search params are the correct mechanism — no new API needed. QuoteBuilderPage uses wouter for routing; useSearch() returns the query string. businessRecordId is already a field on the quotes/proposals schema (business_record_id in shared/schema.ts). The UX-001 story's QuickActionsBar 'New Quote' action should use these same params. This eliminates 4-6 manual form fields in the quote creation flow.

userStories.title: Build a multi-step quote wizard with progress indicator to reduce quote creation errors
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the quote creation flow to guide me through clearly labeled steps (Customer, Products, Pricing, Review & Send) with a visible progress indicator so I know what's required at each step and don't accidentally skip required fields before sending.
acceptanceCriteria: Refactor QuoteBuilderPage.tsx into a multi-step wizard with 4 steps: Step 1 'Customer & Contact' (skip if pre-seeded from QP-001), Step 2 'Products & Line Items', Step 3 'Pricing & Terms', Step 4 'Review & Send'
Add a horizontal step progress indicator at the top of the wizard showing all 4 steps with the current step highlighted and completed steps marked with a checkmark
Step 1 (Customer & Contact): company name (required), primary contact (required), billing address, quote expiry date (default: 30 days from today)
Step 2 (Products & Line Items): product catalog search, quantity, unit price, line item notes, subtotal running total visible in sidebar
Step 3 (Pricing & Terms): discount (%, flat, or tiered), tax rate, payment terms (Net 15/30/45/60, Due on Receipt), internal notes, customer-facing notes

Step 4 (Review & Send): full read-only preview of the quote as it will appear to the customer, with a 'Edit' button per section to jump back, and primary CTA buttons: 'Save as Draft', 'Send to Customer', 'Download PDF'
Each step validates required fields before allowing 'Next' — show inline validation errors, not a global alert
Step navigation: 'Back' and 'Next' buttons on each step, plus clicking a completed step in the progress bar jumps to it
Wizard state is preserved in component state (not URL) — navigating Back does not lose entered data
If pre-seeded from QP-001, Step 1 is auto-completed and the wizard opens on Step 2 with a 'Customer pre-filled' notice in the step indicator
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Current QuoteBuilderPage is a single-form page. Converting to a wizard reduces cognitive load and prevents incomplete quotes from being sent. The product catalog search for Step 2 uses GET /api/products/search?q=. Pricing logic from Step 3 mirrors existing quote schema fields: discount, taxRate, paymentTerms, notes. The Review step in Step 4 can reuse the existing QuoteView component in read-only mode. Pre-seeding from QP-001 means Step 1 is skipped — implement by tracking a completedSteps Set and marking step 1 complete if businessRecordId param was present.

userStories.title: Add quote templates with one-click application and product bundle presets
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need to start new quotes from pre-built templates (e.g., 'Standard Copier Lease', 'MPS Agreement', 'Equipment + Service Bundle') that pre-fill the line items, pricing structure, and terms so I can generate a complete quote in under 2 minutes for common deal types.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a quote_templates table in shared/schema.ts: id, tenantId, name, description, category (lease/service/equipment/bundle), lineItems (jsonb array), defaultTerms (text), defaultPaymentTerms, defaultExpiryDays, isActive, createdBy, createdAt
Create GET /api/quote-templates endpoint returning active templates for the tenant, grouped by category
Create POST /api/quote-templates endpoint for admins/managers to create new templates (minLevel: 4 required)
Create PUT /api/quote-templates/:id and DELETE /api/quote-templates/:id for template management
On the QuoteBuilderPage Step 2 (Products), add a 'Start from Template' button that opens a template picker sheet
Template picker shows templates grouped by category with name, description, line item count, and an estimated total based on standard pricing
Applying a template appends all template line items to the current quote (does not replace existing items) and applies the template's default terms
Seed 5 starter templates for the Printyx copier dealer context: 'Standard Copier Lease', 'Color MFP Purchase', 'MPS Service Agreement', 'Equipment + 1yr Service Bundle', 'Trade-in + New Device'
Template management UI at /admin/quote-templates accessible to users with minLevel: 4
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: QuoteTemplates component already exists at client/src/components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx but appears to be a display component only. This story adds the database backend and the apply-to-active-quote flow. The lineItems jsonb stores [{productId, description, quantity, unitPrice, notes}] matching the existing quote line item schema. Templates reduce the average quote creation time from 8-12 minutes to under 2 minutes for repeat deal types. Admin management route should use ProtectedRoute with minLevel: 4 consistent with RBAC-001.

userStories.title: Redesign 404 page with brand presence, helpful navigation, and search
userStories.description: As a user who lands on a non-existent page, I need a helpful 404 page with branding, suggested links, and search so I can find what I'm looking for instead of bouncing.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the developer-facing message ('Did you forget to add the page to the router?') with a user-friendly message
Add Printyx branding (logo or brand name) to the 404 page
Add a prominent 'Go to Dashboard' or 'Go Home' CTA button
Add 3-5 quick navigation links to common pages: Dashboard, Leads, Customers, Quotes, Support
Add a search input or link to trigger the command palette (Cmd+K) for finding content
Include visual illustration or icon that communicates 'page not found' clearly
Page is fully responsive on mobile with touch-friendly targets (48px min)
Proper semantic HTML with h1 heading and descriptive alt text for any images
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Current 404 page (client/src/pages/not-found.tsx) is only 21 lines with a developer-facing message. This is the #1 bounce-rate reducer.

userStories.title: Enhance footer with legal links, company info, navigation, and SEO-friendly structure
userStories.description: As a user and for SEO, I need a comprehensive footer with legal links (Privacy, Terms), company info, navigation shortcuts, and social links so the site feels professional and search engines can discover all key pages.

Add social media links placeholder (LinkedIn, Twitter/X) with proper rel='noopener noreferrer' and target='_blank'
Footer is responsive: 4-column grid on desktop, 2-column on tablet, stacked on mobile
Include system status indicator (existing online/offline functionality)
Use semantic HTML with nav element and aria-label for footer navigation
Footer links use proper anchor tags for SEO crawlability
Typecheck passes: npm run check

userStories.notes: Current footer (client/src/components/layout/footer.tsx) is only 23 lines with just copyright and a hardcoded version. Missing all standard SaaS footer content: legal links, company info, navigation. This is a significant SEO gap (missed internal linking opportunity) and reduces user trust. FooterSitemapLinks component exists in client/src/lib/seo/InternalLinking.tsx but isn't used in the actual footer.

userStories.title: Add KPI summary cards to Invoices page for revenue visibility
userStories.description: As a billing manager, I need summary KPI cards at the top of the Invoices page showing total outstanding, overdue count, payment rate, and total revenue so I can assess billing health at a glance without scrolling through individual invoices.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 4 KPI summary cards at the top of the Invoices page: Total Outstanding (sum of unpaid invoices), Overdue Count (invoices past due date), Paid This Month (sum of recently paid), Total Invoices (count of all invoices)
Each card displays a relevant icon, metric value formatted as currency where applicable, and a label
Cards use color coding: green for positive metrics (paid), red/amber for attention metrics (overdue), blue for neutral (total)
Cards use skeleton loading state while data is being fetched
Cards are responsive: 4-column grid on desktop, 2-column on tablet/mobile
KPI values are computed from the existing invoices query data (no new API endpoint needed)
