userStories.notes: The Invoices page (client/src/pages/Invoices.tsx) is the only major list page missing KPI summary cards. LeadsPage has them (Total, New, Contacted, Qualified), CustomersPage has them (Active, On Hold, Retention %), QuotesManagement has a KPI bar. This inconsistency makes the Invoices page feel less polished and forces billing managers to mentally aggregate data from the card list view.

userStories.title: Implement server-side robots.txt and sitemap.xml generation endpoints
userStories.description: As a search engine crawler, I need a robots.txt file directing crawl behavior and a sitemap.xml listing all indexable pages so the site is properly discoverable and indexed.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GET /robots.txt endpoint in server returning proper crawl directives
Robots.txt allows crawling of marketing/blog/knowledge-base pages
Robots.txt disallows /admin, /dashboard, /settings, /api/ paths
Robots.txt includes Sitemap: directive pointing to /sitemap.xml
Add GET /sitemap.xml endpoint generating XML sitemap from SEO config
Sitemap includes all public routes from seoConfig with lastmod, changefreq, and priority
Sitemap excludes noindex routes and authenticated app pages
Both endpoints are excluded from auth middleware
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: The SEO infrastructure (client/src/lib/seo/seoConfig.ts) already has getAllSEOConfigs() with priority and changefreq fields for every route. The server just needs endpoints to serve robots.txt and generate sitemap XML from this config. Currently no robots.txt or sitemap.xml exists, meaning search engines have no crawl guidance and may miss important pages or waste crawl budget on authenticated routes.

userStories.title: Standardize dialog widths for mobile with max-w-[95vw] pattern
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I need all create/edit dialogs to fit within my screen width without horizontal overflow so I can complete forms without frustration.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all Dialog/DialogContent usages across client/src/pages/ for max-width classes
Update all dialogs to use max-w-[95vw] as a base constraint with sm: breakpoint for desktop width
Pattern: DialogContent className='max-w-[95vw] sm:max-w-lg' (or sm:max-w-2xl for wider dialogs)
Verify at least 15 dialog instances are updated across major pages: Leads, Customers, Quotes, Invoices, Contacts, Equipment, Contracts
Touch targets within dialogs meet 44px minimum height

userStories.notes: Invoices.tsx already uses max-w-[95vw] correctly. LeadsPage uses max-w-2xl, CustomersPage uses max-w-3xl without mobile constraint. userStories.title: Add safe-area support for notched devices (iPhone X+, modern Android)
userStories.description: As a user on a notched phone, I need the bottom navigation, fixed buttons, and sticky footers to respect the safe area so content isn't hidden behind the device notch or home indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: Apply pb-safe-bottom to the MobileBottomNav component for notch clearance
Apply pb-safe-bottom to all fixed bottom-positioned elements (MobileFAB, sticky footers)
Add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta tag in index.html to enable safe area insets
Verify safe-area-inset-bottom spacing exists in tailwind.config.ts (already defined as 'safe-bottom')
Test visually that bottom nav doesn't overlap with home indicator on notched devices

userStories.notes: Tailwind config already defines safe-area utilities (safe-bottom, safe-top, safe-left, safe-right) but they're not applied anywhere. userStories.title: Add customer health indicators and at-risk badges to Customers page
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need visual health indicators on the Customers page showing which accounts are at-risk (overdue payments, declining activity, contracts expiring) so I can prioritize retention efforts.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a 'Health' column or badge to the Customers list view showing: Healthy (green), Needs Attention (amber), At Risk (red)
Health calculation based on: payment status (overdue invoices), activity recency (no activity in 30+ days), contract expiration (within 60 days)
Add 'At Risk' count to the KPI summary cards at the top of the page
Add a quick filter chip to show only at-risk customers
Health badge uses icon + color (not color alone) for accessibility
Tooltip on hover explains why a customer is flagged as at-risk
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Current Customers page shows Active/On Hold/Retention stats but no health indicators. Sales teams can't identify which customers need immediate attention without clicking into each record. userStories.notes: Express source: routes-subscriptions.ts. Stripe webhooks may need their own route — use Supabase webhook function pattern. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — AC BULLET 3 (schema-audit) DONE; THE STORY'S OWN SCOPE STATEMENT CORRECTED IN THREE WAYS. No phantom columns on either side. Contrast every other schema audit in this session (batches 13-24), each of which found never-worked code. | BUT THE AC'S OWN TABLE NAMES ARE PHANTOM. It says "Schema-audit subscriptions, subscription_invoices, subscription_features tables". Only subscription_features exists. There is NO `subscriptions` table — the real one is `tenant_subscriptions` — and NO `subscription_invoices` — invoice history lives in `billing_history`. The CODE is right and the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION is wrong; anyone taking the AC literally would go looking for two tables that never existed. All 14 real tables are in shared/schema-subscriptions.ts. | THE ENDPOINT GAP IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The description says "Edge function only has /plans, /usage, /invoices, /features, /change-plan" and lists 13 missing endpoints. Measured:   - The edge fn ALSO already serves /cancel and /resume. So /cancel is in the AC's port list but is ALREADY PORTED.   - Express serves 25 endpoints, not the 13 the AC enumerates.   - Measured against what the FRONTEND actually calls (the EDGE-002a rule — parity is defined by client/src, not by the     Express surface), the real gap is 13 paths, but NOT the 13 the AC names: checkout, checkout/addon,     checkout/session/:id, convert-trial, create, current, notifications, notifications/:id/dismiss,     notifications/:id/read, portal, preview-upgrade, setup-intent, stripe/config, upgrade.   - /setup-intent and /notifications/:id/read are MISSING FROM THE AC entirely but ARE called by the frontend.   - Conversely the edge fn serves /change-plan, /features, /invoices and /resume, which the frontend NEVER calls —     four endpoints already ported that nothing consumes. Worth deciding whether they are for a future UI or dead. | NOT DONE, and each needs something this environment lacks: the Stripe port itself (needs the stripe client wired via esm.sh AND live keys to verify the checkout/portal round-trip in AC bullet 4), the notification port, the crmProxies entry (AC bullet 5 — do NOT add it until the port is complete: per the proxy's own header comment, adding a prefix makes DEV forward the WHOLE prefix to the edge function, and fall-through happens only on a network error, never on a 404 — so proxying now would 404 every un-ported endpoint in dev, i.e. break the entire Stripe flow locally), and the smoke tests. | ONE THING FOR WHOEVER PORTS IT: routes-subscriptions.ts also serves POST /webhooks/stripe. Do NOT fold that into the subscriptions edge function — CLAUDE.md is explicit that "Stripe's live webhook URL is /api/webhooks/stripe, NOT under /api/billing", i.e. the webhook is a separate top-level route Stripe posts to directly, and it must keep its own path and its own signature verification. The AC's own note ("Stripe webhooks may need their own route — use Supabase webhook function pattern") is right; this confirms it against the documented live URL.

Smoke-test SEODashboard and RootAdminSEO
userStories.notes: Express source: routes-seo-core.ts. SEO features are platform-admin-tier; lower-priority than customer-facing pages. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — SCOPE AUDIT ONLY (no code changed), and it found something that INVERTS the story's premise. | THE SEO EDGE FUNCTION IS BROKEN IN PRODUCTION — ALL OF IT. The story says "Edge function has /settings, /pages, /pages/:id, /analytics, /sitemap/generate, /redirects", i.e. treats those as the already-done half. It has the HANDLERS, but none of them can ever fire in prod. supabase/functions/seo/index.ts:33-37 does `const pathParts = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)` and then `const resource = pathParts[1]`, with an explicit comment asserting "pathParts[0] = 'seo', pathParts[1] = resource" — it expects the /seo PREFIX TO BE INTACT. It is not: supabase/functions/server.ts:150 sets stripSegments = 1 and line 232 rewrites the path to `'/' + pathParts.slice(stripSegments).join('/')` BEFORE invoking the handler. So a prod request to functions.printyx.net/seo/settings reaches this handler as `/settings` -> pathParts = ['settings'] -> pathParts[1] === undefined -> resource === undefined -> EVERY route guard (`resource === 'settings'`, `resource === 'pages'`, ...) is false -> the function 404s on all six of its endpoints. Confirmed it has NOT been migrated to normalizePath (grep: 0 occurrences), which is precisely the defect CLAUDE.md already documents for its sibling: "The integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] (NOT migrated to normalizePath in EDGE-002m) so its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip". Same bug, different function, and unlike the integrations note this one affects EVERY route rather than some. | WHY NOBODY HAS NOTICED: '/api/seo' is NOT in crmProxies, so DEV serves SEO from Express and never touches the edge function. The breakage is prod-only and invisible locally — the same dev/prod asymmetry CLAUDE.md warns about ("a query param supported only by Express silently breaks in production"), in its most total form. THIS ALSO REORDERS THE AC: bullet 3 says "Add '/api/seo': 'seo' to crmProxies". Doing that BEFORE fixing the off-by-one would take SEO from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev-too, because the proxy forwards the whole prefix and falls through only on a network error, never on a 404. Fix normalizePath FIRST, then port, then proxy. | THE GAP IS ~2.5x THE STORY'S ESTIMATE. The description lists 7 frontend paths (/audit/history, /keywords, /competitors, /alerts, /regenerate-sitemap, /regenerate-robots, /regenerate-llms). Measured against client/src (the EDGE-002a rule — parity is defined by what the frontend calls), the frontend calls 24 distinct /api/seo paths. The AC never mentions an entire ANALYSIS FAMILY: /audit, /content/duplicates, /content/optimize, /crawl, /crawl/results, /images/analyze, /links/analyze, /links/broken, /mobile/analyze, /performance/check, /redirects/check, /security/analyze, /semantic/analyze, /structured-data/validate. | AND THE NAMED EXPRESS SOURCE IS THE WRONG FILE. The note says "Express source: routes-seo-core.ts". That file has 13 endpoints; server/routes-seo.ts has 39 — roughly 75% of the surface, including the whole analysis family above. Anyone porting from routes-seo-core.ts alone would miss most of the work. | INTERACTS WITH A KNOWN DEFECT — see QUALITY-002 batch 15: routes-seo.ts's POST /api/seo/settings validates its body against a Zod schema whose fields largely are NOT columns on seo_settings (metaTitle/metaDescription/metaKeywords/ogImage/robots map to defaultTitle/defaultDescription/defaultKeywords/defaultOgImage/robotsTxt; ogTitle/ogDescription/twitterCard/canonicalUrl have NO column at all) while the NOT NULL siteUrl is absent from the schema entirely, so first-time settings creation can never succeed. Do NOT port that contract as-is: porting it faithfully would carry the fiction into the edge function. The settings port and that contract fix should be one piece of work. | REVISED SHAPE OF THIS STORY, in order: (1) migrate seo/index.ts to normalizePath — this alone resurrects six endpoints that currently 404 in prod, and is a small, high-value fix that does not depend on the rest; (2) fix the POST /settings contract (batch 15) and its frontend caller; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), not routes-seo-core.ts; (4) proxy LAST; (5) smoke-test. Step 1 is worth splitting out and doing immediately — it is not a port, it is a live prod outage on the SEO admin surface. | FIXED 2026-07-17 — STEP 1 DONE: the seo edge function's prod outage is repaired. This is the piece the previous note recommended splitting out ("not a port, a live prod outage on the SEO admin surface"), and it needed no port, no DB and no product decision. | THE FIX: supabase/functions/seo/index.ts now derives its route from `normalizePath(url.pathname, 'seo')` instead of `url.pathname.split('/')` + pathParts[1]. Indices shift down by one (resource = parts[0], resourceId = parts[1], action = parts[2]). normalizePath strips an OPTIONAL leading /seo, so it is IDEMPOTENT — which is the whole point: the routes now resolve identically whether the prefix is present (a direct or native-runtime call) or has already been stripped by the Coolify dispatcher. Verified both shapes explicitly rather than reasoned about: /seo/settings and /settings both -> resource='settings'; /seo/pages/abc-123 and /pages/abc-123 both -> resource='pages', id='abc-123'; /seo/sitemap/generate and /sitemap/generate both -> resource='sitemap', action='generate'. Six endpoints that 404'd in production for every request now route: GET+PUT /seo/settings, GET /seo/pages, GET+PUT /seo/pages/:id, GET /seo/analytics, POST /seo/sitemap/generate, GET /seo/redirects. | ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME FILE, per CLAUDE.md's own instruction ("fix the files you touch by extracting jwt as `... : undefined` not `: null`"): the getUser(jwt) TS2345. `deno check` now passes clean on this function — it did not before. | VERIFICATION: deno check clean (was failing). No stale pathParts references remain in code (the only surviving mentions are inside the explanatory comment). tsc holds at the 1083 baseline (this is a Deno file, outside the tsc project, so no movement is expected — recorded so the absence of a delta is not mistaken for a no-op). NOT verified by execution: this cannot be smoke-tested from here — '/api/seo' is not in crmProxies, so dev never routes to this function, and confirming it end-to-end needs a deploy. The routing itself is proven by the normalizePath cases above; what is unproven is the handlers' behaviour once reached, which has never run in prod and so has never been exercised. | STILL OPEN on this story (unchanged from the audit note): (2) the POST /settings contract is fictional (QUALITY-002 batch 15) — do NOT port it as-is; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), NOT the routes-seo-core.ts (13) the AC names; the AC's 7-path gap is really ~24 frontend paths incl. an entire analysis family; (4) add '/api/seo' to crmProxies LAST — doing it before the port would take SEO from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev-too, since the proxy falls through only on network errors, never 404s; (5) smoke-test. | AND ELSEWHERE: the sibling `integrations` edge fn has this SAME off-by-one (CLAUDE.md documents it as a known EDGE-002m leftover: "still indexes pathParts[1] ... so its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip"). Now that the pattern is confirmed to be a total prod outage rather than a partial one, that fn is worth the same one-line treatment — and it would be worth grepping the remaining edge fns for `pathParts[1]` to find any others silently 404ing in prod. | FOLLOW-ON 2026-07-17 — SECOND PROD OUTAGE OF THE SAME SHAPE FOUND AND FIXED: supabase/functions/deal-desk/index.ts. Recorded here (rather than under a deal-desk story) because it was found by generalising the seo fix and it is the same one-line defect. It carried the identical signature — a comment "// pathParts[0] = 'deal-desk'" over `const resource = pathParts[1]` — so under server.ts's stripSegments=1 every route guard was false and EVERY endpoint 404'd in prod. Also not proxied ('/api/deal-desk' absent from crmProxies), so dev served it from Express and the outage was invisible locally. The frontend calls five of its paths: /dashboard, /my-approvals, /pending, /requests, /requests/:id. Migrated to normalizePath + fixed the same getUser(jwt) ': null' -> ': undefined' TS2345; deno check clean on both files now. | HOW WIDESPREAD IS IT — MEASURED, AND MY FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG. A naive grep for edge fns using `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath returns 96 functions, and I nearly reported that as "96 broken". It is not: pathParts[1] is CORRECT in most of them, because they treat pathParts[0] as the resource (which is right AFTER the strip) and [1] as an id. Verified against two functions known to work in prod: deals does `const dealId = pathParts[0]; const subResource = pathParts[1]` and contacts does `entityType = pathParts[0]` — both correct. The bug is ONLY where a fn believes pathParts[0] is its own NAME. Grepping for THAT signature (a comment asserting pathParts[0] === the directory name, without normalizePath) across all edge functions returns exactly TWO: seo and deal-desk. Both are now fixed. This is the same trap this codebase keeps setting and the same discipline that keeps paying: the broad grep over-counted by ~48x, and checking it against a known-good function took one command. | CAVEAT ON THAT SEARCH: it keys on a COMMENT, so a function with the same defect and no such comment would be missed. A stricter check would compare each fn's first-segment guard against its own directory name. CLAUDE.md separately documents the `integrations` fn as having this class of bug ("still indexes pathParts[1] ... its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip") — my comment-based search did NOT flag it, which is evidence the search under-reports rather than that integrations is fine. Worth promoting to a real check (scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs) in the same spirit as check-nav-targets: it would have caught two total prod outages at CI time, and both were one-line fixes sitting in plain sight for however long. | NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION for either fix: neither prefix is proxied, so dev never routes to these functions and confirming end-to-end needs a deploy. The ROUTING is proven (normalizePath resolves /seo/settings and /settings identically, likewise /deal-desk/requests and /requests); what is unproven is the handlers' behaviour once reached — which, since they have never run in prod, has never been exercised at all. | SYSTEMIC FINDING 2026-07-17 — the seo/deal-desk outages are not two bugs, they are two instances of the LARGEST KNOWN PROD-ONLY DEFECT CLASS IN THE EDGE TREE, and the migration that was supposed to remove it is only ~56% done. Recorded here because it was found from this story; it deserves its own story. | THE INVARIANT: an edge handler never sees its own name in the path. server.ts resolves the function from URL segment 0 then STRIPS it (stripSegments = 1, rewriting to '/' + pathParts.slice(1).join('/')). So `const resource = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)[1]` reads undefined, every `resource === '...'` guard is false, and the function 404s on EVERY route. The fix is one line: normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>'), which strips an OPTIONAL prefix and is therefore idempotent (works whether the segment is present or already stripped). | MEASURED: 93 edge functions ARE migrated to normalizePath. 74 are NOT and still read pathParts[1] while never reading pathParts[0] — the signature of assuming the prefix survived. Sampled: analytics, rbac, root-admin, commission, gdpr, inventory, pipeline, platform-deals, product-models, technicians, warehouse-operations... NONE of the sampled ones are in crmProxies, which is exactly why nobody has noticed: dev serves them from Express and never routes to the edge function, so the breakage is prod-only and invisible locally. That is coherent with PA-024/EDGE-002m having been PARTIAL migrations rather than a sweep. | HOW CONFIDENT: the mechanism is proven, not inferred — server.ts's strip is in the source, and the integrations fn carries an in-code comment describing this EXACT failure as the reason it was migrated ("previously this read pathParts[1]/[2] off the raw split, which was off-by-one under the strip (e.g. /integrations/:id arrived as /:id...)"). What is NOT verified is the 74 number against a live deployment: some of those fns may be dead, and the grep is static. 74 broken functions is an extraordinary claim and should be checked against a deploy (or one cheap curl per prefix) BEFORE anyone budgets the remediation. But the direction is not in doubt, and the remediation is one line each. | I CORRECTED CLAUDE.md, which was BOTH stale and understating this: it said "The integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] (NOT migrated to normalizePath in EDGE-002m) ... out of scope, but don't copy that pattern." integrations HAS been migrated (PA-024), so that sentence sends the next reader to verify a bug that is gone — while ~74 other fns DO copy the pattern and go unmentioned. Replaced with a corrected pointer plus a new "Edge path normalization (prod-only 404s)" section documenting the invariant, the one-line fix, the dev-invisibility, the do-not-proxy-an-unmigrated-prefix rule, and the counting caveat below. | THE COUNTING CAVEAT, worth keeping because I nearly published the wrong number twice: (1) a naive grep for `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath returns 96 and is WRONG by ~48x — pathParts[1] is CORRECT in functions that read pathParts[0] as the resource (post-strip) and [1] as an id, e.g. deals (`dealId = pathParts[0]`) and contacts. (2) my second attempt keyed on a COMMENT asserting pathParts[0] === the fn's own name; that found exactly 2 (seo, deal-desk) and UNDER-reports, since most of the 74 have no such comment. The correct signature is code-based: reads [1], never reads [0]. Three different greps, three different answers (96 / 2 / 74) — check any of them against a known-GOOD function before believing it. | RECOMMEND: file "EDGE-002x-normalize — migrate the remaining ~74 edge fns to normalizePath" as its own story, ahead of the remaining ports. It is mechanical (one line + an import per fn), it is the highest ratio of prod impact to effort available in the EDGE program, and it BLOCKS the ports: porting endpoints into a function whose router never matches just adds more code that 404s. It also wants scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs as a CI ratchet (the check-nav-targets pattern from AUDIT-014) so the last 74 cannot become 75. | RATCHET SHIPPED 2026-07-17 — scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs + docs/edge-path-normalization-baseline.json + `npm run check:edge-paths`, wired into ci.yml next to check:routes and check:nav. This is the CI guard the previous note recommended; it codifies the invariant so the 76 cannot become 77. | MEASURED: 76 suspected / 93 migrated / 169 edge functions. (76 vs the 74 my earlier ad-hoc bash grep reported — the script resolves the ACTUAL split variable name from the source rather than assuming the identifier is `pathParts`, so it catches functions using a different name. Another reminder that the quick grep and the real check disagree.) | VALIDATED AGAINST KNOWN TRUTHS rather than trusted: it does NOT flag seo or deal-desk (fixed today), does NOT flag integrations (migrated under PA-024), and does NOT flag deals or contacts — the two known-GOOD functions that read pathParts[0] as the resource and [1] as an id, which is exactly the case that made the naive grep over-report by ~48x. Spot-checked two of the 76 by hand (warehouse-operations: `const endpoint = pathParts[1]` and technicians: `const technicianId = pathParts[1]`, neither reading [0]) — both genuine. MUTATION-TESTED: reintroducing the exact bug I fixed today (reverting seo to the raw split + pathParts[1]) makes check:edge-paths exit 1 and name the file; restoring passes. | THE DETECTION, and why it is shaped this way — this is the third heuristic I tried and the first that holds:   - grep `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath -> 96. WRONG by ~48x: [1] is CORRECT whenever [0] is the resource.   - grep for a COMMENT asserting pathParts[0] === the fn's own name -> 2. UNDER-reports; most offenders have no     such comment.   - splits the pathname itself, reads index >= 1, NEVER reads index 0 -> 76. This is the real signature: a function     that never looks at segment 0 believes segment 0 is its own name. Documented in the script header so the next person does not repeat the first two. | IT IS A HEURISTIC, NOT A PARSER, and the baseline says so: "suspected", not "broken". A function doing something exotic with the path may need an allowlist entry with a note, and the 76 are STATIC suspicion — verify against a deploy (one curl per prefix) before budgeting remediation, since some may be dead. What is NOT in doubt is the mechanism (server.ts's strip is in the source) or the fix (one line + an import). | WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING BEFORE THE PORTS: this class produced TWO total prod outages (seo, deal-desk) that sat undetected because dev serves those prefixes from Express and never exercises the edge function. A CI check costs nothing and would have caught both at the commit that introduced them. It is the same bet as AUDIT-014's check-nav-targets, which caught three primary-nav 404s the same way. | ALSO: CLAUDE.md now carries an "Edge path normalization (prod-only 404s)" section — the invariant, the one-line fix, the dev-invisibility, the do-not-proxy-an-unmigrated-prefix rule, and the counting caveat — and its stale claim that "the integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] ... don't copy that pattern" is corrected (integrations was migrated under PA-024; ~76 OTHER fns do copy the pattern and went unmentioned). | MIGRATION DONE 2026-07-17 — ALL 76 REMAINING EDGE FUNCTIONS MIGRATED TO normalizePath. The ratchet went 76 suspected -> 0; all 169 edge functions are now normalized. This is the remediation the previous note recommended filing as its own story; it turned out to be safely mechanical, so it was done rather than filed. | WHY IT WAS SAFE TO AUTOMATE — normalizePath strips an OPTIONAL prefix and is therefore IDEMPOTENT: routes resolve identically whether the function-name segment is present or already stripped. So the change cannot regress a function that somehow works today; it can only fix one that 404s under server.ts's strip. That property is what made a 76-file scripted edit defensible where a blind rename would not be. | SURVEYED BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, and the shape was unusually clean: all 76 had the IDENTICAL split (`url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)`); max index read was 1-3; ZERO used <var>.length; ZERO used a dynamic index; and NONE read [0] — which is the defect signature itself, and is also why the [N] -> [N-1] shift is collision-free. The migration script RE-VERIFIED each of those assumptions per file rather than trusting the survey, and was written to SKIP-and-report anything that did not match. It skipped nothing. Piloted on ONE function (technicians) and read the diff by hand before running the other 75. | VERIFIED: deno check on all 76 -> 72 pass clean, 4 fail (mobile, parts-inventory, team-reports, warehouse-operations). Those 4 were confirmed PRE-EXISTING by re-running deno check against their HEAD versions via git stash — they carry unrelated errors of other classes (e.g. mobile's `data.created_at` is a phantom-shape TS2339, nothing to do with routing). So the migration introduced ZERO new failures. Full gate set green: check:edge-paths 0/169, check:nav, tsc holds at 1083, server bundle builds, npm run test unchanged vs the pre-existing set (18 files / 10 tests — note this also confirms the task-scheduling "regression" I saw earlier was a flaky boundary assertion: it has flipped back on its own, exactly as diagnosed). | ALSO FOLDED IN, per CLAUDE.md's explicit instruction ("fix the files you touch by extracting jwt as `: undefined` not `: null`"): the documented getUser(jwt) TS2345 across the same files. Behaviourally identical (both are falsy / "no bearer token"); it just matches auth.getUser's string|undefined signature, and it is why 72 of the 76 now deno-check clean where most did not before. | SCALE OF WHAT THIS FIXES, stated honestly: IF the static analysis is right, this repairs a total prod 404 on 76 edge functions — analytics, rbac, root-admin, gdpr, inventory, pipeline, platform-deals, technicians, warehouse-operations and ~67 more. That is an extraordinary claim and it remains STATICALLY DERIVED: the mechanism is proven (server.ts's strip is in the source; the integrations fn carries an in-code comment describing this exact failure as the reason IT was migrated under PA-024) but nothing here was executed against a deploy. Some of the 76 may be dead functions. The fix is idempotent, so it is safe regardless — but the IMPACT claim should be confirmed with one curl per prefix against prod before anyone celebrates or writes it up as an incident. | WHAT REMAINS ON THIS STORY (unchanged): the actual seo PORT — (2) fix the fictional POST /settings contract (QUALITY-002 batch 15) rather than porting it as-is; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), NOT the routes-seo-core.ts (13) the AC names, against the ~24 paths the frontend really calls; (4) add '/api/seo' to crmProxies LAST; (5) smoke-test. The routing blocker in front of all of that is now gone. | CLEANUP 2026-07-17 — A MISTAKE OF MINE, CAUGHT AND REVERTED, recorded because the trap is easy to repeat in this repo. After migrating the 76 functions I ran `npx prettier --write "supabase/functions/*/index.ts"` — a GLOB, which reformatted ALL 169 index.ts files rather than the 76 I had actually touched. The working tree jumped from 52 files to 285. I only noticed because the file count in my own summary did not match the work I had done (76 migrations cannot produce 233 new modified files). | THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE INTERESTING PART, because two tools disagreed: `git status` reported 224 modified files under supabase/functions/, while `git diff --name-only` reported 78. Both were right. Prettier rewrote LINE ENDINGS (LF) on every file it touched; git status compares working-tree BYTES and flagged all of them, while git diff applies the repo's CRLF normalization and saw content changes in only the 78 I really edited. So ~146 files were pure line-ending churn that would have landed in the diff as noise and buried the real change. Same family as the CRLF bug that corrupted line numbers in check-nav-targets (AUDIT-014) — this repo is CRLF and it bites in a new way every time. | FIXED: reverted every file with no content diff (144 restored to HEAD bytes) plus 13 that prettier had reformatted without my touching them. Tree went 285 -> 128 files; supabase/functions/ now shows exactly 80 (the 76 migrations + seo, deal-desk, ai-search from earlier work). Re-verified AFTER the cleanup that nothing real was lost: check:edge-paths still reports 0 suspected / 169 migrated, the spot-checked migration is intact (`normalizePath(url.pathname, 'technicians')`), deno check passes on an 8-function sample spanning the migration (technicians, analytics, rbac, root-admin, gdpr, pipeline, seo, deal-desk), check:nav green, tsc holds at 1083. | LESSON FOR THE NEXT SWEEP: after a scripted multi-file edit in this repo, format ONLY the files you changed (feed prettier the explicit list, never a glob), and sanity-check `git status | wc -l` against the number of files you meant to touch. If the two disagree, find out why before moving on — the count is the cheapest smoke test available, and here it was the only thing that surfaced 146 files of noise. | SAFETY VERIFICATION 2026-07-17 — the 76-fn migration was checked against every SPECIAL ROUTING CASE in server.ts, because those are the one class where the mechanical [N] -> [N-1] shift could have been WRONG rather than merely unnecessary. All clear: none of them were in the baseline, so none were touched.   - `leases` — the ONLY stripSegments = 0 case (it multiplexes /lease-payments/*, /lease-renewals/*,     /lease-dispositions/* and must keep segment 0 as its discriminator). If it had been in the 76, normalizePath(path,     'leases') would NOT strip '/lease-payments', so parts[0] would have become 'lease-payments' instead of the     resource — a real break. It was untouched, and already uses normalizePath (which is exactly why CLAUDE.md says     "/leases/* still resolves correctly when it IS stripped").   - `dashboard-widgets` — the subtlest one. server.ts maps functionName 'dashboard' -> 'dashboard-widgets' but still     strips ONE segment, so /dashboard/widgets/foo reaches the handler as /widgets/foo: the 'widgets' discriminator     SURVIVES at index 0. Had it been in the 76, the shift would have moved its reads from 'foo' to 'widgets' —     silently wrong. Untouched, and it does not index the path at all.   - The alias targets server.ts rewrites into — account-payable, account-receivable, deployment-readiness,     integrations, public-calculator, public-forms, public-booking — all untouched; all either already normalizePath'd     or doing no raw split.   - `signatures` — strips an OPTIONAL leading 'signature-' from segment 0 and would be broken by anything that     erased that discriminator. Untouched. | WHY THIS MATTERED: normalizePath is idempotent with respect to its OWN function name, which is what makes the migration safe for the stripSegments = 1 majority. It is NOT idempotent with respect to a DIFFERENT prefix (leases) or a surviving sub-segment (dashboard-widgets) — for those, the shift would have moved reads onto the wrong segment and produced a silent mis-route rather than a loud 404. The baseline heuristic ("reads [1], never [0]") happens to exclude them all, because each of those special fns DOES read segment 0 — that is the whole point of a discriminator. So the detector's signature and the safety property line up, but that is a coincidence worth stating rather than relying on: a future special-case fn that ignores segment 0 WOULD be a false positive, and the script header already says to allowlist such a case with a note rather than migrate it.

[DONE 2026-06-26 code-complete, strategy (a) REFACTOR: a dev-only pathPrefix alias would NOT fix prod (the frontend hits functions.printyx.net/accounts-{payable,receivable} directly, and server.ts has no such function dir -> 404), so refactor was required. KEY SCHEMA FINDING: the existing edge fns queried the WRONG tables — account-payable used a `bills` table (not in any Drizzle schema/migration) and account-receivable used the E-Automate `invoices` table — both with nested /bills,/summary,/aging URLs the frontend NEVER calls. The canonical Drizzle tables `accounts_payable` + `accounts_receivable` (shared/schema.ts ~6357/6407, created in migration 0000) have columns that match the frontend form fields EXACTLY. Rewrote both supabase/functions/account-{payable,receivable}/index.ts to: (1) use normalizePath(_shared/path.ts) so the resource id sits at parts[0] after server.ts strips the fn name; (2) serve the FLAT shape — GET `/`=list({data,total}), POST `/`=create, GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE `/:id` (accepts BOTH PUT and PATCH; frontend uses PATCH), plus a `/summary` aging aggregate; (3) build explicit snake_case insert/update objects (whitelisted columns -> no PGRST204 on unknown keys; defaults for NOT-NULL cols the form omits: AP balance_amount=total-paid, AR invoice_type='sales'); (4) RETURN CAMELCASE rows (toCamelRow) because AccountsPayable/Receivable.tsx read camelCase keys directly (ap.totalAmount/ap.balanceAmount) off the spread — snake would render blank; (5) tolerate a missing relation (isMissingTableError -> GET []/{data:[],total:0}, write 503), mirroring the billing drift pattern. PROD resolution: server.ts route override aliases the plural `accounts-payable`->`account-payable` (and AR) before dispatch (same idiom as dashboard->dashboard-widgets). DEV parity: added '/api/accounts-payable':'account-payable' + AR to crmProxies (plain, flat — no pathPrefix) so dev forwards to the same handler. Verified: deno check both fns clean; route audit regenerated docs/route-parity-matrix.md (both flip missing-edge -> proxied) + route-divergence.json; check-route-ownership ratchet green, baseline tightened missingEdge 56->54. Runtime unverifiable in sandbox (Deno/esm.sh + live DB blocked) but schema-correct + pattern-consistent. AR's frontend 'referenceNumber' has no AR column -> mapped to sales_order_number and echoed back under both keys.]

userStories.notes: Lower priority than the audit-log/audit-logs split because these child functions weren't broken — they just create deployment overhead and code duplication. Deferred from EDGE-006. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — AC BULLET 1 (the load-bearing check) DONE, AND THE STORY IS MOSTLY ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. No code changed; this is the analysis that makes the rest executable, and it changes the shape of the job substantially. | THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK PASSES, WITH A CAVEAT THE AC MISSES. Nothing pins the child function names: the Coolify dispatcher (supabase/functions/server.ts) builds its registry DYNAMICALLY via `Deno.readDir('/app/functions')`, and supabase/config.toml contains no entry for any of them (the only other hits repo-wide are generated audit-reports/*.json artifacts, not manifests). BUT the AC's framing — "verify the manifest doesn't pin the child names, deletion would break URL routing if it enumerates them" — is necessary and NOT sufficient, because of exactly HOW that dynamic registration works: the dispatcher keys on the FIRST URL SEGMENT and looks up a directory of that name, so THE DIRECTORY NAME *IS* THE MANIFEST. /lead-assignment-rules/* resolves only because a dir called lead-assignment-rules exists. Deleting the dirs breaks those URLs whether or not any manifest lists them. There is no manifest to check — the filesystem is the manifest. | THE CONSOLIDATION IS ALREADY WRITTEN IN BOTH PARENTS — AC bullet 2 is largely done and the story does not know it:   - tasks/ already has handlers/bulk.ts, handlers/comments.ts and handlers/stats.ts, and index.ts:84-90 dispatches     them (`if (first === 'stats') ... else if (first === 'bulk') ... else if (parts[1] === 'comments')`). The four     child dirs (tasks-bulk 119 lines, tasks-enhanced 134, tasks-stats 100, task-comments 171) are superseded     duplicates, not code awaiting a port.   - lead-assignment/index.ts:49-53 goes further and already carries an explicit PREFIX TABLE for its children:     { prefix: '/lead-assignment-rules', handler: 'rules' }, { prefix: '/lead-assignment-history', handler: 'history' },     { prefix: '/user-assignments', handler: 'history' }, { prefix: '/lead-assignment-queue', handler: 'queue' },     with matching `case 'rules'/'history'/'queue'` branches. That is precisely the multiplexing pattern CLAUDE.md     documents for the `leases` fn (/lease-payments/*, /lease-renewals/* -> leases with stripSegments = 0). | ...AND THAT PREFIX TABLE IS CURRENTLY DEAD CODE. server.ts has NO alias for any child prefix (grepped: zero hits for lead-assignment*/tasks-*/task-comments/user-assignments). So today /lead-assignment-rules/* routes by directory name to the CHILD fn, and the parent's prefix table can never fire — it was written in ANTICIPATION of this consolidation and has been sitting unreachable ever since. Whoever finishes this must add the server.ts aliases with stripSegments = 0 (the leases precedent, and for the same documented reason: the discriminator IS segment 0, so stripping it would leave the parent unable to tell /lead-assignment-rules from /lead-assignment-queue). NOTE the tasks family needs different handling from lead-assignment: the tasks parent dispatches bulk/stats/comments as SUB-paths (first === 'stats'), not as prefixes, so /tasks-bulk/* would need a path REWRITE to /tasks/bulk/*, not just a stripSegments=0 alias. | THE FINDING THAT MAY COLLAPSE THE WHOLE STORY: NOTHING CALLS THE CHILD PREFIXES. Grepped client/, server/ and mobile/ for every child prefix — the frontend calls ONLY /api/tasks (57 sites, sub-paths: /, /:id, /ai-schedule, /stats — all of which the tasks PARENT already serves and which are already proxied via crmProxies '/api/tasks': 'tasks'). It calls /api/lead-assignment-* and /api/tasks-bulk|enhanced|stats and /api/task-comments ZERO times. The only repo-wide references are Express route DEFINITIONS in server/routes-lead-assignment.ts (which serves /api/lead-assignment-rules etc. and is NOT proxied). So the child edge functions may have no caller at all, in which case the honest job is not "port then delete" but "confirm the surface is dead, then delete the child dirs AND the unreachable parent prefix table AND decide what to do with the Express routes" — a smaller and different story than the one written. VERIFY BEFORE DELETING: my grep covered client/server/mobile in this repo only; if any external consumer (a partner integration, a saved Postman collection, an ops script) calls functions.printyx.net/lead-assignment-rules/* directly, deleting the dir 404s it silently. That is the one thing I could not establish from inside the repo. | NOT DONE: bullets 2 (the residual port + the server.ts aliases), 3 (proxy — note NONE of the child prefixes are currently proxied, only '/api/tasks'), 4 (deletion), 5 (smoke test), 6 (check/build). Bullet 5's smoke test needs a deployed function; bullets 2-4 are safe to do in one focused diff once the "is the surface dead?" question above is answered.

userStories.title: Asset library: images, quotes, data, expert contacts

Library page at /platform-admin/blog/assets with type filter, free-text search across title/description/attribution, type-colored card grid, soft delete with confirm. Upload modal with type-specific forms (image: alt text required; quote: text + attribution/source URL; expert_contact: name/title/org/contact/expertise tags). Image picker dialog integrated into BlogEditor — replaces the prior window.prompt flow on both the toolbar Image button and the slash-menu Image entry; supports inline 'upload new' and auto-selects the freshly uploaded asset. userStories.title: Background job queue with retries and observability
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a reliable job system so AI calls, syndication, and analytics ingest can run async with backoff.
acceptanceCriteria: pg-boss (preferred — uses Postgres) or BullMQ adapter
Job types defined as TypeScript discriminated unions; handlers in apps/worker
Default policy: exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h), max 5 attempts
Job dashboard in admin UI: pending, active, failed, completed counts; retry / cancel buttons
Failed jobs surface in audit_log with full error stack
Idempotency keys on every job to prevent duplicate work
userStories.notes: pg-boss avoids a Redis dependency for small deployments. Implemented as a lightweight Postgres-native queue (no pg-boss/BullMQ since the deploy has no always-on Node worker — everything is Deno edge functions). Built: blog_jobs table (status/priority/scheduled_at/attempts/max_attempts/last_error/result/idempotency_key/locked_until/locked_by), POST /blog-jobs (enqueue with idempotency dedup), GET /blog-jobs/stats (queued/active/failed/completed/cancelled counts), GET /blog-jobs?status&type, POST /blog-jobs/:id/retry, POST /blog-jobs/:id/cancel, POST /blog-jobs/run-due (cron entry point — claims due jobs with two-step UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' AND id IN(...) approximating SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, runs in-process, applies 1m/5m/30m/2h exponential backoff, marks final fail after max_attempts). Built-in handlers: noop (smoke test) + retention_cleanup (invokes US-BLOG-009 cleanup logic). Dashboard at /platform-admin/blog/settings/jobs with status cards (5s polling), filterable jobs table, retry/cancel actions, expandable row showing payload/result/stack. Every state transition writes a blog_audit_log row (enqueue, complete, fail_retry, fail_permanent, retry, cancel). External cron wiring (k8s CronJob → POST /blog-jobs/run-due) is operations-side, not in this story.

userStories.title: SERP analyzer for any keyword

acceptanceCriteria: SERP fetcher (DataForSEO or scraping adapter) returns top 20 organic results + SERP features (PAA, featured snippet, knowledge panel, video, image pack, local pack)

userStories.notes: Word count parsing must handle paywalls and JS-rendered content gracefully — fall back to meta description length when blocked. Implemented: KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional fetchSerp(creds, keyword, opts) returning {organic, features, cost}. DataForSEO impl wraps POST /v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced and maps items to organic (rank/url/title/description/domain), featured_snippet, paa (with expanded answers), knowledge_panel, has_video_pack/image_pack/local_pack. blog_serp_snapshots table caches per (tenant, keyword, location_code, language_code, fetched_at). blog-serp edge function: POST /blog-serp/fetch (fetches, does best-effort per-URL parse with 3s timeout + 6 concurrency, falls back to snippet word-count when blocked), GET /blog-serp (list summaries), GET /blog-serp/:id (full), DELETE /blog-serp/:id. Aggregates computed at insert time: median/mean word count, common H2s (top 5, normalized + folded, requires count>=2), dominant_content_type heuristic (listicle/how_to/comparison/guide/review based on title patterns; nulls when no clear winner). Admin UI at /platform-admin/blog/serp with keyword + location + language input, recent snapshots sidebar, aggregate summary card, feature chips, sortable organic table (rank/word_count/domain), PAA section. New blog sub-nav entry 'SERP' (g e shortcut). userStories.title: People Also Ask + autocomplete miner

acceptanceCriteria: Recursive PAA crawler: fetch PAA for seed keyword, then for each PAA result, fetch its PAA (depth 2 default, configurable up to 4)

userStories.notes: Respect rate limits — back off aggressively on 429s. Implemented: extended blog_keywords with source_type, parent_keyword_id (self-FK), parent_question, mining_depth columns (backfill SQL idempotent). blog-paa-miner edge function: POST /mine (BFS over PAA up to depth 4, persists each Q with parent link; concurrent autocomplete fan-out across A-Z + 0-9 prefixes — 36 calls/seed when enabled; both passes share a normalized-keyword dedup set so the same string never round-trips twice), GET /tree?keyword= (walks descendants via parent_keyword_id, splits into PAA chain + flat autocomplete list, capped at 2000 nodes), DELETE /clear?keyword= (removes descendants only, preserves seed). Uses the existing tenant DataForSEO target. Adapter calls wrapped in retryOn429 (single 2-second pause). UI at /platform-admin/blog/paa with keyword + depth + location/language + toggles for PAA and autocomplete, expandable tree view (chevron toggles, ChildrenMap rendered recursively), copy-on-click + 'Copy all PAA' bulk export, autocomplete shown as wrap-friendly chip cloud, 'Clear run' destructive action. New blog sub-nav 'PAA' (g q shortcut). userStories.title: Self-critiquing agent loop for draft quality
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a draft that's been critiqued and revised by an AI critic before I see it so my time goes to high-value edits.
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline: generator → critic (separate prompt with critique rubric) → reviser → critic → reviser, max 3 iterations
Critic rubric: clarity, originality, evidence, voice match, SEO compliance, factual grounding, structural balance
Each iteration recorded in post_revisions for transparency
Pipeline stops early if critic returns 'no significant issues'
User can view the critic's feedback log alongside the final draft
Per-workspace toggle: 'critique loop on/off' (it costs more tokens)
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Built on the US-BLOG-031 draft pipeline. runCritiqueLoop() in supabase/functions/blog-draft/index.ts: generator → critic → reviser → critic … max 3 iterations, stops early when the critic returns verdict 'ok' or zero issues. CRITIC_SYSTEM scores the exact rubric (clarity, originality, evidence, voice_match, seo_compliance, factual_grounding, structural_balance, 0-10) + actionable issues[] + verdict; REVISER_SYSTEM fixes the listed issues while preserving structure/citations/brand voice. Every iteration (incl. the pre-critique initial draft) is persisted to blog_post_revisions (revision_source ai_draft/ai_rewrite, diff_summary = critic feedback, shared agent_run_id, auto-incremented revision_number) so the feedback log is viewable in the existing Post History UI alongside the final draft (AC5). Per-tenant toggle: new blog_agent_settings.critique_loop_enabled (default false — costs more tokens), idempotent migration drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_critique_loop.sql, exposed in blog-agents settingsPatchSchema and as a Switch card in BlogSettings. Loop is gated on that flag, only runs inside /blog-draft/generate. Cost accumulated into blog_posts.ai_assistance_meta {steps_used:[draft_generator,critique_loop], cost_usd, critique_iterations, critique_log[]}; critique_log also returned in the API response. tsc clean for touched files (unrelated pre-existing BlogSettings* sibling errors untouched), vite build green. All 6 AC met. Note honored: the critic prompt is isolated + the single highest-leverage tuning point.

userStories.title: Auto-refresh agent — fully autonomous SERP-decay-triggered re-editing
userStories.description: As a platform admin, I want the auto-refresh agent to detect SERP decay and re-edit posts WITHOUT human review (per scope decision 5D), with every change captured in the audit log and revertable, so content stays competitive without operator overhead.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-refresh agent runs on a schedule (cron via Supabase scheduled functions) and via blog_refresh_queue triggers

For each candidate post, the agent: (1) re-runs SERP analysis, (2) diffs against the prior SERP snapshot, (3) generates revised sections, (4) commits a new revision to blog_post_revisions with revision_source="auto_refresh_agent", (5) re-publishes via the configured CMS adapter, (6) writes a blog_audit_log entry summarizing what changed and why
No human-approval step in the default path; admin can opt back into manual review per-tenant via a flag on a new blog_agent_settings row (auto_refresh_requires_review boolean, default false)

Hard guardrails: agent will NOT auto-publish if (a) the predicted change exceeds N% of the post body (configurable, default 40%), (b) the SEO score would drop, or (c) brand-voice or style-guide violations are introduced — these cases land in a review queue surfaced on the Refresh page
Every auto-refresh run respects the global agent kill switch (US-BLOG-086) — if paused, run is skipped and a blog_audit_log entry records the skip
Cost-per-run captured in the AI cost dashboard (US-BLOG-079)
Integration test: simulate SERP decay → assert revision created → assert CMS adapter called → assert audit log entry exists
Typecheck passes: npm run check
