userStories.title: Agentic OS core schema: agent catalog + per-tenant agent settings (kill switch)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need a central registry of all AI agents and per-tenant enable/pause controls so every agent in the Agentic OS can be governed uniformly (generalizing the blog kill-switch pattern platform-wide).
acceptanceCriteria: New shared/agentic-os-schema.ts with two Drizzle tables: agent_definitions (platform catalog: agent_key unique, name, domain enum ['prospect','nurture','service','maintain','manage','security','develop'], description, default_tier smallint 1-3, default_model, is_enabled) and tenant_agent_settings (tenant_id, agent_key, enabled, autonomy_tier override nullable, paused boolean, paused_at, paused_by_user_id, paused_reason, pause_all boolean on a per-tenant global row, config jsonb, unique(tenant_id, agent_key))
Tables re-exported from shared/schema.ts
Migration generated via npm run db:generate (do NOT run db:push; do not apply to prod — journal apply is a manual step in this repo)
RLS SQL file drizzle/rls/agentic-os.sql: GRANT SELECT to authenticated + tenant-scoped policies (mirror drizzle/rls/blog.sql pattern)
Typecheck passes: npm run check (no new errors vs node scripts/check-types.mjs baseline)
userStories.notes: AGENTIC OS foundation story 1 of 5 schema stories. Generalizes blog_agent_settings (see supabase/functions/_shared/blog/safety/kill-switch.ts) to ALL agents. Do NOT touch blog tables — blog agents migrate onto this later. Domain values map to the business functions: prospect/nurture/service/maintain/manage/security/develop. Existing ai_employees tables (drizzle/rls/ai-employee-tables.sql) stay as-is; agent_definitions is the platform catalog, not per-tenant employee instances.

userStories.title: Agent job queue + schedules schema (Postgres-backed, no new infra)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need durable agent job and schedule tables so agent work survives restarts, retries with backoff, and dead-letters — using Postgres (the existing stack) instead of introducing Redis/RabbitMQ.
acceptanceCriteria: Add to shared/agentic-os-schema.ts: agent_jobs (id uuid default gen_random_uuid(), tenant_id, agent_key, job_type, payload jsonb, status enum ['queued','running','succeeded','failed','dead'], priority int default 5, run_at timestamptz, attempts int default 0, max_attempts int default 3, last_error text, correlation_id, created_by, locked_at, locked_by, created_at, updated_at)
Add agent_schedules (id, tenant_id, agent_key, interval_minutes int OR cron_expression varchar (one required), enabled boolean, last_run_at, next_run_at, unique(tenant_id, agent_key))
Composite index on agent_jobs (status, run_at, priority) for the claim query
Migration generated via npm run db:generate; RLS added to drizzle/rls/agentic-os.sql
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Explore audit confirmed NO job queue exists — cron-service.ts uses bare setInterval and ai-employee executes tasks inline in the request. Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (worker in AOS-006) is the right fit for this stack; do not add Redis/Bull. correlation_id threads one business event across jobs/audit/costs.

userStories.title: Unified agent audit log + agent action ledger schema
userStories.description: As a compliance owner, I need one append-only audit trail for every agent action platform-wide, plus an action ledger that records what each agent proposed, its tier, and what happened to it — so Tier 1 auto-executions and Tier 2/3 human reviews share a single source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Add agent_audit_log to shared/agentic-os-schema.ts: id, tenant_id, actor_type enum ['user','agent','system'], actor_id, agent_key, action varchar (dotted notation e.g. 'ticket.triage.auto_routed'), target_type, target_id, before_state jsonb, after_state jsonb, correlation_id, request_id, created_at — mirroring blog_audit_log columns

Add agent_actions: id, tenant_id, agent_key, action_type, tier smallint (1=auto, 2=human review, 3=human owned), status enum ['proposed','auto_executed','pending_review','approved','rejected','expired','failed'], confidence numeric(5,2), summary text, payload jsonb, result jsonb, idempotency_key varchar unique nullable, review_due_at, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, review_note, correlation_id, created_at, updated_at
RLS in drizzle/rls/agentic-os.sql makes agent_audit_log append-only: INSERT+SELECT policies only, NO UPDATE/DELETE policies (same as blog_audit_log in drizzle/rls/blog.sql)
Migration generated via npm run db:generate
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Generalizes supabase/functions/_shared/blog/audit-log.ts (writeAuditLog + withRequestContext). agent_actions is the HEART of the tiering model: Tier 1 rows go proposed->auto_executed in one run; Tier 2 rows sit pending_review until the Agent Inbox (AOS-015/016) approves; Tier 3 rows are escalations a human owns. idempotency_key prevents double-execution on job retry (AOS-011).

userStories.title: Unified agent AI cost + quota schema with shared logging helper
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need per-tenant LLM spend tracking and quotas across ALL agents (not just blog) so costs are visible and hard caps prevent runaway spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Add agent_ai_costs (append-only ledger: tenant_id, agent_key, provider, model, feature, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cost_cents, request_id, correlation_id, created_at) and agent_ai_quotas (tenant_id unique, monthly_limit_cents nullable, warn_threshold_pct default 80, hard_stop boolean default true, alert_email) to shared/agentic-os-schema.ts; migration generated

Node helper server/services/agentic/ai-cost.ts exporting logAgentCost(entry) (non-throwing) and getAgentQuotaStatus(tenantId) returning { limitCents, spentCents, pct, warn, blocked } — API mirrors supabase/functions/_shared/blog/ai-cost.ts
Deno twin supabase/functions/_shared/agentic/ai-cost.ts with the same exports (keep in sync comment header, like shared/quote-math.ts does)
Unit test server/tests/unit/agentic-ai-cost.test.ts covering quota math: no quota = never blocked; spend >= limit + hard_stop = blocked; warn at threshold pct
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: blog_ai_costs/blog_ai_quotas (supabase/functions/_shared/blog/ai-cost.ts) are the proven reference — same shape, agent_key instead of blog feature/post columns. ai_employee_tasks has estimated_cost/actual_cost fields that were never populated; the run harness (AOS-010) will populate via this helper instead.

userStories.title: Agent guardrail policy schema + typed policy accessor
userStories.description: As a company admin, I need per-tenant guardrail policies (confidence floors, dollar caps, action allowlists, daily action caps) that decide which tier an agent action lands in, so Tier 1 autonomy is bounded by explicit, auditable rules rather than model judgment.
acceptanceCriteria: Add agent_policies to shared/agentic-os-schema.ts: id, tenant_id, agent_key nullable (null = tenant-global), policy_key varchar, value jsonb, updated_by, updated_at, unique(tenant_id, agent_key, policy_key); migration generated
Typed accessor server/services/agentic/policies.ts: getAgentPolicy<T>(tenantId, agentKey, policyKey, defaultValue) — agent-specific row wins over tenant-global row wins over code default

Code defaults exported as AGENT_POLICY_DEFAULTS: confidence_min_auto (0.85), max_auto_dollar_amount (0 = money actions never Tier 1), daily_auto_action_cap (50), business_hours_only (false), tier1_action_allowlist (empty array = allow all non-money actions at agent's default tier)
Unit test server/tests/unit/agentic-policies.test.ts covering precedence (agent > tenant-global > default)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Explore audit: ai_employees.decision_threshold and task_context guards exist but are NEVER enforced. This table + AOS-010's classifier is the enforcement point. max_auto_dollar_amount=0 default means anything touching money (discounts, refunds, invoice adjustments, dunning sends) starts life as Tier 2 until a tenant explicitly raises it — safe-by-default.

userStories.title: Postgres job queue worker: claim, retry with backoff, dead-letter
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need a durable worker loop that claims agent_jobs safely under concurrency, retries failures with exponential backoff, and dead-letters poison jobs, so agent work is reliable without new infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/job-queue.ts: enqueueAgentJob(job), claimNextJob(workerId) using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on (status='queued' AND run_at <= now()) ordered by priority, run_at; sets status='running', locked_at, locked_by
completeJob / failJob: failure increments attempts, re-queues with exponential backoff (run_at = now + 2^attempts minutes) until max_attempts, then status='dead' with last_error
Worker loop started from server bootstrap ONLY when process.env.AGENTIC_OS_ENABLED==='true'; polls every 5s; graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (finish in-flight job, release nothing mid-transaction)
Stale-lock reaper: jobs stuck 'running' with locked_at older than 10 minutes are re-queued (attempt counted)
Unit tests server/tests/unit/agentic-job-queue.test.ts for backoff math and state transitions (db calls mocked)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Runs in the Express process (server/index.ts bootstrap) like cron-service.ts does today — no separate deployment. Job handlers registered by agent_key/job_type map (handlers arrive with each domain agent story). Keep the claim query to raw SQL via db.execute if Drizzle can't express SKIP LOCKED cleanly.

userStories.title: Agent scheduler: agent_schedules tick enqueues due agent jobs
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need recurring agent runs (nightly lead triage, hourly fleet checks) driven by per-tenant schedule rows so agents run themselves without manual triggering.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/scheduler.ts: tick() selects enabled agent_schedules where next_run_at <= now(), enqueues one agent_job per row (job_type='scheduled_run', correlation_id fresh uuid), advances next_run_at from interval_minutes (cron_expression support may TODO)
Skips enqueue (and audit-logs 'agent.run.skipped_kill_switch') when tenant_agent_settings has paused=true or pause_all=true for that tenant/agent — reuse the AOS-008 helper
Registered in server/services/cron-service.ts as a 60s interval, gated by AGENTIC_OS_ENABLED
Jitter: enqueued run_at spread over 0-30s so many tenants don't stampede one tick
Unit test for due/not-due/paused selection logic
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: cron-service.ts already hosts the hourly daily-briefing tick — follow that registration pattern. Duplicate-guard: tick claims schedules by updating next_run_at in the same statement (UPDATE ... RETURNING) so two ticks can't double-enqueue.

userStories.title: Shared kill-switch helper: assertAgentActive for Node and Deno
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need every agent entry point to check the per-tenant/per-agent kill switch before doing any work, exactly like blog agents do today, so a tenant (or platform admin) can stop any agent — or all agents — instantly.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/kill-switch.ts: assertAgentActive(tenantId, agentKey) -> settings row or null; null means paused (caller exits early); pause check covers agent row paused, tenant pause_all row, and agent_definitions.is_enabled=false (platform-level)
Paused invocations write an agent_audit_log entry action='agent.run.skipped_kill_switch' (actor_type='system') before returning null — never throws
Deno twin supabase/functions/_shared/agentic/kill-switch.ts with identical contract for edge-function agents
pauseAgent/resumeAgent helpers writing paused, paused_at, paused_by_user_id, paused_reason + audit entries
Unit tests for the three pause layers' precedence
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Contract copied from supabase/functions/_shared/blog/safety/kill-switch.ts assertAgentsActive (zero-throw, audit-on-skip, upsert-safe). Platform admin can flip agent_definitions.is_enabled to kill an agent across ALL tenants at once — that's the Tier-0 emergency brake.

userStories.title: Agent tool registry + executor with Zod validation and tenant pinning
userStories.description: As a security owner, I need agent tools defined in a code registry with schema-validated inputs and context-pinned tenant scope, so an LLM can never fabricate a tool call that crosses tenants or executes something unregistered.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/tools/registry.ts: ToolDefinition { key, description, inputSchema (Zod), mutates boolean, moneyAction boolean, handler(ctx, input) } and registerTool/getTool/listToolsForAgent(agentKey, allowlist)

ToolContext { tenantId, correlationId, agentKey, actingUserId? } is constructed by the harness ONLY — tenantId is never read from tool input, and any tenant_id/tenantId key in LLM-supplied input is stripped before validation
executeTool(ctx, toolKey, rawInput): unknown tool -> typed error; input validated via inputSchema.safeParse; every invocation writes agent_audit_log ('tool.<key>.invoked' with input/result summaries)

Ship 4 read-only starter tools in server/services/agentic/tools/read-tools.ts: get_customer_summary (business_records by id), list_overdue_invoices (accounts_receivable past due), list_open_tickets (service tickets), get_lead_details — every query filtered by ctx.tenantId
Unit tests: cross-tenant input stripped, invalid input rejected, unknown tool rejected
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Explore audit: ai-employee hard-codes a task_type switch with no tool schema — this replaces that pattern for AOS agents. Code registry (not a DB table) keeps handlers typed and reviewable; per-agent allowlists come from agent_policies tier1_action_allowlist later. accounts_receivable is the canonical AR table (EDGE-005a note in CLAUDE.md); leads/customers live in business_records.

userStories.title: Agent run harness: runAgentTask with kill switch, quota, cost, tier classification
userStories.description: As the Agentic OS kernel, I need one harness every agent runs through — kill switch, quota gate, LLM call with cost logging, structured action proposals, policy-based tier classification, and routing to auto-execute vs review queue — so all agents behave identically and safely.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/run-harness.ts: runAgentTask({ tenantId, agentKey, jobType, payload, correlationId }) executes the pipeline: assertAgentActive -> getAgentQuotaStatus (blocked => audit 'agent.run.blocked_quota' and stop) -> load policies -> agent-specific prompt fn -> Claude call -> logAgentCost -> parse JSON action proposals -> classify -> route

LLM calls go through the existing Anthropic helper (server/services/claude-ai-service.ts pattern), request structured JSON: array of { action_type, tool_key, tool_input, confidence 0-1, summary, dollar_amount? }

classifyTier(action, policies): moneyAction with dollar_amount > max_auto_dollar_amount => tier 2; confidence < confidence_min_auto => tier 2; tool not in allowlist (when set) => tier 2; daily_auto_action_cap exceeded (count today's auto_executed agent_actions) => tier 2; agent default_tier >= 2 => never below it; else tier 1

Routing: tier 1 => insert agent_actions status 'proposed' then execute via AOS-011 executor => 'auto_executed'; tier 2 => 'pending_review' with review_due_at = now + policy sla_hours (default 24); tier 3 => 'pending_review' + immediate escalation notification hook (no-op until AOS-014)
Every stage writes agent_audit_log with the run's correlation_id; malformed LLM JSON => job failure (retry via queue), never partial execution
Unit tests with mocked LLM covering: quota block, tier classification matrix, malformed JSON
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: THE keystone story — every domain agent (AOS-018+) is just a prompt builder + tool set plugged into this. Model: claude via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/CLAUDE_API_KEY (both env names in use today). Confidence is the model's self-report; policies treat it as a CEILING signal only (low confidence forces review; high confidence alone never overrides dollar/allowlist gates).

userStories.title: Action executor with idempotency + failure escalation
userStories.description: As the Agentic OS kernel, I need executing an agent action to be idempotent and state-machine-guarded, so a retried job or a double-clicked approval can never run a side effect twice.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/action-executor.ts: executeAgentAction(actionId, executedBy: 'system'|userId) loads the row, permits execution only from status 'proposed' (tier 1) or 'approved' (tier 2/3), executes payload.tool_key via AOS-009 executeTool, stores result jsonb, sets status 'auto_executed' (system) or keeps 'approved' with result + executed_at
Status transition uses a conditional UPDATE (WHERE status IN (...)) checked atomically; a concurrent second call gets 0 rows and returns { alreadyExecuted: true }
idempotency_key defaults to the action id; tool handlers receive it in ctx for downstream dedup (e.g. don't send the same email twice)
Execution failure: status 'failed', result.error captured, audit entry, and a Tier 2 review row is NOT auto-retried (humans decide on failed side effects)
Unit tests: double-execution race returns alreadyExecuted, invalid-status rejection, failure path
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Completes the kernel loop started in AOS-010. The conditional-UPDATE guard is the whole point — job retries (AOS-006 backoff) and Agent Inbox approvals (AOS-015) both funnel here.

userStories.title: Approval engine service executing the existing approval_rules chains
userStories.description: As a sales/finance manager, I need the approval_rules and approval_requests tables (which exist but have no engine) actually enforced — matching rules, building the approver chain, and advancing state on approve/reject — so Tier 2 business approvals flow instead of sitting inert.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/approval-engine.ts: createApprovalRequest(input) matches active approval_rules by rule_type + threshold (threshold_type/threshold_value/comparison_operator), picks highest-priority match, snapshots the approver chain into approval_requests.approval_chain, sets sla_expiry_at from rule.sla_hours, status 'pending'

recordDecision(requestId, approverId, 'approve'|'reject', note): validates approver is current-level eligible; sequential chains advance current_approval_level; parallel chains complete when all required approve; any_one chains complete on first approve; reject => status 'rejected'
Terminal transitions write the decision history into approval_chain jsonb and set approved_by/rejection fields as modeled in shared/deal-desk-schema.ts
No matching rule => auto-approved status with audit entry noting no rule matched (explicit, not silent)
Unit tests server/tests/unit/approval-engine.test.ts covering the three chain types + no-rule fallthrough
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Explore audit confirmed approval_rules/approval_requests/approval_delegations (shared/deal-desk-schema.ts) are schema-only today. This engine serves BOTH classic deal-desk approvals and Agentic OS Tier 2 money actions (an agent_action can open an approval_request when a rule matches its dollar_amount). Delegations (approval_delegations date-ranged rows) may be a follow-up — keep scope to the three chain types.

userStories.title: SLA poller: auto-escalate overdue approvals and stale agent actions
userStories.description: As an operations manager, I need overdue approval requests and expired pending agent actions escalated automatically, so Tier 2 items can't rot in a queue nobody watches.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/sla-poller.ts scheduled via cron-service (15 min interval, gated by AGENTIC_OS_ENABLED): approval_requests past sla_expiry_at with escalation_enabled => status 'escalated', escalation_count incremented, auto_escalated=true, escalate_to_role_id/user_id notified (AOS-014 hook)
agent_actions in 'pending_review' past review_due_at: first breach re-notifies reviewers; second poll past due+24h sets status 'expired' with audit entry (expired actions are NEVER silently executed)
Each escalation writes agent_audit_log ('approval.sla.escalated' / 'agent_action.review.expired')
Poller is idempotent — re-running the same tick escalates each row at most once (guard on escalation_count/last-notified timestamp)
Unit tests for breach detection and idempotency guard
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: sla_expiry_at exists on approval_requests but nothing checks it (explore audit gap #6). Expire-don't-execute is a deliberate safety choice: a stale proposed discount from 3 days ago should die, not fire late.

userStories.title: Escalation + review notifications: in-app, email, websocket
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I need to be notified when an agent action awaits my review, gets approved/rejected, escalates on SLA breach, or a cost quota trips, so the human side of the loop is pulled in rather than expected to poll.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/notifications.ts: notifyAgentEvent(event) fanning out to (a) userNotifications insert (types: 'agent_action_review', 'agent_action_decided', 'agent_escalation', 'agent_quota_warning'), (b) email via the existing email-service provider abstraction, (c) websocket push via webSocketService for real-time badge updates

Reviewer resolution: Tier 2 actions notify users holding the reviewing permission for that agent's domain (fallback: company admins); Tier 3 escalations notify the escalate_to user/role from the matched rule or the tenant's admins
AOS-010 tier-3 hook, AOS-013 SLA breaches, and AOS-004 quota warn threshold all call notifyAgentEvent (replace their no-op hooks)
Notification payload deep-links to /agent-inbox?action=<id>
Unit test for reviewer resolution fallback chain
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: All three channels already exist: userNotifications table + routes-notifications.ts (in-app), server/services/email-service.ts (SendGrid/SES/Resend/simulation), webSocketService (real-time). This story is pure wiring — no new channel infra. SMS/Slack escalation is explicitly out of scope for v1.

userStories.title: Agent Inbox API: list, approve, reject, edit-and-approve (Express + edge fn parity)
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I need API endpoints to see pending agent actions and decide them, available in both dev (Express) and prod (edge function) backends, so the Agent Inbox UI works in every environment.
acceptanceCriteria: server/routes-agent-inbox.ts registered in server/routes.ts: GET /api/agent-inbox (pending_review agent_actions, filters: agent_key, domain, tier, date range; paginated; tenant-scoped via getTenantId), GET /api/agent-inbox/:id (full payload + audit trail by correlation_id), POST /api/agent-inbox/:id/approve, POST /api/agent-inbox/:id/reject { reason required }, POST /api/agent-inbox/:id/edit-approve { patchedInput } (stores reviewer's edited tool_input, then approves)

deno check passes on the new edge function
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: CLAUDE.md hard rule: frontend endpoints must exist on BOTH backends (Express serves dev, prod hits functions.printyx.net directly). Follow the blog-* edge fn auth pattern (createSupabaseClient -> auth.getUser -> permission gate -> service client with tenant filter). 'agent.action.review' permission is seeded in AOS-040 — until then gate on company-admin role level as the blog fns do.

userStories.title: Agent Inbox UI page: review queue with approve/reject/edit
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want an inbox page showing everything agents have proposed, with enough context to decide in seconds — summary, confidence, dollar impact, proposed payload — and one-click approve/reject.
acceptanceCriteria: client/src/pages/AgentInbox.tsx routed at /agent-inbox in App.tsx (lazy import, Wouter route)

List groups pending actions by agent domain with badges for tier, confidence, and dollar_amount when present; TanStack Query with loading/error/empty states; typed useQuery<AgentAction[]> (no untyped data reads)

Detail drawer: summary, proposed tool_input rendered as labeled fields, audit-trail timeline for the correlation_id, Approve / Reject (reason textarea required) / Edit-and-approve (editable form) buttons
Decisions optimistic-update the list and fire the websocket-refreshed unread badge
Sidebar entry in RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx with a pending-count badge
Mobile-responsive (drawer becomes full-screen sheet below md)

userStories.title: Agent feedback capture: rating + correction on decided actions

userStories.title: Prospect: lead triage agent (score, qualify, route inbound leads)

Tier 1 actions: write score + qualification note to the lead record and assign owner via the existing lead-assignment rules (auto-lead-routing-service / lead_assignment_queue path); confidence below policy floor => Tier 2 review with the model's reasoning attached
Batch cap per run (default 25 leads) from agent_policies to bound cost
New write tools registered: update_lead_score, assign_lead_owner (mutates=true, moneyAction=false)

userStories.title: Prospect: outreach draft agent for stale leads

Default flow: every draft is a Tier 2 agent_action ('send_outreach_email' tool, mutates=true) — approve in Agent Inbox sends via email-service and logs the touch on the lead record
Per-tenant policy outreach_auto_send=false; when true AND confidence >= floor, sends are Tier 1 with a daily send cap policy (default 20)
send_outreach_email tool is idempotent on the action's idempotency_key (no double-send on retry)
Drafts never invent facts not present in tool output (prompt constraint + unit test asserting the prompt includes the grounding rule)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: email-autopilot (routes-email-autopilot.ts) already fingerprints user voice for replies but never sends — reuse its draft-style approach where sensible. Outbound sending = the classic trust-ramp agent: ship review-first, earn auto-send. Suppress leads with unsubscribe/do-not-contact markers if such a field exists on business_records — check before sending.

userStories.title: Nurture: stalled-deal agent creating next-best-action tasks
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I want deals that stall in a pipeline stage to automatically get a concrete next-best-action task on the owner's plate (Tier 1 — it only creates tasks), so pipeline hygiene runs itself.

Tier 1 action via new create_crm_task tool: creates a task assigned to the deal owner with the suggested action + rationale; duplicate-guard skips deals that already have an open agent-created task
Deals older than policy write_off_suggest_days (default 60 stalled) produce a Tier 2 'suggest_close_lost' action instead (a human decides to kill a deal, never the agent)
Runs land in the ops digest counts (agent_actions rows queryable by agent_key='deal_nurture')
Unit test for stall detection + duplicate-guard
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Task creation is the safest possible write — perfect Tier 1. Check what the canonical CRM task table is before building create_crm_task (there are multiple task-ish tables; server/routes/task-routes.ts is the live path). Suggest-close-lost as Tier 2 keeps humans owning pipeline truth.

userStories.title: Nurture: contract renewal agent generating renewal proposals
userStories.description: As an account manager, I want contracts entering their renewal window to automatically produce a draft renewal proposal for my approval (Tier 2), so renewals start 90 days out instead of being discovered late.

Generates a Tier 2 'create_renewal_proposal' action: draft terms grounded in the current contract + usage; approval creates the renewal_proposals row and logs to renewal_communication_log
Price changes beyond policy renewal_max_auto_uplift_pct (default 0) are flagged in the action summary so the reviewer sees them first

Duplicate-guard on contract id (one open renewal action per contract)

Tier 1 via new tools set_ticket_priority + route_ticket; policy triage_human_categories (default: ['contract_dispute','billing','safety']) forces those categories to Tier 2 regardless of confidence

Audit rows per ticket with correlation_id = ticket id-scoped uuid

userStories.title: Maintain: meter read anomaly agent

userStories.title: Manage: AR collections agent drafting dunning sequences

Hard exclusions in code: accounts with a dispute/hold marker, accounts with a payment recorded since draft time (re-check at execution), one dunning touch per account per policy dunning_min_interval_days (default 7)

Unit tests: bucket assignment, exclusion rules, re-check-at-execution

userStories.title: Manage: billing anomaly agent holding suspect invoices

Unit tests for all three detection rules

userStories.title: Security: sentinel agent detecting auth and data-access anomalies
userStories.description: As a security owner, I want anomalous account behavior — impossible travel, mass data export, off-hours admin changes, permission self-escalation — detected and escalated (Tier 2/3), with only strictly-safe responses automated, so security watch runs 24/7 without a SOC.
acceptanceCriteria: Agent 'security_sentinel' (domain 'security'): scheduled run (15 min) applies deterministic rules over auth/audit event data: new-country login within impossible window, export volume > policy, role/permission changes outside business hours, permission grants where grantor=grantee

Detections create Tier 2 actions (suggested response: force re-login, temp-disable account, revert grant) — a human approves any account-affecting response; severity>=critical ALSO fires an immediate Tier 3 escalation to platform/company admins via AOS-014

The ONLY Tier 1 action permitted: flagging the account record for step-up re-auth on next login IF such a mechanism exists — otherwise no Tier 1 actions at all (auto account-lock is explicitly forbidden in code)
Rules and thresholds live in agent_policies (security_* keys) with documented defaults
False-positive feedback (AOS-017 negative rating) captured per rule for tuning
Unit tests per detection rule with synthetic event fixtures
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Deliberately rule-based (not LLM-judgment) for detections — security responses must be explainable. Investigate what auth/audit event data actually exists (Supabase GoTrue audit, agent_audit_log, any session table) and scope rules to available signals; document unavailable signals in the story notes on completion. Auto-lock is forbidden because a false positive locks out a paying customer.

userStories.title: Security: access review agent (RBAC drift + dormant accounts report)

Each finding becomes a Tier 2 remediation action (deactivate dormant user, suggest role downgrade) — approval executes via new deactivate_user / change_user_role tools; rejection records the exception with a note (auditable accept-risk)
Report itself stored as an agent_action of type 'access_review_report' (acknowledgeable, like Tier 3) with the full findings jsonb
Never touches platform-admin accounts automatically (excluded in code)
Unit test for dormancy + zero-user-role detection
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Two role systems exist (CLAUDE.md gotcha): roles table (frontend) vs enhanced_roles (backend RBAC) — the review must read whichever actually gates access (enhanced-rbac-middleware) and say so in the report. users table has isActive + tenantId (memory notes).

userStories.title: Develop: data hygiene agent (dedupe + normalize business records)

acceptanceCriteria: Agent 'data_hygiene' (domain 'develop'): scheduled run over business_records: (a) safe normalizations — phone/email/state formatting, trims, casing — via normalize_record_fields tool at Tier 1; (b) duplicate candidates (same email domain+name similarity, same phone) as Tier 2 'merge_records' actions with a side-by-side field preview in the payload
Merge execution preserves the older record id, re-points child rows, and stores the losing record snapshot in the action result (undo data)
Normalization is deterministic code (no LLM); duplicate-candidate similarity may use the LLM for the explanation only
Per-run cap policy (default 100 records) and audit rows per changed record

userStories.title: Develop: knowledge agent drafting KB articles from resolved tickets

userStories.title: Quota enforcement wiring: warn alerts, hard stop, monthly reset verification

Cross-tenant test: every registered tool called with ctx tenant A and input referencing tenant B's ids returns empty/not-found (query-level scoping verified per tool)
Findings documented in a SECURITY section of the module docs (AOS-041)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Defensive-security story. The mocked-LLM-echoing-injection technique makes these real regression tests, not vibes. Multi-tenant isolation is THE security invariant of this codebase (CLAUDE.md) — agents are a new query surface and get the same bar.

userStories.title: Fix tenant-resolution middleware ordering fail-open bypass
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need tenant resolution to run AFTER authentication so an authenticated user of tenant A cannot read/write tenant B by sending an x-tenant-id header. Currently resolveTenant is mounted before JWT auth, so req.supabaseUser is unset, header validation fails open, and req.tenantId is set to any attacker-supplied header value.
acceptanceCriteria: Register authenticateSupabaseJWT/session auth BEFORE resolveTenant so user identity is populated when tenant is resolved (server/routes.ts ordering)
validateTenantHeader must FAIL CLOSED when no authenticated userId is present (server/middleware/tenancy.ts:64-67)
Verify the requested x-tenant-id is one the authenticated user is authorized for; reject with 403 otherwise
Add an integration test proving a tenant-A JWT + tenant-B x-tenant-id header is rejected across customers/leads/products/billing/AP/AR routes
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: [SECURITY/CRITICAL] Source: automated code review 2026-07-11 (branch claude/web-app-code-review-y1eqny). Headline cross-tenant exposure. Files: server/routes.ts:103 (resolveTenant mount) vs :150 (auth), server/middleware/tenancy.ts:64-67 (fail-open) & :129-182. All getTenantId() routes affected. [DONE 2026-07-13] Root cause: resolveTenant ran at routes.ts:72 BEFORE session(95)+authenticateSupabaseJWT(119), so req.supabaseUser was unset and it fell through to trusting the x-tenant-id header. Moved the resolveTenant/trackApiCall/blockRegistrations block to AFTER auth + req.user population (before the auth-required gate) so resolveTenant Priority-1 validates the header against the JWT tenant (403 for non-admins, admin bypass preserved). Also made validateTenantHeader FAIL CLOSED when no userId (was returning valid:true+trusting header). Unit test proves tenant-A JWT + tenant-B header -> 403, matching -> resolves, admin -> allowed, unauthenticated+header -> 403 (fail closed). resolveTenant gates ALL /api routes so this covers customers/leads/products/billing/AP/AR. Ratchet 1353.

userStories.description: As a new tenant importing data, I need Execute to actually create records, not report a fake success.

userStories.notes: [FUNCTIONALITY/BLOCKER] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/routes-tenant-onboarding.ts:396 "TODO: Implement actual data import execution" — sets importExecuted:true + importedRows from req.body but writes no rows. Silent data loss during onboarding. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23. ROOT CAUSE: the execute handler flipped importExecuted:true and echoed req.body.rowsToImport as importedRows while inserting NOTHING; worse, the validation record never persisted the parsed CSV rows, so execute had no data to insert even if it wanted to. FIX (3 layers): (1) SCHEMA — added rawRows jsonb to data_import_validations (shared/tenant-onboarding-schema.ts) + migration 0035_pa042_import_raw_rows.sql (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS raw_rows jsonb; journaled idx 18, tag 0035 — clean per check:migrations); importDataWithValidation now stores rawRows: csvData at validate time. (2) EXECUTE ENGINE — rewrote POST /api/tenants/import/:validationId/execute to: load the validation (404 if absent, 409 if already executed), resolve the target from an IMPORT_TARGETS registry, resolve tenantId from validation.tenantId (fallback getTenantId/body), rebuild each row that PASSED validation (errors carry 1-based row numbers -> skip those) by translating columnMappings[*].mappedTo names to real target columns, and INSERT them inside db.transaction so a mid-insert failure rolls the whole import back (AC2). importedRows = real inserted count; failedRows = total - imported; response returns both. (3) TARGET SAFETY — the honest scoping decision: the onboarding auto-mapper (autoMapColumns) only ever produces a company name + contact/address fields, which cleanly satisfies business_records (companyName NOT NULL is mapped; recordType/status default). The other three dataTypes CANNOT be safely inserted from that CSV shape — equipment.customerId (FK) NOT NULL, contracts.customerId/startDate/endDate NOT NULL, inventoryItems.name/category NOT NULL are all absent from the field map — so 'customers' inserts into business_records (recordType='customer', status='active', email->primaryContactEmail, phone->primaryContactPhone, address->addressLine1, zipCode->postalCode) and equipment/contracts/inventory return an explicit 400 UNSUPPORTED_IMPORT_TYPE. This REMOVES the silent data loss for EVERY type: the supported type writes real rows, the unsupported types now fail loudly instead of reporting fake success (was the actual audit defect). TEST: server/tests/unit/tenant-onboarding-import.test.ts (5 tests, supertest over the mounted router, db + auth mocked): valid customers import inserts only the non-error rows with tenant+defaults and reports importedRows=1/failedRows=1; unsupported type -> 400 with no importExecuted; insert failure -> 500 with importExecuted never set (rollback); unknown validation -> 404; already-executed -> 409. VERIFICATION: vitest 5/5; tsc ratchet holds at 1083; lint ratchet DECREASED 11996->11995 (baseline tightened); prettier clean; migration guard's 25 pre-existing SUPA-002 drift files (0008-0028) untouched, 0035 journaled + not flagged. userStories.notes: [DATABASE/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). routes-products-crud.ts:1645/1658 parse insertMeterReadingSchema without createdBy; meter_readings.created_by is NOT NULL -> parse throws -> 500. CLAUDE.md BATCH 8 flagged this as still-open server debt; pattern recurs across schema.ts lines 1394/1815/2021/2218/2281/2566/2700/2807/2871. PROGRESS 2026-07-12: meter-readings POST fixed (createdBy injected at both parse sites); systemic sweep of other NOT-NULL created_by insert-parse sites + integration test still pending a tsc/live-DB environment. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23 — bullet 1 (meter-readings) was already done; this closes the systemic sweep (bullet 2) + adds a regression test (bullet 3). THE AUDIT was done authoritatively, not by the shared-schema heuristic (which had a ~5x false-positive rate from schema/DDL drift): scanned the actual migration DDL for every table with created_by/tenant_id NOT NULL (no default), mapped table -> insertXSchema via createInsertSchema/pgTable, and matched parse sites — CRUCIALLY shorthand-aware (`tenantId,` counts as injected, not just `tenantId:`; missing that inflated a first pass to 62 bogus hits, e.g. routes-tasks.ts which injects via shorthand and works fine). TRUE list: 10 sites. RESOLVED ALL 10: FIXED 8 real bugs — 5 INSERT via `.omit({tenantId[,createdBy]:true})` before parse (routes-knowledge-base.ts:122 category + :395 article [both tenantId+createdBy] + :695 feedback, routes-enhanced-service.ts:157 phone-in-ticket, routes-warehouse-fpy.ts:26 kitting — each injects the field at .values() downstream, so omit is safe); 1 INSERT via INJECT (routes-manufacturer-integration.ts:50 -> `.parse({...req.body, tenantId})` rather than .omit, because createIntegration(tenantId, data) is typed Omit<Insert,"tenantId"> and the Zod-omit inferred type mismatched it — injecting keeps the type aligned and was the +1 tsc regression I caught and fixed); and 2 UPDATE routes via `.partial()` (routes-social-media.ts:263 post + :409 cron-job — these misuse an INSERT schema to validate a PUT, so the full-required-fields parse 500s any partial update; .partial() is the correct update contract, matching the existing knowledge-base category PUT). EXCLUDED 2 with rationale: routes-client-monitoring.ts:538 is a FALSE POSITIVE (tenantId is spread into the `clientData` object BEFORE parse; the audit missed it only because the parse arg is a variable, not a literal); routes-seo-core.ts:57 (seo_settings) is the KNOWN broken settings contract tracked under EDGE-002e (batch 15 — missing NOT NULL siteUrl etc.), a separate story, deliberately not touched here. TEST (bullet 3): server/tests/unit/insert-schema-server-injected.test.ts asserts on the REAL schemas that each base schema required the server field (safeParse({}) reports a tenantId/createdBy issue = the bug) and that `.omit(...)` removes it from both `.shape` and the parse contract — 24 tests, all pass. Chose a schema-level test over a route test because it validates the exact fix on the real schemas with zero db/route mocking (robust, not brittle). userStories.title: Fix generic webhook HMAC verifier computing signature over re-serialized JSON, not raw body
userStories.description: As an integrations owner, I need the generic webhook verifier to validate real provider signatures.
acceptanceCriteria: verifyStripeSignature (and Salesforce/Microsoft paths) hash the raw request buffer, not JSON.stringify(payload); preserve req.rawBody.
Test with a Stripe-format signature fixture that passes only against raw-body HMAC.
userStories.notes: [SECURITY/LOW] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/integrations/webhook-service.ts:230,275 use JSON.stringify(payload); real signatures are over raw bytes so it can never validate. Fails-closed today (rejects all), but is a latent bypass if any caller treats false as "skip". Primary Stripe path (stripe-service.ts) correctly uses constructEvent. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23 — the generic webhook verifier now HMACs over the RAW request bytes, not JSON.stringify(payload). ROOT CAUSE: verifyStripeSignature (webhook-service.ts:279), the Salesforce inline path (:231), and verifyQuickBooksSignature (:327) all hashed JSON.stringify(payload); a real provider signature is over the raw body bytes, whose key order/whitespace/unicode-escaping differ from a re-serialization, so it could never validate (fail-closed, but a latent bypass if any caller read false as "skip"). FIX: threaded an explicit rawBody:string param through processWebhook -> verifyWebhookSignature -> the three verifiers, and HMAC over it (Stripe: `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`; Salesforce/QuickBooks: rawBody). Chose an explicit param over mutating req.rawBody — same effect, no Express-global coupling. ROUTES (webhook-routes.ts): stripe/quickbooks already used express.raw() so req.body is the raw Buffer — now capture rawBody = req.body.toString() and pass it; SWITCHED the salesforce route from express.json() to rawBodyParser (it needs the bytes, which express.json discards) and parse from rawBody; the generic /:provider route passes rawBody too. microsoft-calendar (clientState token) and google-calendar (channel token/id) do NOT HMAC the body, so rawBody is unused there — they pass JSON.stringify(req.body) as a documented placeholder. Also fixed a latent caller bug found on the way: verifyWebhookSignature's quickbooks branch still passed `payload` after the rename — now rawBody. Hardened both non-Stripe comparisons to length-guarded crypto.timingSafeEqual (QuickBooks was a plain === ; Salesforce could throw on a length mismatch). TEST (AC bullet 2): server/tests/unit/webhook-signature.test.ts — a fixture whose raw bytes differ from their re-serialization (RAW_BODY !== JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(RAW_BODY))), asserting for Stripe/Salesforce/QuickBooks that a signature over the RAW body VALIDATES and one over the re-serialized body is REJECTED (the exact case the old JSON.stringify code failed), plus missing-secret / malformed-signature negatives. 7/7 pass. VERIFICATION: vitest 7/7 green; tsc ratchet holds at 1083; lint ratchet DECREASED 12003->12001 (two `payload: any` params became `rawBody: string`) — baseline tightened. Note the primary Stripe path (stripe-service.ts constructEvent) was already correct; this fixes the secondary generic path.

userStories.title: [SECURITY/MEDIUM] Harden root-admin raw SQL executor with a read-only DB role instead of regex parsing
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the root-admin SQL console to be safe by construction rather than by a home-grown keyword/semicolon regex, so that a crafted query using escaped quotes or dollar-quoting cannot slip past the filter.
acceptanceCriteria: server/routes-root-admin.ts (~lines 483-508): run the submitted query inside a read-only transaction (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY) using a dedicated low-privilege DB role with SELECT-only grants
Remove reliance on the .replace(/'[^']*'/g,'') literal-stripping regex as the sole safety gate (it does not handle '' escapes or $$ dollar-quoting)
Add a test that a query with a dollar-quoted or escaped-quote payload cannot execute a second statement or a write
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by security audit 2026-07-14. Defense-in-depth: route is already requireRootAdmin-gated and SELECT-only, so this hardens rather than fixes an external break. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. (1) THE REAL FIX — the console statement now runs inside a transaction with `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, so write capability is removed BY THE ENGINE rather than by text matching: Postgres raises SQLSTATE 25006 ("cannot execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL in a read-only transaction") for anything that slips past the static gate, including payloads nobody thought of. SET LOCAL scopes the settings to the transaction so the pooled connection is unaffected once it returns to the pool. This is the "safe by construction" the story asks for. (2) NEW server/lib/sql-console-guard.ts replaces the `.replace(/'[^']*'/g, '')` literal stripping with a real lexer implementing Postgres's rules for '' escapes, E'' backslash strings, "quoted idents", $$ / $tag$ dollar quoting, -- line comments and NESTED /* */ block comments. The gate (SELECT/WITH-only, single-statement, dangerous-keyword denylist, 1000-row cap) now runs against text that agrees with the server about what is code and what is data. The denylist is deliberately KEPT even though the read-only transaction covers writes, because it also blocks things a read-only transaction happily permits: pg_read_file, pg_sleep, pg_terminate_backend, SET ROLE. (3) TESTS (AC bullet 3): server/tests/unit/sql-console-guard.test.ts, 30 tests, driven by the exact payload classes the AC names — a second statement hidden after a dollar-quoted literal, after an escaped-quote literal, after an E-string, and behind a comment-terminated line; plus every write verb, a write disguised by a leading comment, and the non-write dangers above. Full unit suite green (60 files / 1263 tests); tsc holds at the 1315 baseline. | AN HONEST CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S PREMISE — the old regex was NOT exploitable in the way the description claims ("a crafted query using escaped quotes or dollar-quoting cannot slip past the filter"). I diffed the OLD stripping against the NEW lexer across the named payload classes and every divergence went the SAFE way: the old regex OVER-blocks, it does not under-block. `SELECT $$a;b$$ FROM t` — the old regex never strips dollar quotes, so it sees the data semicolon and REJECTS a legitimate query; `SELECT $x$ DELETE FROM users $x$ FROM t` — it leaves the literal visible so the DENYLIST fires on data; nested block comments likewise. On the escaped-quote cases (SELECT 'a''; SELECT 1; --') the old and new strippers AGREE. I could not construct a payload where the old regex MISSED a real second statement. So this story is genuinely what its own note says — defence-in-depth hardening, not an open hole — and the practical user-visible effect of the lexer is FEWER FALSE REJECTIONS (dollar-quoted and nested-comment queries now work). The security value comes from the read-only transaction, and from no longer depending on a parser that disagrees with Postgres about what a string is — which is worth doing precisely because "it happens to fail safe today" is not a property anyone should be relying on. | NOT DONE — the AC's "dedicated low-privilege DB role with SELECT-only grants" is an OPS change, not a code change: it needs a role created in Postgres (CREATE ROLE ... ; GRANT SELECT ...) and a SECOND connection string for the app to use for this endpoint (e.g. READONLY_DATABASE_URL), plus pool wiring. That cannot be done from here — the DB is unreachable (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials) and the role/grants live in the target environment, not the repo. The read-only TRANSACTION delivers the same protection against WRITES with no infra change, so the remaining gap the dedicated role would close is READ SCOPE: the console still connects as the app role, so any SELECT can read across tenants and bypass RLS. That residual is documented in the route header as a TODO(prod) and is unchanged by this story. Worth a follow-up if cross-tenant read via the console is considered unacceptable.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Eliminate the edge-router per-response double JSON parse + recursive date walk
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the edge dispatcher to stop buffering, JSON.parsing, recursively walking, and re-stringifying every response body, so that the platform-wide CPU/memory tax on 100% of prod JSON traffic is removed and large list responses stop paying an O(payload)-twice cost.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/server.ts (lines 172-182 + recursive walker 19-38): stop unconditionally doing const body = await response.json(); normalizeDates(body); re-stringify on every response
Gate date normalization to only the callers that need it (e.g. iOS User-Agent/header), or move it into the specific handlers/PostgREST that emit PG timestamps
At minimum, skip normalization for bodies over a size threshold and add a cheap length/charAt prefilter before running PG_TIMESTAMP_RE.test on every string value
Verify streaming responses are no longer buffered by the router
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Highest-leverage single change: every prod response currently pays this. Confirm no handler depends on the router mutating its dates before changing the default. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. CRITICAL FINDING FIRST — AC BULLET 2 ("gate date normalization to only the callers that need it, e.g. iOS User-Agent/header") MUST NOT BE IMPLEMENTED. It would be a silent, platform-wide DATA CORRECTNESS regression. Reason: NOTHING in shared/schema.ts uses withTimezone — all 432 timestamp columns are `timestamp WITHOUT time zone`, so PostgREST emits NAIVE strings ("2024-01-15T10:30:00.123456"). JavaScript parses a naive timestamp as LOCAL time, so new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00") in a browser at UTC-5 is SIX HOURS off. The Z this router appends is exactly what makes the WEB frontend render correct times — it is a correctness dependency of every browser client, not an iOS convenience, despite the comment naming iOS. Gating it behind an iOS User-Agent would shift every timestamp for every web user by their UTC offset, with no error and no test failure. This is precisely what the story's own note asked to confirm ("Confirm no handler depends on the router mutating its dates before changing the default") — the answer is that the entire web client does. So normalization stays UNIVERSAL and was made CHEAP instead, which achieves the story's actual goal (remove the CPU/memory tax) without the regression. WHAT CHANGED: the old path ran JSON.parse -> a recursive walk that REBUILT every object/array -> JSON.stringify, on 100% of JSON responses (3 full passes + a complete object-graph allocation). Replaced with (a) a single regex pass over the RAW TEXT — no parse, no rebuild, no re-stringify — matching only quoted JSON tokens that are exactly a PG timestamp, (b) a Date-free fast path: for naive/+00:00/-00:00 (the overwhelming majority) the result is just ts.slice(0,19)+'Z', so no Date object is constructed at all; only a genuine non-zero UTC offset takes the Date path, (c) a cheap prefilter (text.indexOf('T') === -1 -> skip the scan entirely, which covers date-free payloads). MEASURED on a real 934KB list response: 23.91ms -> 7.50ms per response = 3.2x, on 100% of prod JSON traffic. EQUIVALENCE PROOF (this is a hot, subtle path, so it was verified not argued): a harness EXTRACTED both implementations from source — the new one from the patched file, the old one from `git show HEAD` — so neither was retyped by hand, then fuzzed 80,000 randomly generated timestamps (all fraction widths 0-6 digits, and zones '', Z, +00:00, -00:00, +05:30, -05:00, +14:00, -11:00, +09:45) => 0 mismatches, plus 8 whole-document shapes (single row, 200-row list, bare array, nested, empty object/array, unicode+escapes, no-dates) => all byte-identical. TWO SUBTLETIES DELIBERATELY PRESERVED, both verified by the fuzz: (i) a value already ending in Z is returned UNTOUCHED — the old code appended a SECOND Z, got an Invalid Date and fell through to the original string, so "...T10:30:00.123Z" keeps its fractional seconds. That is arguably a latent bug for iOS ISO8601DateFormatter, but it is EXISTING behavior and out of scope to change here; flagged for a follow-up. (ii) object KEYS are never rewritten — the recursive version only normalized values, so the text pass checks whether the next non-space char after the token is ':' and skips it. Without that guard a timestamp-shaped key would have been silently rewritten. BONUS BUG FIXED: the old code did `await response.json()` inside a try, and on parse failure fell through to `return new Response(response.body)` — but .json() had ALREADY consumed the body, so the "pass through the original response" fallback itself threw. Now the body is read once via .text() and reused, so the fallback is real. Also drops a stale content-length header (timestamp rewriting changes byte length). STREAMING (AC bullet 4): only application/json is buffered, which is unavoidable if the bytes must be rewritten. Everything else — text/event-stream (SSE), PDFs, octet-stream — still streams straight through via `new Response(response.body)` and is not buffered. That was already true and is preserved. deno check: identical error profile before/after (2 TS18046 + 1 TS2307 + 1 TS2345, all pre-existing); tsc unaffected (supabase/ is outside tsconfig include). Removed the now-orphaned PG_TIMESTAMP_RE constant. | FOLLOW-UPS: (a) The Z-ending-keeps-fraction quirk above means iOS may still receive "...T10:30:00.123Z" from any handler that emits an already-Z-suffixed timestamp; if iOS decode failures are ever reported, that is the first place to look — the fix is one line in normalizeTimestamp, but it is a behavior change and wants its own story + iOS verification. (b) The REAL structural fix is upstream: make the 432 timestamp columns `withTimezone: true` (or have handlers emit ISO-8601 UTC), after which this router pass could be deleted outright rather than optimized. That is a migration, not a router change. (c) If a size ceiling is ever wanted (AC bullet 3), the natural knob is now a single early return in normalizeDatesInJsonText — but note that skipping normalization on large bodies would reintroduce the timezone bug selectively for big lists, which is worse than the cost; the text pass is cheap enough that a threshold is not needed.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Cut two serialized auth round-trips per request (local JWT verify + role cache)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need edge functions to avoid an HTTP round-trip to GoTrue (auth.getUser) plus a second role-lookup query on every request, so that per-request latency across the whole platform drops.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify the JWT signature locally in supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts (jose + GoTrue JWKS/secret) using claims already in the token, instead of calling supabase.auth.getUser(jwt) on every request; OR cache getUser results by token-hash with a short TTL

For functions that additionally query users->roles for gating (e.g. platform-analytics/index.ts:70-86, platform-cs/index.ts:32-43, deployment-readiness/index.ts:53-57), cache the role row by token-hash/user-id with a short TTL
Confirm platform-admin / role-level gates still hold after the change (add/keep a test)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Two serialized network hops on every prod request in ~212 functions. Local verification must still honor token revocation expectations — document the TTL tradeoff. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. KEY MEASUREMENT FIRST — the AC pointed at _shared/auth.ts, but that is NOT where the tax lives: only 52 of the 255 function dirs import _shared/auth.ts, while 214 call supabase.auth.getUser(jwt) DIRECTLY (that is the story's "~212 functions"). Fixing only requireAuth would have optimized the minority path and left the real cost untouched. The choke point is _shared/supabase.ts createSupabaseClient(req) — the shared factory all 214 already go through — so the cache is installed THERE and every one of them benefits with ZERO call-site edits. CHOSE CACHING OVER LOCAL JWT VERIFY (the AC offered either). Local jose/JWKS verification would remove the hop but CANNOT see a revoked or signed-out session at all, so a stolen token stays valid for its whole lifetime; it also puts hand-rolled crypto in front of ~212 functions. Caching keeps GoTrue as the source of truth and bounds staleness to a short TTL — strictly safer for the same win on repeat traffic. WHAT LANDED: (1) NEW supabase/functions/_shared/auth-cache.ts — a token-hash-keyed TTL cache for getUser plus cachedRoleLookup for the second hop. Deliberately import-clean (no supabase-js, no Deno APIs at module scope) so it is unit-testable under the repo vitest runner. (2) _shared/supabase.ts wraps the returned client so getUser(jwt) is cached for all 214 direct callers; a NO-ARGUMENT getUser() is passed straight through UNCACHED, because it resolves against the client's own session/header state which we are not keying on — caching it could return the wrong user. (3) _shared/auth.ts requireAuth routed through the same cache (the other 52). (4) The second serialized hop: the users->roles gate is cached by user id in ALL SEVEN functions that run it (database-updater, platform-activities, platform-analytics, platform-crm, platform-cs, platform-deals, root-admin) — the AC named only three; the query is byte-identical in all seven. deployment-readiness (also named) does NOT do a role query, only getUser, so it is already covered by the factory wrap. TRADEOFF, per the story note: a revoked token keeps working for up to AUTH_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 30s), and a role change lands within ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 30s). Both are env-tunable and both accept 0 as a full kill switch (no redeploy needed, TTL is read at call time). The cache is per-isolate, so a restart clears it. TESTS (AC bullet 3): new server/tests/unit/auth-cache.test.ts, 17 tests. This sits in front of authentication for ~212 functions, so the four safety invariants are PINNED rather than assumed: (1) errors are NEVER cached — a failure cannot be replayed and a transient GoTrue blip cannot lock a user out (both tested); (2) a cache entry never outlives the token — TTL is capped at the JWT exp, so a token expiring in 5s under a 30s TTL is re-verified rather than served stale (this one would be an auth bypass if wrong); (3) keys are SHA-256 hashes, not raw bearer tokens; (4) the cache is bounded. Gate behavior is pinned too: role rows key by user id, and a low-privilege user still gets level 1 on a cache hit even when an admin row is cached (no cross-contamination), a null role row is never cached (a missing role re-checks instead of pinning a user in or out), and a role change is picked up after the TTL. VERIFICATION: deno check clean (0 errors) on all 10 touched edge files; full unit suite green (58 files / 1220 tests); tsc holds at the 1335 baseline. | TWO TYPE GOTCHAS worth remembering for anyone touching this: (a) `T extends ReturnType<typeof createClient>` does NOT work as a constraint — with no type args that resolves to SupabaseClient<unknown, never, GenericSchema> and the real client is not assignable to it (TS2345 "public is not assignable to never"). Constrain structurally instead (`T extends { auth: unknown }`). (b) cachedRoleLookup takes `() => T | PromiseLike<T>`, NOT `() => Promise<T>`: supabase's PostgrestBuilder is a THENABLE, not a real Promise (no .catch/.finally), so a Promise-typed callback rejects a bare `admin.from(...).single()` and breaks T inference at every call site (TS2739 + TS2339 on .data). | FOLLOW-UPS / NOT DONE: (i) createSupabaseClient(req) still builds a NEW supabase client per request (an allocation per call, on top of the hop this story removed). Reusing one anon client and passing the jwt explicitly would cut that too, but it changes the shape of a factory 214 files depend on — separate story. (ii) The 214 direct auth.getUser callers are still an architectural smell: they each re-implement auth+tenant resolution rather than using requireAuth, which is why the tenant-resolution fallbacks in _shared/auth.ts do not protect them. Migrating them onto requireAuth would be the real consolidation (and would make this cache redundant at the call sites). (iii) No integration test exercises a REAL platform-admin gate end-to-end — the edge functions are Deno and the repo runner is node/vitest, so the gate logic is pinned at the cache layer only. A deno-test harness for the edge functions is a genuine gap worth its own story.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Replace full-table scans with SQL aggregates + pagination in analytics, billing, AP/AR
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need dashboard and ledger endpoints to compute counts/sums in Postgres and paginate list results, so that they stop fetching entire tables into JS (which also silently truncates at PostgREST's 1000-row cap and produces wrong numbers as data grows).
acceptanceCriteria: platform-analytics/index.ts: replace select('*') + JS reduce/filter (helpers ~100-114 used at 121-129, 441, 537-543, 627-633, 685-688, 761-763) with { count: 'exact', head: true } for counts, narrowed selects for sums, or a Postgres RPC/view; run the independent fetches in revenue-metrics (121-129) and churn-analysis (737-763) via Promise.all
billing/index.ts (141-186): compute revenue/outstanding/overdue/MRR via SQL aggregates/RPC instead of loading every invoice row for the tenant

account-payable/index.ts (132-141) and account-receivable/index.ts (150-160): add .range() pagination (frontend already handles { data, total }); compute /summary buckets with filtered aggregate queries instead of fetching all rows
platform-cs/index.ts (75-82) and platform-analytics health-trends (627-657): average overall_score with a SQL avg() rather than fetching every health-score row
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. These are the biggest data-volume time bombs as tenants grow, and the 1000-row cap makes the metrics wrong (not just slow). platform-cs already does head-count Promise.all correctly — mirror that pattern. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. HOW THE APPROACH WAS CHOSEN (not guessed): the AC offers "count/head, narrowed selects for sums, or a Postgres RPC/view". Checked what is actually PROVEN in this codebase before picking: `{ count: exact, head: true }` is used in 51 files; `.rpc()` in 11 files with SQL functions living in drizzle/functions/*.sql (a documented convention — idempotent CREATE OR REPLACE, applied out of band via \i, SECURITY INVOKER, tenant-scoped by explicit parameter, deliberately kept OUT of drizzle/migrations per that dir's README). PostgREST aggregate selects (.sum()/.avg()) have ZERO usage anywhere, so that feature is unproven here and was NOT used. THE REAL BUG IS CORRECTNESS, NOT SPEED — worth restating because it drove every decision: PostgREST silently caps a response at db-max-rows (1000 by default) and does NOT error. So every one of these "SELECT * then reduce in JS" sites produced WRONG MONEY NUMBERS for any tenant past 1000 rows (revenue, outstanding, MRR/ARR, AP/AR aging buckets) — quietly under-reported, with no failure to notice. Narrowing a select does not fix that; only aggregating in SQL or paging explicitly does. | WHAT LANDED: (1) NEW drizzle/functions/billing-aggregates.sql — ap_aging_summary(tenant), ar_aging_summary(tenant), billing_analytics(tenant), using SUM(...) FILTER (WHERE ...) so each bucket is one pass. The bucket boundaries reproduce the JS they replace EXACTLY (AP: due<now -> overdue, <=now+7d -> dueThisWeek, else current; AR: days past due <=0/30/60/90/90+), so applying it must not move any number. README.md updated with the file + its consumers, per that directory's convention. (2) billing/index.ts /analytics, account-payable /summary and account-receivable /summary now call the RPC and FALL BACK to the existing JS scan when it is missing — drizzle/functions is applied OUT OF BAND, so the code can legitimately deploy before the SQL exists; a missing function must not 500 the page. (3) AP + AR list endpoints now .range() paginate via a new shared readRange() helper in _shared/http.ts (there was no pagination helper; now both AP/AR share one). Their `total` already came from an exact count, so the frontend's { data, total } contract is unchanged. (4) platform-analytics revenue-metrics: churnedTenants and newCustomers were full row fetches used ONLY for `.length` -> now { count: exact, head: true } DB counts; activeTenants still needs values but the select is narrowed to just current_mrr; all three now run via Promise.all instead of serialized. Added countRecords() + fetchAllRows() helpers (fetchAllRows pages explicitly so a sum is correct at any size). (5) platform-cs health average: was a plain select of every overall_score, so past 1000 rows it averaged an ARBITRARY SUBSET. Now paged. Its counts were already correct head:true + Promise.all (as the AC noted) and were left alone. VERIFICATION: deno check clean (0 errors) on all 5 touched edge functions; tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | IMPORTANT CAVEATS / NOT DONE — read before closing this out: (a) THE SQL IS NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE. The pooler rejects the checked-in credentials ("Tenant or user not found" — the CLAUDE.md note that the committed keys are rotated/stale), so billing-aggregates.sql has never been executed. It must be applied (\i drizzle/functions/billing-aggregates.sql) and SPOT-CHECKED against the JS fallback on a real tenant before being trusted — compare /billing/analytics and both /summary endpoints with the RPC present vs absent and confirm the numbers match. The fallback means a MISSING function is safe; it does NOT protect against WRONG SQL. (b) A PRE-EXISTING ODDITY PRESERVED DELIBERATELY: billing analytics reports averageInvoiceAmount = totalRevenue / totalInvoices, i.e. PAID revenue divided by ALL invoices (not paid-over-paid, and not total-over-total). That is almost certainly a bug, but changing it would silently move a number the story did not ask about; it is reproduced exactly and flagged here (billing_analytics also returns paidCount so a future fix has what it needs). (c) platform-analytics still has other select(*) + JS-reduce sites the AC lists (441, 537-543, 627-657, 685-688, 761-763 in the original numbering) plus the churn-analysis Promise.all — revenue-metrics was done as the pattern and the helpers (countRecords/fetchAllRows) are now in place for the rest, but they are NOT all converted. fetchDeals is also still an unpaged select(*). Worth a follow-up pass; the mechanical part is done. (d) fetchAllRows pages in the client, which is correct but still transfers every row — it fixes the WRONG-NUMBER bug, not the transfer cost. The full fix for the platform_* sums is an RPC like the billing one.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Fix backend N+1 query fan-out across dashboards and list endpoints
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need list/dashboard endpoints to batch their per-row lookups into single grouped/IN queries, so that response time stops scaling linearly with fleet/team/pipeline size and the connection pool stops being hammered.
acceptanceCriteria: server/routes-remote-monitoring.ts (29-52, 450): replace 2-queries-per-device with one DISTINCT ON (device_id) latest-metrics query + one grouped 24h aggregate via inArray(deviceId, ids)
server/routes-technician-management.ts (92-118): replace 2 count queries per technician with a single GROUP BY technicianId using count(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)
server/routes-root-admin.ts (317-333, and enrich loops at 165/398/608/741): select roles.name/level and tenants.name in the existing joined base query and delete the per-row enrichment lookups
server/routes-service-dispatch.ts (699-729): collect all part numbers and do one inArray(partNumber, all) query for batch-check-parts
server/routes-address-books.ts (218-227): replace per-book count with one GROUP BY bookId over inArray(bookId, ...)
