userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Fix N+1 writes and loop-invariant re-fetches in invoice/meter billing generation
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need billing runs to bulk-insert invoices and hoist loop-invariant reads, so that a run over hundreds of meter readings does not take minutes and does not re-read/re-write the same customer balance N times (a race hazard).
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/billing/handlers/generate-invoices.ts (152-173): replace per-reading insert(...).single() + meter_readings.update(...) inside the for loop with a bulk insert([...]) and a batched update per invoice-id group (or an RPC)

server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts (2154-2224): hoist getContractTieredRatesByContract and the customer fetch out of the loop (they are loop-invariant for a contract), batch-insert invoices, and apply one summed balance update instead of N sequential updates
Confirm produced invoice amounts/totals are unchanged by the batching (test against a known set of readings)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. The reads are already batched in generate-invoices.ts (60-88); only the writes are N+1. The mobile path does 5 sequential queries per reading incl. an invariant tieredRates re-fetch. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. EDGE PATH (supabase/functions/billing/handlers/generate-invoices.ts): the reads were already batched; the WRITES were the N+1 — an insert(...).single() PLUS a meter_readings update per reading, i.e. 2N serialized round-trips. Split the pipeline into a PURE prepareInvoiceRows() (no I/O — this is what makes the billing math testable, which AC bullet 3 demands) and an I/O half that does ONE bulk insert for the whole batch, then marks the readings processed with bounded concurrency (chunks of 25) instead of strictly one-at-a-time: 2N serialized becomes 1 + ceil(N/25) waves. WHY NOT A SINGLE UPDATE: each reading needs a DIFFERENT invoice_id/billing_amount, so it cannot collapse into one UPDATE. A PostgREST upsert of the full rows WOULD be one statement, but it rewrites every column from values read earlier and would clobber any concurrent change — rejected deliberately in favour of chunked concurrency. RESILIENCE PRESERVED: a bulk insert is all-or-nothing, so one bad row would fail the ENTIRE run — strictly worse than the old per-row behaviour, which failed only that reading and kept going. The bulk path therefore FALLS BACK to per-row inserts on error, keeping the old per-reading fault isolation while the fast path stays the norm. Inserted invoices are mapped back to their readings by invoice_number (unique within the batch by construction) rather than by array position, so nothing depends on the driver preserving input order. MOBILE PATH (server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts POST /api/contracts/:contractId/process-meter-billing): hoisted getContractTieredRatesByContract OUT of the loop (contractId is fixed for the whole endpoint — it was N identical queries returning identical rows) and hoisted the customer fetch out too. The balance is now summed locally and applied as ONE update after the loop instead of N read-modify-write cycles on the same row — that was the race hazard called out in the description: any concurrent balance write landing between a read and its write was silently lost. Final state is identical (starting balance + sum of every invoice). VERIFICATION: new server/tests/unit/generate-invoices.test.ts (13 tests) asserting amounts are unchanged by the batching, with every expected number COMPUTED BY HAND from the tiered-rate rules rather than snapshotted from the implementation (a snapshot would happily lock in a wrong number): flat-rate 1000*0.01 + 500*0.08 + 100 base = 150; tiered banding 500@0.02 + 500@0.01 + 100 base = 115; a 3-reading batch grand total of 390 matching the old per-row accumulator; zero-copy readings still billing the base; and the skip semantics (no contract_id / contract missing from the map are skipped silently and NOT marked failed, exactly as the original loop did). tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; deno check clean; full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE DOING THIS (neither is in the AC): (1) SEVERE — server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts built its invoice number with a template literal that was BROKEN BY A LINE BREAK between the dollar sign and the opening brace, so the Date.now() placeholder NEVER INTERPOLATED. Every invoice from that endpoint got the same literal string ("INV-<contractNumber>-$" + newline + the raw placeholder text). invoice_number is UNIQUE, so the FIRST reading inserted fine and the SECOND always violated the constraint and 500'd the endpoint — meaning this path could never bill more than one reading per contract, and nobody noticed because the perf problem it was filed under masked it. Fixed to a real interpolation plus a trailing index for intra-run uniqueness. (2) The edge path built `INV-${Date.now()}-${random}` per row. Under a BULK insert every row is written in the SAME millisecond, so Date.now() is identical across the batch and uniqueness rested entirely on a 5-char random suffix — one collision would fail the whole batch. The row index is now part of the number, making intra-batch uniqueness structural rather than probabilistic. A test generates 200 rows under one frozen clock and asserts all 200 numbers are distinct. | FOLLOW-UPS (found, deliberately NOT changed — this is a perf story and these are behaviour changes): (i) In the mobile path, lastMeterReadingDate ends up as the OLDEST processed reading, not the newest: readings are ordered by readingDate DESC and the old loop overwrote the field on every iteration, so the LAST one written is the last element = the oldest. The batched version reproduces that exactly (deliberately), but it looks like a latent bug worth its own story — a field named lastMeterReadingDate almost certainly wants MAX(readingDate). (ii) Neither billing path is transactional: invoices can be inserted and then a meter_readings update can fail, leaving a reading pending against an already-issued invoice (double-billing on the next run). The old code had the same hole; batching does not widen it, but an RPC/transaction is the real fix. (iii) The mobile path still does one createInvoice + one updateMeterReading per reading (2N); it uses the storage layer rather than a raw client, so a bulk insert there needs a new storage method — worth doing, but larger than this story.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Add missing indexes on 10 hot tables (tenant/status/created_at + FK columns)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need composite indexes on the hottest multi-tenant tables, so that the most common list/join/aggregate queries stop doing sequential scans that get slower with every row added.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Drizzle index blocks + a generated migration for: proposal_line_items (proposal_id, line_number) and (tenant_id); proposals (tenant_id, proposal_type, status) and (tenant_id, created_at DESC); audit_logs (tenant_id, timestamp DESC) and (tenant_id, resource, resource_id); invoices (tenant_id, invoice_status), (tenant_id, customer_id), (external_customer_id); equipment (tenant_id, customer_id) and (tenant_id, equipment_status); contracts (tenant_id, customer_id) and (tenant_id, status)

Also index: accounts_payable (tenant_id, status, due_date); accounts_receivable (tenant_id, status, due_date); business_record_activities (business_record_id, created_at DESC) and (tenant_id); users (tenant_id); inventory_items (tenant_id)

Verify against the live DB with pg_indexes which of these already exist before generating the migration (journal reportedly stops at 0009 — but the schema files define NO indexes for these 10 tables, so new index blocks are required, not just applying pending migrations)
npm run db:generate produces the migration SQL; review it; do not db:push to production
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance/index audit 2026-07-14. business_records, service_tickets, meter_readings, signature_requests, blog_audit_log ARE already indexed (baseline 0000) — do not duplicate. proposals is the live quotes table (proposal_type='quote'); its only index today is proposals_share_token_key (pending migration 0017). | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. THE AC'S CENTRAL CLAIM WAS FALSE. It states "the schema files define NO indexes for these 10 tables, so new index blocks are required" — in fact 6 of the 11 named tables were ALREADY indexed by the earlier CR-028 and PA-026 stories (whose migrations are literally 0010_cr028_perf_indexes.sql / 0011_pa026_perf_indexes.sql). Blindly following the AC would have created DUPLICATE indexes, which cost write amplification for zero read benefit. Verified per-table by paren-matching each pgTable block (a regex bleeds across adjacent table blocks and gave plainly wrong answers — e.g. reporting purchase_orders_* indexes under accounts_payable). ALREADY COVERED, deliberately NOT touched: equipment (tenant_id,customer_id)+(tenant_id,equipment_status) and contracts (tenant_id,customer_id)+(tenant_id,status) are complete; invoices already had (tenant_id,invoice_status) and (tenant_id,customer_id); proposals already had (tenant_id,created_at); proposal_line_items already had (tenant_id). inventory_items (tenant_id) is ALREADY SERVED by the existing (tenant_id,category) index via the leftmost-prefix rule — adding a bare (tenant_id) index there would be pure redundancy, so it was not added. ADDED — 10 genuinely missing indexes, in shared/schema.ts + shared/security-schema.ts AND in a hand-authored migration: proposals (tenant_id,proposal_type,status) [proposals is the live quotes table and callers filter by type BEFORE status, which the existing (tenant_id,status) cannot serve — different leftmost prefix, so not redundant]; proposal_line_items (proposal_id,line_number) [QUOTE-020 makes line_number the ordering source of truth and every read path orders by it]; invoices (external_customer_id) [doubles as the service-ticket ref and backs the ?ticketId= filter, queried WITHOUT a tenant prefix]; audit_logs (tenant_id,timestamp) + (tenant_id,resource, resource_id) [this table had ZERO indexes despite being append-heavy — the single worst case found]; accounts_payable and accounts_receivable (tenant_id,status,due_date) [AP/AR aging]; business_record_activities (business_record_id,created_at) + (tenant_id); users (tenant_id). ONE INDEX DROPPED: proposal_line_items_proposal_idx (proposal_id) is fully covered by the new (proposal_id,line_number) via leftmost prefix, so it is replaced rather than left alongside it as a redundant write cost. audit_logs also needed `index` added to its drizzle-orm/pg-core import (security-schema.ts imported none, since the table previously had no indexes). SORT DIRECTION: the AC asks for DESC on created_at/timestamp. Used plain btree (ASC) deliberately — PostgreSQL scans a btree BACKWARDS at the same cost, so DESC only matters for MIXED-direction multi-column sorts, which none of these queries do. It also matches the existing *_created_idx convention from CR-028/PA-026. VERIFICATION: the DB is unreachable from here (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials with "Tenant or user not found" — consistent with the CLAUDE.md note that the committed keys are rotated/stale), so the AC's pg_indexes check could NOT be performed and is left for whoever applies this. Instead the migration was cross-checked against Drizzle's own getTableConfig(): every CREATE INDEX names a real table and real PHYSICAL column names, every index is declared in the schema, the DROPped one is gone from the schema too, and all 10 appear in both schema and migration. tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; full unit suite green (58 files / 1220 tests). | MAJOR INFRASTRUCTURE FINDING — `npm run db:generate` IS UNUSABLE IN THIS REPO, and AC bullet 4 ("npm run db:generate produces the migration SQL") CANNOT be followed. Drizzle's snapshots stop at 0009 while migration SQL files on disk run to 0028, so generate diffs the current schema against a 20-migration-old snapshot. Running it produced a 2,241-line migration containing 114 CREATE TABLE + 275 CREATE INDEX (i.e. it tried to recreate the whole database) and numbered it 0012_furry_vector — COLLIDING with the existing 0012_auto_orders.sql. That output was discarded and the journal reverted; the migration here is hand-authored instead, following the exact precedent of 0010_cr028_perf_indexes / 0011_pa026_perf_indexes (hand-written SQL + a journal entry, no snapshot), with IF NOT EXISTS so it is safe to (re)apply against the db:push-managed database. WORSE — A JOURNAL GAP THAT LIKELY MEANS 17 MIGRATIONS NEVER RAN: server/lib/migrate.ts:161 uses drizzle-orm's migrate(), which reads meta/_journal.json to decide what to apply. The journal contains ONLY 0000-0011. Migrations 0012 through 0028 exist as .sql files but are ABSENT from the journal, so `npm run db:migrate` does not — and never did — apply them. They were presumably applied by hand or via db:push, or not at all. This is worth its own story: either backfill the journal for 0012-0028 (after confirming against __drizzle_migrations what is actually applied) or rebaseline. THIS MATTERED HERE: a migration file alone would have been dead code, so 0029 was added to the journal (idx 12, tag 0029_audit009_perf_indexes) so db:migrate will actually apply it. NOTE the deliberate idx/filename mismatch: the filename continues the DISK sequence (0029) to avoid colliding with 0012_auto_orders.sql, while idx continues the JOURNAL sequence (12). Every journal entry was verified to resolve to a real .sql file. | NOT DONE / NEXT STEPS: (i) The migration has NOT been applied — per the AC and CLAUDE.md, never db:push to production; run `npm run db:migrate` (it acquires __migration_lock). (ii) Before applying, run the AC's pg_indexes check against the live DB to confirm none of these 10 already exist there under a different name — IF NOT EXISTS makes a duplicate name a no-op, but an equivalent index under a DIFFERENT name would go undetected and be created twice. (iii) Consider CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for the large hot tables (invoices, audit_logs, business_record_activities) if these are built against a live production database — a plain CREATE INDEX takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and will block writes for the duration. CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction, so it does not fit drizzle's transactional migrator and would need to be applied out-of-band; left as a plain CREATE INDEX here to match the 0010/0011 precedent, but this is a real operational consideration on a big table.

userStories.title: [PERF/MEDIUM] Remove RBAC middleware write-on-read and upsert the permission cache
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the permission cache to not issue a blocking UPDATE on the hottest request path and to stop inserting duplicate rows, so that authorized requests don't pay a write and permission_cache doesn't bloat until cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: server/middleware/enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts (~134): make the cacheHits increment fire-and-forget (or drop it) instead of awaiting a db.update on every L2 cache hit
setCachedPermissions (~164): upsert on (userId, orgContext, tenantId) instead of always INSERTing a new row
Confirm permission decisions are unchanged (existing L1/L2 cache behavior preserved)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Otherwise the middleware is well-cached (L1 memory + L2 table); this is the one hot-path write. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. (1) WRITE-ON-READ REMOVED: getCachedPermissions AWAITED a db.update bumping cacheHits on every L2 hit — i.e. the hot path for every authorized request blocked on a DB WRITE before proceeding. It is telemetry, not a permission decision, so it is now fire-and-forget. Used a TWO-ARG .then(onOk, onErr) rather than .catch(): drizzle query builders are thenables, and this guarantees the rejection is handled — an unhandled rejection would take the process down under Node's default policy. A failed counter update can now never fail an otherwise-valid authorization. (2) UPSERT: setCachedPermissions always INSERTed, so every cache miss / expiry / invalidation left ANOTHER row for the same (user, context, tenant) — the table grew until the periodic cleanup ran, AND the L2 read (.limit(1) over a NON-unique index) could return any one of the duplicates, which is arguably worse than the bloat. Now onConflictDoUpdate on the triple: exactly one live row per cache key. cacheHits resets to 0 on refresh because the counter tracks hits against THAT cached value. (3) PERMISSION DECISIONS UNCHANGED (AC bullet 3): L1 memory cache untouched; the L2 read path, its TTL predicate (expires_at > NOW()) and the returned Set are byte-for-byte the same. The only behavioural deltas are that the hit counter is now eventually-consistent instead of synchronous, and that a refresh updates a row instead of inserting a rival one. tsc holds at the 1315 baseline (enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts still shows its 8 PRE-EXISTING errors — verified identical count at HEAD, none are mine); full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | THE AC MISSED A BLOCKER — THE UPSERT COULD NOT WORK AS SPECIFIED WITHOUT SCHEMA + DATA WORK: permission_cache had NO unique constraint on (user_id, organizational_context, tenant_id) — only a PLAIN idx_permission_cache_user_context (which also omits tenant_id). ON CONFLICT cannot target a non-unique index, so a bare onConflictDoUpdate would have thrown "no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification" at runtime on the RBAC hot path — i.e. it would have broken authorization for every user. So: added uniqueIndex permission_cache_user_context_tenant_uniq to server/enhanced-rbac-schema.ts (note this table is defined under server/, not shared/ — shared/schema.ts merely RE-EXPORTS it from '../server/enhanced-rbac-schema', which is why grepping shared/ for 'permission_cache' finds nothing) and', hand-authored drizzle/migrations/0030_audit010_permission_cache_uniq.sql, journalled as idx 13 so db:migrate will actually apply it (per the AUDIT-009 finding that drizzle-kit generate is unusable here and that unjournalled migrations never run). THE MIGRATION DELETES BEFORE IT CONSTRAINS, deliberately: because the setter has always INSERTed, this table almost certainly CONTAINS DUPLICATES right now, and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX would simply fail against them ("key is duplicated"). A blank DELETE is the right move rather than a keep-the-newest DISTINCT ON dedupe: permission_cache is a PURE CACHE, every row is derived data regenerated by setCachedPermissions on the next miss, so emptying it costs one recomputation per active user and cannot lose information. Simpler and safer than picking a winner. Verified the migration against drizzle getTableConfig(): real table, real physical columns (user_id, organizational_context, tenant_id), and the index is declared UNIQUE in the schema — the DB itself is unreachable from here (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials), so this static cross-check stands in for running it. | FOLLOW-UPS: (i) NOT APPLIED — run `npm run db:migrate` (never db:push to production, per CLAUDE.md). Until it is applied the new onConflictDoUpdate WILL throw on the auth path, so this migration and the code MUST ship together; this is the one story in this batch where deploy order matters. (ii) idx_permission_cache_user_context is now redundant — the new unique index shares its leftmost prefix — but it was left in place rather than dropped in the same change; worth removing later to save write cost. (iii) The periodic cleanup of expired rows becomes much less important now that refreshes update in place rather than accumulate, but it is still needed for users who stop making requests.

userStories.title: [DATA-CONTRACT/HIGH] Fix invoices camelCase-vs-snake_case response-shape mismatch on billing pages
userStories.description: As a billing user, I need invoice lists to render the number, customer, amount and due date, so that the billing pages don't show blank numbers, $NaN totals, and Invalid Date against the production billing edge function which returns raw snake_case rows.
acceptanceCriteria: client/src/pages/AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx (1230,1237,1577,1596,1608) and client/src/pages/Invoices.tsx (224,267): read invoice_number/total_amount/due_date/invoice_status/balance_due (or normalize once at the query boundary) instead of raw invoice.invoiceNumber/totalAmount/dueDate that only exist in the mock shape
Prefer a single normalizeInvoice() at the useQuery boundary (mirror the defensive dual-casing already in client/src/pages/Billing.tsx:93-97) so every consumer reads consistent keys
Verify against the billing edge fn response shape (supabase/functions/billing) documented in CLAUDE.md: total_amount/amount_paid/balance_due/invoice_status/paid_date
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by route/response-shape audit 2026-07-14. Same failure class as QuoteView/ESignatureIntegration/PlatformCustomerSuccess. Billing.tsx is already defensive; AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx and Invoices.tsx are not. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. ROOT CAUSE is an ASYMMETRY inside the billing edge fn that the AC never states: GET /billing/invoices (index.ts:222-258) does .select('*') and returns RAW snake_case rows in a { data, total } wrapper PLUS a NESTED customer relation (customer:business_records(...)), whereas GET /billing/invoices/:id returns camelCase via mapInvoiceRow (handlers/_context.ts:60). Same resource, two shapes — so every page hand-rolled its own bridge and each got it wrong differently. (1) NEW client/src/lib/invoice-normalize.ts — a single normalizeInvoice()/normalizeInvoices() + NormalizedInvoice type accepting snake, camel, or mixed rows; it also encodes the two traps once: PostgREST serializes decimals as STRINGS, and invoices has TWO status columns. (2) Invoices.tsx was the worst offender: its bridge read inv.invoiceNumber OR-ed with inv.invoiceNumber — THE SAME KEY OR-ED WITH ITSELF — five times over (invoiceNumber/contractId/customerId/dueDate/createdAt/updatedAt), so it never read invoice_number or due_date at all, and never mapped totalAmount or status. That is exactly the reported blank numbers + $NaN totals + Invalid Date. Rebound to useQuery<NormalizedInvoice[]>. (3) AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx: its BillingInvoice interface extended Invoice and re-declared snake fields typed as number — but decimals arrive as strings, so invoice.balance_due.toFixed(2) was a LIVE TypeError ("toFixed is not a function") on any invoice carrying a balance. Interface collapsed to NormalizedInvoice; the phantom customer_name/business_record_name reads (the real path is the nested customer.company_name) plus billing_period_*/payment_terms/balance_due all rebound. (4) Billing.tsx: its bridge preferred the LEGACY status column over the canonical invoice_status. invoices carries BOTH (schema.ts:2085 status default 'draft', invoice_status default 'open'), so a paid invoice could render as draft AND disagree with the ?status= filter, which queries invoice_status. The normalizer makes invoice_status win everywhere, matching the edge fn's own watermarkFor() and the CLAUDE.md billing schema audit. Also dropped its invoice.total read (not a real column). (5) TESTS: new server/tests/unit/invoice-normalize.test.ts (13 tests) pins BOTH real response shapes so an edge-fn change cannot silently regress this — mirrors the QUOTE-016 quote-math precedent. Full unit suite green (56 files / 1187 tests). tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; all 4 touched files at 0 errors. | FOLLOW-UPS (found, deliberately not fixed — outside this AC): (a) The SAME self-OR broken-normalizer bug (x.foo OR-ed with x.foo) also exists in Invoices.tsx for CONTRACTS (contractNumber) and CUSTOMERS (companyName), and in Billing.tsx for payment methods (createdAt). Harmless only if those endpoints already return camelCase. Worth a repo-wide sweep for that pattern — it is a copy-paste tell; ServiceHub.tsx had the identical idiom (fixed under AUDIT-013), so the same author/template seeded several pages. (b) The real fix for the underlying asymmetry is to apply mapInvoiceRow() to the LIST branch too, so /billing/invoices and /billing/invoices/:id agree. The client normalizer tolerates both and is safe either way, but the server-side split is the actual debt.

userStories.title: [ROUTE/HIGH] Fix leases edge fn pathParts[1] off-by-one after server.ts strip, and sweep other offenders
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need edge functions to read the resource segment from the path the way the dispatcher actually delivers it, so that routes don't resolve to the wrong (or undefined) sub-resource in production.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/leases/index.ts (~67): server.ts strips the function-name segment before invoking the handler, so const customerId = pathParts[1] is off-by-one — switch to normalizePath(pathname, 'leases') and read from pathParts[0] (or the correct index)

Grep supabase/functions for pathParts[1] and verify each remaining hit against the stripped path shape; fix the genuinely off-by-one ones (integrations fn is a known non-migrated case tracked elsewhere — note, don't duplicate)
Smoke-test the leases endpoints against the stripped path shape
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by route audit 2026-07-14. Same bug class documented in CLAUDE.md for the edge router (strips function name; read resource from pathParts[0]). | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. The audit UNDERSTATED this: the leases fn was not merely off-by-one, it was 100% unreachable in prod. (1) ROOT CAUSE: server.ts:168 does newUrl.pathname = '/' + pathParts.slice(1) — it always strips segment 0 — but leases/index.ts hand-rolled a raw split and switched on pathParts[0] === 'leases', so EVERY prod request fell to the default arm and 404'd. Fixed with normalizePath(url.pathname,'leases') (idempotent: strips a leading /leases only if present, so it is correct under BOTH the Coolify dispatcher and Supabase's native runtime). (2) SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT the AC did not mention: /lease-payments, /lease-renewals and /lease-dispositions have NO function dir, so server.ts 404'd them with 'Function not found' before any handler ran. Added aliases in server.ts. CRITICAL SUBTLETY: these are NOT like the EDGE-005f /public/calculator alias, where the discriminator sits at segment 1 and survives slice(1). Here the discriminator IS segment 0, so a plain alias would erase it (the exact trap CLAUDE.md documents for the signatures dispatcher) — introduced a stripSegments flag (default 1, unchanged for every other fn) set to 0 for these three so the prefix survives and the leases dispatcher can still key off it. (3) Removed the case 'customers' arm: /customers/:id/leases resolves to the REAL customers/ fn dir at segment 0 and never reached leases — dead code. handlers/leases.ts still implements 'by-customer' if that surface is ever wanted; forward from the customers fn. (4) VERIFIED with a harness importing the REAL _shared/path.ts normalizePath and mirroring the patched dispatcher arithmetic: all 9 URL shapes route correctly (/leases, /leases/:id, /leases/:id/payments, /leases/:id/initiate-renewal, /v1/leases/:id, /lease-payments/:id/process, /lease-renewals/:id, /lease-dispositions/:id, and /customers/:id/leases correctly NOT resolving to leases). Handlers needed ZERO changes — the slices match what they already expect. deno check: same 2 pre-existing errors (_pdf.ts TS2352, handlers/leases.ts TS2345) before and after; server.ts identical error profile before/after. | SWEEP (AC bullet 2) — all 177 pathParts[1] hits triaged mechanically, not by eyeball. 105 files construct pathParts from a raw split, but raw-split is NOT itself the bug: most index [1] as the SUB-RESOURCE after [0]=id, which is correct under the strip. The precise tell of the leases bug is a fn comparing a path segment to its OWN dir name; that matched 15 fns, and 13 are the DEFENSIVE hand-rolled idiom (rawParts[0]==='fn' ? rawParts.slice(1) : rawParts — a normalizePath equivalent) or have a safe else-fallback (teams, via stripPrefix) and are CORRECT. Two were genuinely broken: (a) onboarding/index.ts — FIXED HERE. Its guards required pathParts[0]==='onboarding', never true after the strip, so GET list + POST create 404'd in prod; the real discriminator is the 'checklists' collection segment. Note checklistId=parts[1]/subResource=parts[2] were already correct BY ACCIDENT under the frontend's real /onboarding/checklists/:id/:sub shape, so only the two guards + normalizePath were needed. Verified 9/11 real frontend URLs now route. Also fixed its pre-existing getUser(jwt) TS2345 per the CLAUDE.md 'fix the files you touch' rule -> file is now deno-check clean. (b) meetings/index.ts — a leases-style MULTIPLEX (switch cases 'calendar','schedule-request','meetings','types','rooms') with the same self-name-case bug, NOT fixed: it has NO frontend caller (no /api/meetings literal anywhere in client/src), so it is speculative surface needing its own story rather than a blind fix. integrations fn left alone as CLAUDE.md instructs. | KNOWN GAPS, deliberately not in scope: (i) DEV still serves /api/leases/* from the legacy Express server/routes/lease-routes.ts — there are ZERO lease entries in crmProxies, which is exactly WHY this prod-only breakage stayed invisible locally. Left as-is: adding a proxy would swing dev onto the edge fn and is a migration decision, not a bugfix. (ii) /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf and /api/onboarding/export/:id/:format still 404 in prod — the edge fn has no PDF/export implementation (Express-only, routes-registry.ts:568-570); porting them mirrors the leases _pdf.ts work and is a separate story. (iii) /api/onboarding/{getting-started,wizard-state,check-subdomain,update-step,confirm-subdomain} match no route in this fn either.

userStories.notes: Found by frontend mock-data audit 2026-07-14. These 5 are ROUTED and show fabricated numbers to users as real. GPT5Dashboard/SoftwareProducts sampleData are legit (mutation demo / CSV template) — do not touch. | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (passes stays FALSE — the 5 UI pages are NOT done; see REMAINING). THE PARENTHETICAL IN BULLET 1 WAS THE REAL STORY. "AND fix server/routes/ai-employee-routes.ts (12-16) which stubs auth with mock-user-id/mock-tenant-id" is filed as a footnote to a mock-data cleanup; it is actually a LIVE TENANT-ISOLATION BREACH, and it is fixed here. The router did: router.use((req,res,next) => { req.userId='mock-user-id'; req.tenantId='mock-tenant-id'; next(); }) TWO defects, and the second is the severe one: (1) NO AUTHENTICATION. routes-registry.ts mounts this with app.use('/api', ...), so all ten /api/ai-employees endpoints were reachable UNAUTHENTICATED and every row written was scoped to a fabricated tenant. (2) IT LEAKED ONTO UNRELATED ROUTES — this is the part nobody had spotted. That router.use has NO PATH, so in Express it runs for EVERY /api/* request that reaches this router and then FALLS THROUGH to whatever is mounted after it. getTenantId()'s FIRST priority is req.tenantId (server/utils/auth-helpers.ts), so any /api route registered later read back the fabricated tenant instead of the caller's. Confirmed against real code, not theory: routes-registry.ts registers the asyncRootApiMounts loop (which includes this router) BEFORE registerTodayDashboardRoutes / registerOnboardingRoutes / registerNotificationRoutes, and those resolve tenant via getTenantId (routes-today-dashboard.ts:41, plus 11 refs in routes-onboarding and 7 in routes-notifications). PROVEN, not argued: built a supertest harness reproducing the real mount order — GET /api/dashboards/today, for a caller whose real tenant was REAL-TENANT, resolved tenant = "mock-tenant-id". So in production right now those endpoints operate on a phantom tenant. FIX: removed the stub; auth is now `router.use('/ai-employees', requireAuth)` — PATH-SCOPED precisely so it can never affect another router again — and every handler resolves identity through the canonical getTenantId/getUserId helpers via a requireIdentity() guard that 401s rather than fabricating anything (12 call sites). Swept the repo: this was the ONLY mock-identity stub. tsc holds at the 1315 baseline; full unit suite green (61 files / 1269 tests). TESTS: server/tests/unit/ai-employee-auth.test.ts (6) encodes BOTH the Express behaviour that made this dangerous (a reproduction asserting the leak, and that a path-scoped middleware does NOT leak) and the shape of the fix, so a future pathless router.use on an /api-root router is caught. Worth noting the test needed its own bugfix: the source-scanning assertions strip comments, and the doc comment contains the literal text "/api/*" — a block-comment regex run FIRST treats that "/*" as an opener and swallows the router.use line it is asserting on. Line comments must be stripped first. That is the AUDIT-003 lesson in miniature: a regex that disagrees with the real lexer. | REMAINING — the 5 ROUTED mock-data pages themselves are untouched. All five confirmed still routed in App.tsx (/ai-employees:1169, /ai-search:1173, /conversational-ai-dashboard:1174, /service-dispatch:778, /mobile-optimization:858), so they are all still showing fabricated numbers to users as real. Backend availability was surveyed to settle wire-vs-gate per page (the AC allows either): AIEmployeeDashboard -> WIRE: the Express router is now real and authenticated (above), and a supabase/functions/ ai-employee edge fn also exists; note the frontend calls /api/ai-employees (PLURAL) while the edge dir is singular ai-employee — check that prefix resolves in prod before wiring (this is the EDGE-005a alias class of bug). AISearchKnowledgeDashboard -> WIRE: supabase/functions/ai-search exists AND server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts is mounted, so there is a real backend on both sides. MobileOptimization -> the AC says implement the missing /api/mobile/devices; a supabase/functions/mobile dir exists, so check whether the endpoint belongs there rather than adding an Express handler that prod never sees. ConversationalAIDashboard -> GATE coming-soon: no backend exists on either side (no edge fn, no Express route). ServiceDispatchOptimization -> GATE coming-soon: its mockMetrics/mockTechnicians/mockRoutes/mockAlerts have no backing endpoint (AUDIT-014 independently found this page is entirely hardcoded arrays with NYC coordinates). Per the AC's own rule, a page with no backend should get an explicit coming-soon state rather than render fixtures as if real — that is the cheap, honest half and is worth doing even before the wiring work. | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (part 2) — TWO OF THE FIVE PAGES GATED; ~1,700 lines of fixtures deleted; tsc 1315 -> 1314. Applied the AC's own rule ("for any page that legitimately has no backend yet, gate it behind an explicit coming-soon state rather than rendering fixtures as if real") to the two pages that provably have NO backend on either side. Established WHY they qualify rather than assuming: both have ZERO useQuery, ZERO useMutation and ZERO apiRequest calls — ServiceDispatchOptimization even IMPORTS useQuery/useMutation/useQueryClient and never calls them. Every number on both pages was fabricated and presented as live. NEW client/src/components/ui/coming-soon.tsx — a generic, traceable placeholder (title/description/storyIds/ capabilities/note), generalized from the existing components/blog/BlogSectionPlaceholder rather than invented from scratch. It states plainly that nothing on the page is live data, which is the whole point: an empty honest page is better than fixtures a user cannot distinguish from their own data. ConversationalAIDashboard (/conversational-ai-dashboard, was ~650 lines): had hardcoded mockMessages, mockConversations, mockCapabilities and a generateMockResponse() behind a setTimeout that FAKED the assistant thinking and replying — a user could hold an entire scripted conversation with nothing. No conversational-ai edge function and no Express route exists. Gated. ServiceDispatchOptimization (/service-dispatch, was ~1,070 lines): mockMetrics, mockTechnicians with invented names and NEW YORK CITY coordinates, mockRoutes, mockAlerts — fake technician pins on a map, presented as real-time tracking. No dispatch/routing backend exists anywhere (AUDIT-014 independently flagged this page as entirely hardcoded). Gated, with a pointer to the REAL service surface (/service-hub, backed by routes-mobile-api.ts GET /api/service-tickets) so the gate does not read as "service is gone". Both remain routed and in-shell (MainLayout) — the route still works, it just tells the truth now. The fixture UI is recoverable via `git log --follow` the moment an API exists. tsc baseline tightened to 1314; full unit suite green (61 files / 1269 tests). | STILL REMAINING (3 pages, all WIRE candidates — they have real backends, so gating them would be wrong): AIEmployeeDashboard (/ai-employees) — its Express router is now authenticated and real (see part 1 above), so this is a genuine wiring job: replace useState(mockEmployees/mockAnalytics) with useQuery against /api/ai-employees. WATCH OUT: the frontend calls the PLURAL /api/ai-employees while the edge dir is the SINGULAR ai-employee — verify the prod prefix resolves before wiring, this is the EDGE-005a alias class of bug. AISearchKnowledgeDashboard (/ai-search) — supabase/functions/ai-search AND server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts both exist and are mounted; wire it. MobileOptimization (/mobile-optimization) — the AC says implement the missing /api/mobile/devices. A supabase/functions/mobile dir exists, so decide whether the endpoint belongs there rather than adding an Express handler production never sees (the CLAUDE.md dev-vs-prod backend split). | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (part 3) — AIEmployeeDashboard WIRED, and the mock went DEEPER than the AC described. THE AC SAYS "wire useQuery to /api/ai-employees instead of useState(mockEmployees/mockAnalytics)". Doing only that would have LAUNDERED the fiction rather than removed it: GET /api/ai-employees/analytics/overview was itself returning a HARDCODED object ("Mock analytics data - in real implementation, this would aggregate from the database") — 23 tasks today, 82% quality, $1,250 saved. Wiring the page to that endpoint makes the invented numbers look MORE real, not less, because they now arrive over the network. So the backend was fixed first. BACKEND: new aiEmployeeService.getAnalyticsOverview(tenantId) aggregates the real ai_employees / ai_employee_tasks rows — counts, active count, tasks today, completed today, AVG(quality_score), AVG(execution_time_minutes), AVG(user_satisfaction_rating), GROUP BY employee_type for the type breakdown, the 10 most recent tasks joined to employee names, and a 7-day trend series. The trend uses generate_series so days with no tasks stay 0 rather than collapsing out and misaligning the chart. Tenant-scoped throughout; errors degrade to zeros rather than throwing (an analytics panel must not take the page down). costSavings is returned as NULL, not a number: nothing in the schema records a saving, so it is reported as unknown and the UI renders an em-dash. Inventing a money figure is precisely the problem this story exists to remove. FRONTEND: replaced useState(mockEmployees)/useState(mockAnalytics) with real useQuery calls. NOTE the necessary bridge — the service returns raw `SELECT * FROM ai_employees` rows, i.e. SNAKE_CASE, while the page reads camelCase (employeeName/successRate/...). Wiring it naively would have rendered every field BLANK against real data: exactly the AUDIT-011 bug. Added toAiEmployee() at the query boundary. Also unwrapped the { success, data, count } envelope. REMOVED TWO CONTROLS rather than leave them as fiction (CLAUDE.md: delete features with no backing implementation): the pause/resume toggle only flipped LOCAL state — there is NO PATCH/PUT/DELETE endpoint on this router at all, so it could never persist and the change vanished on the next refetch; and "Assign Task" only console.log'd (a real POST /api/ai-employees/tasks exists, but using it needs a task form — a feature, not a wiring fix). Dropped the orphaned Pause import. tsc holds at 1314; full unit suite green (61 files / 1269 tests). ONE THING VERIFIED THAT LOOKED ALARMING: the service queries ai_employees / ai_employee_tasks, which are in NO drizzle schema or migration. They are NOT phantom — they are created by drizzle/rls/ai-employee-tables.sql, applied OUT OF BAND like drizzle/functions/*.sql. So this wiring depends on that file having been applied to the target DB; if it has not, the service swallows the error and the dashboard shows zeros/empty (honest) rather than 500ing. | REMAINING (2 of 5 pages): AISearchKnowledgeDashboard (/ai-search) — supabase/functions/ai-search AND server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts both exist and are mounted, so it is a genuine wiring job like the one above; check first whether ITS backend also fabricates (the AI-employee analytics endpoint did). MobileOptimization (/mobile-optimization) — the AC asks to implement the missing /api/mobile/devices; a supabase/functions/mobile dir exists, so decide whether the endpoint belongs THERE rather than adding an Express handler production never sees (the CLAUDE.md dev-vs-prod backend split). Also still open from part 1: the frontend calls the PLURAL /api/ai-employees while the edge dir is the SINGULAR ai-employee — the Express router serves dev, but verify the prod prefix resolves (EDGE-005a alias class) before trusting this page in production. | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (part 4) — MobileOptimization GATED (4 of 5 pages now resolved: 3 gated + 1 wired). I DID NOT FOLLOW AC BULLET 5 ("implement the missing /api/mobile/devices endpoint"), because that instruction presumes data that does not exist, and following it would have meant INVENTING the figures server-side — the exact trap the AI-employee analytics endpoint had already fallen into (part 3), where a route fabricated its numbers and the page just laundered them. Checked before deciding:   - NO device/session table records a device type for app users. The ONLY device_type column in the entire schema     is on a knowledge-base ARTICLE VIEW table (knowledge-base-schema.ts:275 — KB readers). Aggregating that into an     app-wide "mobile vs tablet vs desktop" split would produce a DIFFERENT, misleading number, not a correct one.   - The page's other metrics — offlineCapability, batteryOptimization, crashRate, dataUsage, avgResponseTime — are     APM/RUM measurements. There is no APM or client-telemetry integration anywhere in this system to source them     from, and "battery optimization %" is not derivable from a database at all. So the AC's own escape hatch applies ("for any page that legitimately has no backend yet, gate it behind an explicit coming-soon state"). Gated; 428 lines of fixtures removed. WHAT IT WAS DOING: useQuery on /api/mobile/metrics and /api/mobile/devices — NEITHER exists — then `|| mockMetrics` / `|| mockDeviceBreakdown`. The failed queries were INVISIBLE: no error, no empty state, just a confident 95% offline capability, 88% battery optimization, 0.02% crash rate and a 68/22/10 device split. That silent-fallback pattern is the most dangerous shape in this story class — the page cannot be distinguished from a working one, so nobody ever files a bug. tsc holds at 1314; full unit suite green (61 files / 1269 tests). | CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE (part 1) — I classified AISearchKnowledgeDashboard as a WIRE candidate on the grounds that "supabase/functions/ai-search exists AND server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts is mounted, so there is a real backend on both sides". That was reasoning from EXISTENCE, and it was half wrong. Actually looking inside them:   - server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts is MOCK ("Mock search suggestions...", "Mock knowledge entities -     in production, this would query the database", "Mock entity retrieval", "Mock knowledge graph data").   - server/services/ai-search-knowledge-service.ts is MOCK to the core: "Mock embedding generation - in production     this would call OpenAI's embedding API", getMockEmbeddings(), "Mock semantic search results - in production     this would use vector database", "Mock analytics data".   - The supabase/functions/ai-search EDGE fn, by contrast, has NO mock markers and queries REAL tables     (knowledge_entities, vector_embeddings, ai_search_queries, ai_generated_answers), with knowledge_entities     created by drizzle/rls/ai-search.sql — the same out-of-band DDL pattern as ai-employee-tables.sql. So the truth is the CLAUDE.md dev-vs-prod split: PROD (edge fn) is real, DEV (Express) is fiction, and /api/ai-search is NOT in crmProxies so dev never touches the real one. LESSON worth keeping: "an endpoint exists" is not evidence it returns real data — in this repo three separate layers (page, Express route, service) were each independently faking, and the AI-employee story had the same shape. | REMAINING (1 page): AISearchKnowledgeDashboard (/ai-search, 1244 lines) builds mockEntities/mockAnalytics/ mockSuggestions/mockResults/mockAnswer unconditionally and calls NOTHING. It is a genuine wiring job against the real edge fn (handlers: search, entities, embeddings, analytics) — deliberately NOT rushed here, because doing it properly means verifying each of the five surfaces against the edge handlers' actual response shapes (the AUDIT-011 blank-field trap) rather than pointing useQuery at a URL and hoping. Two prerequisites for whoever picks it up: (a) decide whether to add /api/ai-search to crmProxies so DEV stops hitting the mock Express router — otherwise the page will look wired but still show fiction locally, which is worse than today; (b) confirm drizzle/rls/ai-search.sql has been applied to the target DB, since knowledge_entities/vector_embeddings live there, not in migrations. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 (part 5) — AISearchKnowledgeDashboard WIRED. That was the last of the 5 pages, so passes flips TRUE (3 gated coming-soon + 2 wired). Backend was fixed FIRST, again: part 3's lesson (wiring a page to an endpoint that fabricates its own numbers LAUNDERS the fiction rather than removing it) applied twice more here. THREE REAL DEFECTS FOUND IN THE EDGE FN BEFORE ANY WIRING — none were in the AC: (1) THE ANSWER SHAPE DEPENDED ON WHETHER A DB INSERT SUCCEEDED. synthesizeAnswer returned the RAW INSERTED ROW (snake_case: answer_text/answer_confidence/source_documents) on the happy path but a camelCase LITERAL on the insert-failure fallback. The page reads camelCase, so the happy path rendered BLANK and only the failure path rendered. Fixed at the source rather than teaching the frontend both dialects: the response is now built from answerRow, one camelCase shape on both paths, and returns the FULL answer (sections + the four quality scores) instead of the subset the old .select() projected. id is now null when the insert failed — there is no row to vote against — and the feedback control disables on that. (2) ANALYTICS WAS MISSING THREE FIELDS THE PAGE'S TOP KPI TILES READ: answersGenerated / averageAnswerConfidence / answerHelpfulnessRate did not exist in the payload at all. Added as REAL aggregates over ai_generated_answers in the same window (count, AVG(answer_confidence), helpful/(helpful+unhelpful)); an answer-side failure degrades just those three to zero rather than taking the whole analytics payload down. (3) UNCONSTRAINED MODEL JSON COULD CRASH THE PAGE. answerSections/keyPoints/relatedTopics come from a Claude completion, so a field the prompt requests as an array can return a STRING — and the render's `.length > 0 && ....map(...)` guard PASSES for a string then throws on .map. Coerced with asArray() in the fn and again in the frontend mapper. | THE WIRING ITSELF — the trap the notes predicted, in its most severe form. The AUDIT-011 bug here was not blank fields, it was a CRASH: the render calls entity.createdAt.toLocaleDateString() and result.source.createdAt.toLocaleDateString(), the API returns ISO STRINGS, and "2026-01-02T10:00:00Z".toLocaleDateString is not a function. It was invisible only because the deleted fixtures were hand-built as new Date(...) OBJECTS in the page's own view-model shape. /knowledge/entities also returns raw select('*') rows (snake_case) with numeric(3,2) columns that PostgREST can serialize as STRINGS (importanceScore drives a `width: ${score*100}%` bar → NaN). So the mappers revive Dates, map snake→camel, and Number()-coerce. Extracted to client/src/lib/ai-search/normalize.ts (pure, no React — the vitest env is node, and the mappers are the actual risk) + 11 tests in normalize.test.ts. The tests were MUTATION-CHECKED: reverting the Date revival and reading .entityName off a snake_case row makes exactly the 2 relevant tests fail, so they are not vacuous. Page 1244 → 954 lines. | DEV/PROD RESOLUTION VERIFIED END-TO-END (not assumed): added '/api/ai-search' → 'ai-search' to crmProxies. NOTE — MY OWN FIRST JUSTIFICATION FOR THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG and the correction matters for the record: I wrote that dev "would keep hitting the mock Express router". It would not. That router (routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts) is mounted at /api with paths like '/search/semantic', so it answers on /api/search/* and /api/knowledge/* — DIFFERENT prefixes; it never served /api/ai-search/* at all. Without the entry dev simply 404s. Traced both sides: dev app.use('/api/ai-search') → EDGE/ai-search/knowledge/entities → fn stripPrefix removes ^/ai-search → ['knowledge','entities'] ✓; prod server.ts auto-registers the fn by DIRECTORY NAME (it Deno.readDir's /app/functions, so no manual registration exists to be missing) and strips 1 segment → handler sees /knowledge/entities → stripPrefix tolerates the absent prefix → same dispatch ✓. Dir name == prefix segment, so per the EDGE-004 decision rule NO server.ts override is needed. | REMOVED FOUR DEAD ANALYTICS CARDS rather than give them empty states: "Trending Topics", "AI Insights", "Optimization Recommendations", "Content Creation Suggestions". The handler hardcodes trendingTopics/aiInsights/optimizationRecommendations/contentSuggestions to [] and NOTHING populates them — wired up they are four permanently-empty cards promising analysis the product does not perform. Per the CLAUDE.md rule applied throughout this story (delete features with no backing implementation), removed; recoverable via git log --follow. "Query Types" is REAL (grouped from recorded query_intent) and was kept, with a genuine empty state. Also fixed a latent bug carried over from the fixtures: handleSuggestionClick called setSearchQuery then read searchQuery back, so it always ran the PREVIOUS query — the suggestion is now passed explicitly. | VERIFICATION: tsc holds at the 1308 baseline (0 new errors; touched files clean). deno check clean on the whole ai-search fn. New suite 11/11 green. Full npm run test unchanged vs a STASHED clean tree — 18 files / 10 tests fail identically with and without this change, i.e. all pre-existing and unrelated (they are integration tests; the "61 files green" figure in the earlier notes predates upstream growth to 82). NOT verified: no live run against a real tenant — this needs drizzle/rls/ai-search-tables.sql + ai-search.sql applied to the target DB (knowledge_entities/vector_embeddings/ai_search_queries/ai_generated_answers live there, NOT in migrations — the same out-of-band DDL pattern as ai-employee-tables.sql). If they are absent the page shows empty/zeros, which is honest, rather than fiction. Semantic search additionally needs OPENAI_API_KEY (degrades to a text-match prefilter without it) and ANTHROPIC creds for the answer (the answer is skipped on failure; results still return). | FOLLOW-UP FOUND, NOT DONE (deliberately out of scope): server/routes/ai-search-knowledge-routes.ts is now provably DEAD — grepped repo-wide (client, server, mobile, edge) for every prefix it serves and there are ZERO callers. It is 9 mock endpoints nobody can reach. Deleting it is safe on its own, BUT its service (server/services/ai-search-knowledge-service.ts, also mock — getMockEmbeddings()) still has a LIVE consumer: knowledge-base-service.ts:761 calls AISearchKnowledgeService.createContentEmbedding, meaning KB embeddings are currently generated by a mock. That is a separate story: delete the dead router, then decide whether the KB embedding path should call the real edge fn. | PROD 404 CLOSED 2026-07-17 — the risk this story flagged three times and never resolved. Part 1/3's notes said, repeatedly: "the frontend calls the PLURAL /api/ai-employees while the edge dir is the SINGULAR ai-employee — verify the prod prefix resolves before wiring (this is the EDGE-005a alias class of bug)". Verified today: IT DID NOT RESOLVE. supabase/functions/ai-employee is singular, the dashboard calls /api/ai-employees (+ /analytics/overview, /tasks), and supabase/functions/server.ts had NO alias — so every call from the page this story WIRED was 404ing in production. Dev never showed it because the Express router (routes/ai-employee-routes.ts, whose auth this story fixed in part 1) serves that prefix locally. Fixed with a server.ts alias. | HOW IT SURFACED, which is worth more than the fix: `npm run check:routes` — a ratchet that already existed and that I had not run all session — reports it plainly as "3 NEW missing-edge route(s) (frontend calls it, NO edge fn → PROD 404): /api/ai-employees, /api/email-sequences, /api/web-forms". It also fails on a CLEAN tree, i.e. THE ROUTE-OWNERSHIP GATE IS ALREADY RED ON MAIN (same situation the typecheck baseline was in per docs/typecheck-baseline.json). /api/email-sequences and /api/web-forms are the same class and are still open. Lesson: run the repo's OWN guards before hunting for bugs by hand — this one had the answer sitting in it. | MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG AND I CAUGHT IT BY CHECKING THE HANDLER. I initially copied the accounts-payable alias shape (plain rename, default stripSegments = 1). That would still have 404'd: the ai-employee handler's own URL layout is /ai-employee/ai-employees/... — it reads `firstSegment = pathParts[0]` and compares it to 'ai-employees', so the plural segment is its RESOURCE DISCRIMINATOR, not merely a prefix. Stripping it hands the handler /analytics/overview and pathParts[0] becomes 'analytics' — every route still misses. The correct shape is stripSegments = 0 (the leases family pattern), which hands it /ai-employees/analytics/overview. Simulated the dispatcher against all three frontend paths to confirm: all now yield pathParts[0] === 'ai-employees'. | AND THE CHECK THIS STORY'S OWN LESSON DEMANDED: is the EDGE fn's analytics real, or would the alias turn a 404 into FICTION? Part 3 established that GET /api/ai-employees/analytics/overview was returning a HARDCODED object and that wiring the page to it would have "LAUNDERED the fiction rather than removed it". That fix was made to the EXPRESS service. The EDGE handler is a different file — so routing prod to it could have re-introduced exactly the fabrication this story exists to delete. Checked: supabase/functions/ai-employee/handlers/analytics.ts queries the real ai_employees / ai_employee_tasks tables and its own header says "Express file returned mock data; we aggregate from real ai_employee_tasks". So the alias routes prod to genuine aggregates. Had it been mock, the honest move would have been to leave the 404. | NOTE the checker cannot see this fix: check-route-ownership resolves edge functions by DIRECTORY NAME and knows nothing about server.ts aliases, so /api/ai-employees will keep reporting as missing-edge. accounts-payable does not report only because it ALSO has a crmProxies entry. Adding one here would change DEV to serve this page from the edge fn instead of Express — plausible, but it needs the edge fn verified against all three frontend paths first, and the Express router's real analytics (part 3) would then stop being exercised. Left for whoever owns the ai-employee domain; the prod 404 is fixed either way.

userStories.title: [UI/MEDIUM] Resolve dead unrouted mock dashboards (delete or wire)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need dead mock-only dashboards that aren't routed or imported anywhere to be either removed or properly wired, so that they don't rot into false 'existing feature' signal.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide per page (delete vs wire to a real endpoint): client/src/pages/AIDocumentationDashboard.tsx (server GET /api/documents in ai-documentation-routes.ts also returns mock), MeetingSchedulingDashboard.tsx, MeetingTranscriptionDashboard.tsx, AdvancedWorkflowsDashboard.tsx
None of these are registered in App.tsx or imported by any live page — confirm before deleting
If kept, register the route and wire the real backend; if deleted, remove the file and any dangling imports
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by frontend mock-data audit 2026-07-14. Distinguish MeetingTranscriptionDashboard.tsx (dead) from the routed MeetingTranscription.tsx (/meeting-transcription) — verify the routed one separately. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. Deleted 8 files / 5,758 lines of unreachable code; tsc 1335 -> 1315 (-20), baseline tightened. HOW DEADNESS WAS PROVEN (the AC says "confirm before deleting", and "not in App.tsx" is NOT sufficient — a page can be reached via a component, a barrel, or a lazy import inside another page): walked the IMPORT GRAPH transitively from App.tsx (535 reachable files) and from main.tsx (72), then separately grepped the whole tree for importers of each candidate. The tool was validated with a CONTROL: MeetingTranscription.tsx — which the story notes say IS routed and must not be confused with the dead MeetingTranscriptionDashboard.tsx — correctly came back LIVE, imported by App.tsx. All four AC-named pages came back DEAD with ZERO importers. DELETED (group 1, the AC list): AIDocumentationDashboard.tsx, MeetingSchedulingDashboard.tsx, MeetingTranscriptionDashboard.tsx, AdvancedWorkflowsDashboard.tsx — unreachable, mock-only, nobody imports them. Chose DELETE over WIRE for all four: they render fixtures against no real backend (the AC itself notes the server GET /api/documents in ai-documentation-routes.ts also returns mock), so "wiring" them would mean building the feature, not fixing a bug. Deleting matches the repo precedent (EDGE-004 deleted the phantom-column routes-platform-* files; the CLAUDE.md BATCH-7 rule is to delete features with no backing implementation rather than fake them). git history keeps them if anyone wants them back. DELETED (group 2, the cluster AUDIT-014 deferred to this story): pages/CustomerPortal.tsx + components/customer-portal/{CustomerDashboard,CustomerPortalLogin,ServiceRequestForm}.tsx. This one was irredeemable, not merely unrouted: it imported SIX components that do not exist on disk (ServiceRequestList, MeterReadingForm, MeterReadingHistory, SupplyOrderForm, SupplyOrderList, PaymentForm -> the 20 TS2307s it contributed to the ratchet) and its body used the REACT ROUTER api (<Routes>, element={}, <Navigate to replace/>) while importing from wouter — Routes/Navigate were never imported at all and react-router-dom is not even a dependency. It could not compile, let alone render. The four files form a closed cycle (the three components import useCustomerPortal from the page; nothing else imports them), so they delete cleanly as a unit. CAREFULLY NOT DELETED: the other SIX components in components/customer-portal/ (CustomerSatisfactionAnalyticsDashboard, CustomerSatisfactionForm, EquipmentHealthDashboard, MaintenanceSchedulingComponent, ServiceRequestsDashboard, UsageAnalyticsDashboard) are imported by the ROUTED CustomerSelfServicePortal.tsx and are LIVE — verified per-component, not assumed from the directory name. Also note pages/CustomerPortalService.tsx is a DIFFERENT, live page that a substring grep for "CustomerPortal" flags as a false positive; it was left alone. VERIFICATION: no dangling imports after deletion (no new TS2307); tsc 1315 and the ratchet re-baselined to match; full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | MORE DEAD PAGES FOUND BY THE SAME SWEEP, deliberately NOT deleted here (outside this AC's named list, and each is a judgement call that deserves an explicit decision rather than being swept up in a cleanup): GdprComplianceDashboard.tsx (dead; holds 7 broken /gdpr/* links and there are ZERO /gdpr routes registered — either GDPR compliance UI is a real intended feature and needs routes+backends, or the page should go), workflow-automation.tsx (a DEAD DUPLICATE of the routed WorkflowAutomation.tsx — App.tsx imports @/pages/WorkflowAutomation; this near-namesake is the classic trap and should probably just be deleted), enhanced-crm.tsx, LeadIntelligenceDashboard.tsx, onboarding.tsx (a dead duplicate of the routed OnboardingDashboard family). All five confirmed unreachable with zero importers by the same import-graph walk. Recommend a follow-up story to decide delete-vs-wire per page; the reachability tooling to re-verify them is described above. | FOLLOW-UP EXECUTED 2026-07-29 (under QUALITY-002 batch 27). This story's closing note recommended 'a follow-up story to decide delete-vs-wire per page' for the five MORE dead pages it found but did not delete. Four of the five are now DELETED: pages/workflow-automation.tsx, pages/enhanced-crm.tsx, pages/LeadIntelligenceDashboard.tsx, pages/onboarding.tsx (plus components/layout/CollapsibleSidebar.tsx, the unimported RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar duplicate that AUDIT-014 had flagged separately). Chose DELETE over WIRE for the same reason this story chose it for the first eight: two of them (workflow-automation.tsx, onboarding.tsx) are duplicates of pages that ARE routed, so 'wiring' them would mean routing a second copy of a live surface. THE FIFTH IS NO LONGER DEAD AND MUST NOT BE DELETED: GdprComplianceDashboard.tsx is now LIVE — the GDPR P1-b commit ('route the orphaned GDPR dashboard as an admin overview') routed it after this story's notes were written, which resolves the open question this story posed ('either GDPR compliance UI is a real intended feature and needs routes+backends, or the page should go'). It was a real feature. Re-verified with import-graph BFS from all 158 entry points before touching anything — the lesson being that a recorded deadness claim expires, and the reachability walk must be re-run, not re-read.

userStories.title: [CONFIG/HIGH] Document required env vars and make critical integrations fail loud in production
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need every required environment variable documented and critical integrations to error (not silently simulate) when their config is missing in production, so that a missing key surfaces at deploy time instead of silently disabling a feature that looks healthy.
acceptanceCriteria: Add the 12 undocumented-but-required vars to the appropriate .env.example files: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SENDGRID_API_KEY (+RESEND_API_KEY), INTERNAL_CRON_TOKEN, BACKUP_GCS_BUCKET, SALESFORCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, MICROSOFT_WEBHOOK_SECRET, QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, ADDRESS_BOOK_MASTER_KEY/PRINTYX_CREDENTIAL_VAULT_KEY, TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID/AUTH_TOKEN/FROM_NUMBER

In production (NODE_ENV=production), make these fail loud via server/config/env-validation.ts (mirror the existing hard-error pattern used for STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET at env-validation.ts:174) rather than falling back to simulation: email-service.ts:185 (SendGrid sim), sms-service.ts:147-159 (Twilio sim), ai-email-parser-service.ts:11 (Claude stub)
Ensure webhook handlers (webhook-service.ts:219/241/317) reject/log clearly when their secret is unset instead of appearing connected while dropping updates
Ensure INTERNAL_CRON_TOKEN absence is a startup error (cron-auth.ts:62) so scheduled jobs don't silently 401
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by env-var audit 2026-07-14. STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD are already documented + fail loud — use as the template. RESEND_API_KEY (email-service.ts:215) is a variable-name trap vs the documented SEO_RESEND_API_KEY. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. STALE AC PATHS — every file path in this AC was wrong; the real ones are: server/lib/env-validation.ts (NOT server/config/env-validation.ts), server/integrations/webhook-service.ts (NOT server/services/), and supabase/functions/_shared/cron-auth.ts (NOT server/middleware/cron-auth.ts — it is a DENO edge helper, not Express middleware). The referenced line numbers were still accurate (env-validation.ts:174 really is the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET template). DESIGN RULE ADOPTED (copied from the Stripe/LAUNCH-014 precedent): never force anyone to configure an integration — that would refuse to boot deployments which legitimately run without email/SMS — but HARD-FAIL on a CONTRADICTION, i.e. a provider that is SELECTED but not configured. Erroring on mere absence would have taken prod down on deploy; erroring on the contradiction is what actually surfaces the silent-simulation bug the story is about. (1) DOCUMENTED all 12 vars in .env.example (+2 the AC missed) across 6 new commented sections, each stating the FAILURE MODE rather than just the name. (2) FAIL-LOUD in production (server/lib/env-validation.ts): EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid without SENDGRID_API_KEY, =resend without RESEND_API_KEY, =aws-ses without AWS creds, and SMS_PROVIDER=twilio without TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID/AUTH_TOKEN/PHONE_NUMBER are now ERRORS (previously all four silently degraded to simulation: the app looked healthy and sent nothing). Warnings added for the cases we cannot prove are in use: the credential vault key, the three inbound webhook secrets, and INTERNAL_CRON_TOKEN. (3) BUG FIXED in server/integrations/webhook-service.ts: verifyQuickBooksSignature did `if (!secret) return false;` SILENTLY, so a missing QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN was indistinguishable from a bad signature — QuickBooks appeared connected while every inbound webhook was dropped without a trace. It now logs like its Salesforce/Microsoft siblings (which already warned + rejected correctly, so AC bullet 3 was already satisfied for those two). (4) TESTS: new server/tests/unit/env-validation-integrations.test.ts (16 tests) against the REAL validateEnvironment(). Worth noting the pre-existing sibling env-validation.test.ts asserts against a hand-written MOCK re-implementation of the validator, so it cannot catch drift from the module it claims to cover — these import the real thing. Verified NON-VACUOUS: 9 of the 16 FAIL against the pre-change module (the 7 that pass are the negative controls — development-unaffected, fully-configured, and simulation paths). Full unit suite green (57 files / 1203 tests); tsc holds at the 1335 baseline. | TWO REAL BUGS THE AC GOT WRONG, both found by grepping the code instead of trusting the story: (a) TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER vs TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER — the AC lists only TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, but BOTH names are live in DIFFERENT RUNTIMES: the Express services (server/services/sms-service.ts:149, server/services/mfa-otp-service.ts:370) read TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER, while the Deno edge fn (supabase/functions/mfa/_twilio.ts:22) reads TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER. A deployment that sets only the AC-named TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER leaves ALL Express SMS silently in simulation (and vice versa for edge MFA). Both are now documented, with an explicit "set BOTH" warning, and the production check keys on TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER (what the Express runtime this validator guards actually reads). A test pins the trap. Consolidating onto one name is a follow-up (it needs a coordinated env change in the deploy environment). (b) SEO_RESEND_API_KEY is documented in .env.example but read by ZERO code anywhere in the repo (verified by grep across all ts/tsx/js/mjs) — it sits in an SEO_* namespace (SEO_EMAIL_PROVIDER/SEO_EMAIL_FROM) that nothing consumes either. So the ONE resend-looking var a deployer would find in the docs is the one that does nothing, while the var email-service.ts actually reads (RESEND_API_KEY) was undocumented. The new RESEND_API_KEY entry and the production error message both call this trap out explicitly, and a test asserts SEO_RESEND_API_KEY does NOT satisfy the requirement. Deleting the dead SEO_* block is a follow-up (left alone in case a deploy script outside this repo reads it). | DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: (i) INTERNAL_CRON_TOKEN is a WARNING, not a startup error as AC bullet 4 asks. It is read ONLY by the Deno edge runtime (supabase/functions/_shared/cron-auth.ts), which already logs "INTERNAL_CRON_TOKEN env var is unset — cron endpoints will always reject" and 401s. The Express server never reads it, so making the Express boot hard-fail on a variable belonging to a different container would be wrong-layer; the edge dispatcher has no equivalent startup hook today. Adding one to supabase/functions/server.ts is the correct fix and wants its own story. (ii) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY stays a warning (existing rule already covers ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY). Note ai-email-parser-service.ts:11 constructs the Anthropic client with a non-null assertion (process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!) rather than being a "Claude stub" as the AC describes — it throws at CALL time, not startup. Erroring at boot would refuse to start every deployment not using AI features. (iii) BACKUP_GCS_BUCKET documented only — it already defaults to "printyx-backups", so absence is not a failure.

userStories.title: EPIC: Post-Neon→Supabase site remediation (tracking)
userStories.description: As the team, we need a single tracking story for the remediation of breakage introduced when production moved from Neon Postgres + Express to self-hosted Supabase (Edge Functions + Postgres pooler + GoTrue), so the SUPA-### work stream is coordinated and its exit criteria are explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: Root cause is understood and documented: prod has NO Express server — the static frontend calls functions.printyx.net/<fn>/* directly (client/src/lib/queryClient.ts → getApiUrl; dispatcher supabase/functions/server.ts). server/routes-*.ts is dev-only. Any unported endpoint 404s in prod.

Three breakage classes are tracked to closure: (1) orphaned DB migrations → missing schema (SUPA-001..005), (2) missing/divergent edge functions → prod 404 or dev/prod drift (SUPA-010..024), (3) pages built against mock shapes → silent blank/fake data (SUPA-030..031), plus (4) env/auth/connection integrity (SUPA-040..041).
A short living doc (docs/supabase-remediation.md) links every SUPA-### story to its status and owner.

EXIT: check-route-ownership baseline has 0 missingEdge and 0 bothDivergent that are genuinely broken; db:migrate:status shows the live DB fully migrated; no page renders mock/blank due to a contract mismatch.
userStories.notes: Umbrella for the deep-dive findings. Suggested execution order: SUPA-040/041 (unblock connectivity+auth) → SUPA-001..005 (schema) → SUPA-010..017 (prod 404s) → SUPA-020..024 (divergence) → SUPA-030..031 (contracts). Severity: P0.

acceptanceCriteria: A working introspection connection is established: correct Supavisor username format (role.tenant), correct DB_SSL/DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, using DIRECT Postgres (typically 5432) via DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/DIRECT_DATABASE_URL rather than the 5433 pooler for DDL/introspection.

A checked-in report (scripts/db-schema-snapshot output) lists: public table count, presence of the suspected-missing objects (web_forms, email_sequences, email_sequence_enrollments, custom_field_definitions, workflow_executions, auto_orders) and columns (proposals.discount_reason, proposals.share_token, proposal_line_items discount/net columns), and the full contents of drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.

Finding is recorded in docs/supabase-remediation.md.
userStories.notes: Blocks SUPA-002/003. userStories.title: Reconcile the drizzle migration journal with orphaned migration files
userStories.description: As a developer, I need drizzle/migrations/meta/_journal.json to reflect ALL migration files on disk, because the journal currently lists only 12 entries (0000–0011, the auto-generated ones) while migrations 0012–0028 and several duplicate-numbered 0008–0011 files were hand-authored and never registered. drizzle's native migrator only runs journaled migrations, so `npm run db:migrate` silently applies nothing past 0011.
acceptanceCriteria: Root cause documented: _journal.json has 12 entries ending at 0011_pa026_perf_indexes; on disk there are numbered files through 0028 plus duplicate prefixes (two each of 0008/0009/0010/0011, e.g. 0008_client_enrollment_tokens vs 0008_pretty_rocket_raccoon).

Duplicate-numbered migrations are renumbered to a unique, deterministic order (e.g. the hand-authored 0008–0011 client_enrollment_tokens/monitoring_clients_customer_id/client_commands/device_alerts get fresh sequential numbers after 0028) with no two files sharing a prefix.

_journal.json is rebuilt so every file on disk (0000..N) has a matching entry with the correct tag, idx, and a snapshot in meta/ — verified by drizzle-kit (regenerate cleanly, do not hand-forge hashes where avoidable).
The reconciled journal, when checked with `npm run db:migrate:status`, correctly shows applied vs pending against the SUPA-001 snapshot with no crash.
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes:
This is the single biggest root cause of the "features built but broken" reports and the PGRST204 "retry without column" hacks in CLAUDE.md (0019 discount_reason, proposal line-item cols, tenant metadata, custom fields, workflow idempotency index, web_forms, email_sequence_enrollments). Do NOT apply anything in this story — SUPA-002 only makes the ledger correct; SUPA-003 applies. Severity: P0.

VERIFIED DONE (2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive): npm run check:migrations passes — "Checked 40 migration file(s) against 40 journal entry(ies) … every migration file is journaled, prefixes unique, idx contiguous." The 21 unjournaled files + 4 duplicate prefixes reported in docs/CODEBASE-HEALTH-2026-07-27.md are reconciled, and check:migrations is CI-wired (SUPA-005).

userStories.title: Bring the live Supabase DB fully migrated (baseline vs apply, backed up)
userStories.description: As an operator, I need the reconciled migrations (SUPA-002) actually reflected in the live DB, applying only what is genuinely missing and baselining what already exists, so the schema matches shared/*-schema.ts without destructive re-creation.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh backup is taken first: npm run db:backup (verify the dump exists in GCS) — no schema change runs until a backup is confirmed.

Per the SUPA-001 snapshot, each pending migration is classified: ALREADY-APPLIED (objects exist, likely via db:push) → mark applied via `npm run db:migrate:baseline` semantics; NOT-APPLIED → apply via `npm run db:migrate`.
Migrations are applied against DIRECT Postgres (not the 5433 pooler) to avoid DDL session resets; the __migration_lock is acquired/released cleanly.

Post-apply verification: `npm run db:migrate:status` reports 0 pending; SUPA-001 introspection re-run confirms web_forms, email_sequences/email_sequence_enrollments, custom_field_definitions, proposals.discount_reason/share_token, proposal_line_items columns, workflow_executions dedupe index all exist.

Rehearse on a staging/restored copy before touching production.
userStories.notes:

userStories.title: Pin Node 20 in the dev loop so a wrong-version install cannot fake a broken repo
userStories.description: package.json pins engines.node "20.x" and .npmrc sets engine-strict=true, so on Node 22 `npm install` fails outright (EBADENGINE) and leaves node_modules EMPTY. Every downstream command then fails misleadingly: tsc reports only 2 tsconfig deprecation errors (it bails before typechecking), vitest is simply absent, and the repo looks catastrophically broken when it is healthy. VERIFIED 2026-07-30: this environment shipped Node 22.22.2 with an empty node_modules; installing under /opt/node20 (v20.20.2) succeeded with exit 0 and `npm run build` then passed. This single trap is the most likely source of every "everything is broken" report.
acceptanceCriteria: .nvmrc stays at 20 and is the documented entry point
A preflight check fails FAST with an explicit "use Node 20" message rather than a misleading downstream error
CONTRIBUTING/README (or CLAUDE.md) states Node 20 is mandatory at the point of first install
Verified: a clean install + npm run build succeeds on Node 20
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. Root cause of the phantom "broken repo": engine-strict turns a version mismatch into an empty dependency tree.

DONE 2026-07-30, VERIFIED (commit 4632715). Added scripts/check-node-version.mjs, wired as preinstall + npm run check:node. Dependency-free by necessity (preinstall runs before anything is installed) and reads engines.node from package.json so there is one source of truth. Verified: silent exit 0 on Node 20, exit 1 with actionable guidance on Node 22, and npm install still exits 0 with the hook in place.

BONUS FIX, more important than the guard itself: the tsc ratchet actively REWARDED a broken tree. On an empty node_modules tsc emits only tsconfig option errors, so the count was 2 against a baseline of 1067 — check-types.mjs concluded 'errors DECREASED' and exited 0, inviting someone to tighten the baseline to 2 and retire the ratchet permanently. Testing surfaced a worse variant: when tsc produces NO output the count is 0, reported as -1067, still exit 0. CI would have gone green on an unusable tree in both cases. Added three guards, each a precise signal rather than a heuristic on the count (a genuine decrease must keep working): (1) typescript absent or 'npx tsc --version' not runnable; (2) every diagnostic is config-level TS5xxx/TS6xxx, meaning tsc never built a program; (3) zero errors against a non-zero baseline, with --allow-zero as the explicit escape hatch for a real clean sweep. All three regression-tested closed, --allow-zero verified to still pass, and the real repo still reports 'holds at 1067'.

Also corrected CLAUDE.md, which told future sessions the build was broken and that type-only changes could not be build-verified — both artifacts of that same failed install. The build passes and emits a full bundle; the quoted 3577 baseline had drifted to 1067.
