Playwright specs under tests/ are excluded from vitest and still run under npm run test:e2e
mobile/ and printyx-client/ are excluded from the root vitest run
npm run test failure count drops to only genuine product failures; the 19 config-induced failures are gone
No test that was previously passing stops running (compare the passing-file list before and after)
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. This is a config bug, not 19 broken features — it is the cheapest large signal win in the repo.

DONE 2026-07-30, VERIFIED. Split by EXTENSION not directory (tests/ holds both: tests/blog-e2e-smoke.test.ts is a passing vitest test beside the Playwright specs). vitest include = server/**/*.test.ts, client/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, tests/**/*.test.ts; exclude = **/*.spec.ts, mobile/**, printyx-client/**. Result: 95->79 files collected, 26->10 failing files, 0 regressions (all 69 previously-passing files still pass, verified by diffing the JSON reporter file lists before/after).

SCOPE GREW — two extra defects found while verifying, both fixed here:
(1) THE ENTIRE E2E SUITE COLLECTED ZERO TESTS. 'npm run test:e2e' reported 'Total: 0 tests in 0 files'. Playwright aborts the whole run on ANY collection error and there were two: tests/address-books.spec.ts:18 used __dirname (package.json sets type:module, so it is undefined), and Playwright's DEFAULT testMatch also matches *.test.ts, so it loaded the vitest file and crashed on 'Cannot redefine property: Symbol($$jest-matchers-object)' — vitest's expect colliding with Playwright's. Fixed by pinning testMatch to '**/*.spec.ts' and using fileURLToPath(import.meta.url). 0 -> 882 tests in 10 files. Any prior claim of E2E coverage was false.
(2) server/tests/api-endpoints.test.ts used CommonJS require() for a .ts module, which vitest's ESM loader cannot resolve, so beforeAll threw 'Cannot find module' (the module EXISTS) and all 33 tests SILENTLY SKIPPED. Converted to dynamic import(); they now execute and correctly report needing a DB -> folded into PROD-003.

NOTE ON COUNTS: failing TESTS rose 10->39 while failing FILES fell 26->10. That is the fix working, not a regression — 33 previously-skipped tests now actually run.

userStories.title: Fix the genuine report-execution test failures (permission check ordering)
userStories.description: VERIFIED 2026-07-30: after discounting the 19 config-induced failures and the 6 DATABASE_URL collection failures, the only genuine assertion failures in the suite are in server/tests/integration/report-execution.test.ts. Two distinct defects: (1) at :337 the expected error is "Unsupported format" but the received error is "Missing required permissions" — the permission check fires BEFORE format validation, so an unsupported format is misreported as an authorization failure, which is a real API-contract bug that would mislead callers and hide input errors; (2) at :399 "should handle concurrent report executions" expects all 10 concurrent executions to succeed and they do not.
acceptanceCriteria: Validation ordering produces the correct error for an unsupported format while still refusing unauthorized callers
The concurrent-execution test passes, or the concurrency limit it exposes is fixed / documented as intended with the test updated to match
Both failures resolved without weakening the permission check
npm run test shows 0 genuine assertion failures
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. These are the ONLY real product test failures found; everything else red in the suite is runner configuration.

REFINED 2026-07-30: after PROD-002 these are confirmed as the only genuine ASSERTION failures. Two neighbours in the remaining-10 are NOT product bugs: task-scheduling needs a Claude API key, and api-endpoints needs a database (PROD-003).

COMPLETED 2026-08-01. The suite is green: 79 files, 1507 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures.

CORRECTION — the story's diagnosis was wrong on three counts, found by actually running the suite under Node 20 (the tree had node_modules EMPTY because the container defaults to Node 22; /opt/node20 is present and `export PATH=/opt/node20/bin:$PATH && npm install` is the fix, exactly as CLAUDE.md's pre-flight warns):

1. report-execution.test.ts had NINE failures, not two, and eight shared ONE root cause: MockReportEngine matched permission strings EXACTLY, ignoring the scope hierarchy the real system implements. The canonical ladder is ['own','team','location','regional','company','platform'] (enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts:702,837 and hierarchical-query-builder.ts#canAccessScope, both granting when userScopeIndex >= requiredScopeIndex). No fixture user holds a literal `_team` grant at all, so salesManager (sales.lead.view_location) was refused the team dashboard, and regionalDirector/ceo were refused reports needing `view_own` that their broader grants plainly cover. Fixed with satisfiesPermission(), which requires an exact base match and only ever widens — never narrows.

2. The "concurrency limit" at :399 does not exist. All 10 concurrent executions failed identically for the permission reason above; nothing throttles them. Fixing the permission model fixed the test, and a comment now records this so it is not re-diagnosed as concurrency.

3. The format-ordering defect is NOT a live API-contract bug. "Unsupported format" appears ONLY in this test file — there is no such string anywhere in server/ or supabase/functions/. It was a defect in the test's own mock. Fixed anyway (format is validated before the permission-gated execution: pure request shape, needs no privileges, leaks nothing, and now cannot reach data access), and ordering inside executeReport was aligned with the real requirePermission, which gates permission BEFORE minLevel.

Permission-check strength: the change only widens along the documented hierarchy, so four "Scoped Permission Boundaries" tests were added to lock the directions it must NOT travel — narrower scope must not satisfy broader, a broad scope on one resource must not satisfy another, unscoped permissions must match exactly (platform.admin.full_access must not parse as scope "access"), and the role-level gate must still fire for a caller who does hold the permission. Without these, a regression making the match symmetric would leave every other test green.

TWO MORE GENUINE FAILURES, both mis-attributed to the environment by the original story:

4. task-scheduling.test.ts did NOT need a Claude API key. Its single failure was a real product defect in calculateFallbackPriority (server/services/task-scheduling-service.ts): an already-overdue task fell into the same `daysUntilDue < 1` band as one due in 23 hours, both +30, scoring exactly 80 against an expected >80. calculateUrgency in the SAME class has always ranked overdue (100) above due-today (90), so the fallback scorer was inconsistent with its own sibling and the most urgent work never sorted above merely-due-soon work. Fixed in the PRODUCT (added a `< 0` band at +40), not the test.

5. api-endpoints.test.ts did NOT need a database. All 29 failures were one harness defect: the routers were mounted with NO auth middleware, but every handler opens with `const { tenantId } = req.user`, so the destructure threw before any handler logic ran and produced a blanket 500 that merely LOOKED like a DB outage. These routers serve in-memory fixture data and touch no database — proven by injecting a stub req.user and getting 200 with fixture rows. Added a requireAuth stand-in; 29 failures became 2 real ones:
   - POST /api/tasks/schedule accepted taskIds, validated it was an array, then ignored it and scheduled its 3 hardcoded fixtures regardless — so an empty list returned 3 tasks. Fixed in the product (filter by the requested ids).
   - GET /api/ai/health issues a real Claude completion and 500s by its own catch when the API is unreachable. This is the only genuinely credential-gated test; it is now test.skipIf(!process.env.CLAUDE_API_KEY) (the var the service actually reads) rather than reported red for a missing secret. POST /leads/analyze needs no guard — it falls back when the API is unreachable.

SEPARATE FINDING (out of scope, not fixed): server/routes/task-routes.ts is mounted NOWHERE in the app — routes-registry.ts registers ai-routes-simple and calendar-routes but never task-routes, so /api/tasks from this module is exercised only by this test. Belongs with the route-ownership/sunset work.

Verified: npm run test green; node scripts/check-types.mjs holds at 1067 (baseline 1067); npm run build passes; eslint on all four touched files is unchanged at 38 pre-existing errors (0 added); prettier applied.

MUCH WORSE THAN SCOPED. The story described 3 anon-key copies in mobile/eas.json. Reality was 6 copies of 3 DISTINCT real credentials, including a service_role key:
  - mobile/eas.json x3 (anon) — removed; EAS injects from project env vars/secrets of the same name, and mobile/src/config/index.ts already reads process.env
  - ios/.../AppConfig.swift x1 (anon) — was a #if DEBUG hardcoded fallback, directly under a comment explaining that a hardcoded fallback 'defeated key rotation'. Now reads ProcessInfo environment SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, matching how apiBaseURL already resolves API_BASE_URL, and fails closed in DEBUG with an actionable message instead of returning '' (an empty key produces confusing GoTrue 401s)
  - documents/COOLIFY_SETUP_EDGE_FUNCTIONS.md x2 (anon + SERVICE_ROLE) — the service_role key BYPASSES RLS ENTIRELY, the most privileged credential in the system

ROOT CAUSE OF THE BLIND SPOT, and the reason the docs copies survived: tools/automated-testing/check-no-secrets.ts treated EVERY .md/.markdown/.txt finding as a false positive, on the assumption docs only hold placeholders. So the guard printed 'No secrets detected' while a live service_role key sat in a committed markdown file. Narrowed that exemption with looksLikeRealJwt(): docs stay exempt for placeholder-shaped tokens (repeated-character signatures like XXXX..., ref 'your-project', payloads that do not decode), but a structurally valid JWT whose payload decodes to real claims is now reported. REGRESSION-TESTED both directions: clean tree exits 0, and re-adding the real service_role key to a .md fails with exit 1.

AC #4 (CI gate) was ALREADY satisfied — ci.yml has a blocking 'Secret scanning' step running npm run check:secrets. Which means CI was RED on main for this, as it was for the Tests job (PROD-003).

STILL REQUIRED, CANNOT BE DONE FROM THE REPO — ROTATION. All 3 credentials are in git history; deleting the lines does not un-publish them. Rotate in Supabase, especially the service_role key. CLAUDE.md notes the committed anon keys are already rotated/stale (GoTrue /auth/v1/health returns 401), which suggests the anon keys may already be dead — but that must be CONFIRMED, and it says nothing about the service_role key. userStories.title: Converge the 70 both-divergent domains where dev and prod run different code
userStories.description: VERIFIED 2026-07-30: 70 domains classify as both-divergent — an Express handler AND an edge function exist with no proxy-map entry, so dev (Express) and production (edge) execute DIFFERENT code for the same URL. This is the failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about: a change verified locally can behave differently or break in production, and the divergence is invisible until a user hits it. The count grew 59->69->70 through detection fixes (EDGE-020 taught the tool to see Router-declared routes), so these were always divergent. Highest-risk members touch money and customer data: invoices, contracts, financial, chart-of-accounts, journal-entries, leases, subscriptions, pricing, commission, leads, crm.
acceptanceCriteria: Every both-divergent domain is triaged to one of: add a crmProxies entry so dev forwards to the edge fn, retire the dead Express handler, or reconcile the two implementations
Money and customer-data domains are done first (invoices, contracts, financial, chart-of-accounts, journal-entries, leases, subscriptions, pricing, commission, leads, crm)
Field-level parity is confirmed per domain, not just route existence — a divergent response shape is worse than a 404 because pages silently render wrong or mock data
docs/route-ownership-baseline.json bothDivergent list shrinks as each is closed
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes: Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. Larger than one story — expect to split per domain group, mirroring the SUPA-021..024 convergence batches which cover part of this set. | NEW RATCHET + RBAC FINDING 2026-08-19: scripts/check-duplicate-routes.mjs + docs/duplicate-routes-baseline.json + npm run check:dup-routes, wired into ci.yml. Express matches the FIRST handler registered for a path, so when two server files register the same METHOD+path one silently wins and the other is dead code - and which one wins depends ONLY on the order of register*(app) calls in routes-registry.ts, which is invisible at both call sites. 69 duplicated paths exist today (baselined); --list names the winner for each. THE PAYOFF - 8 of the 69 have a WINNER WITH NO PERMISSION CHECK shadowing a copy that HAS one, i.e. an RBAC gate somebody deliberately wrote that never executes. Five are on real endpoints and are now fixed by adding the gate to the winner: GET /api/product-models + /api/product-models/:id (inventory.item.view), GET /api/vendors + /api/vendors/:id + /api/purchase-orders (inventory.po.view). Before this, any authenticated user in a tenant could list vendors, purchase orders and the whole product catalogue regardless of role. CRITICAL METHOD NOTE - DO NOT 'FIX' THESE BY DELETING THE UNGATED WINNER: the pairs are NOT equivalent. The winning /api/purchase-orders supports a filter=variance_gt_2x query the gated copy lacks, and the winning /api/product-models reads the MASTER catalogue via storage.browseMasterProducts (includes the Production category) while the gated copy runs a filtered tenant query with search/category/manufacturer/status params. Deleting winners would have regressed behaviour; adding the gate to the winner preserves it. Always diff the two bodies before choosing. The other 3 (customer-success health-scores/satisfaction/usage-analytics, where routes-sample-data.ts shadows routes-customer-success.ts) are left alone because BOTH sides are mock, pending the build-or-delete decision on the mock dashboards. MUTATION-TEST LESSON worth reusing on any baselined ratchet: my first version keyed the baseline on METHOD+path ALONE, so a THIRD file registering an already-duplicated path matched the existing entry and PASSED - the check silently had a hole exactly where the risk grows. The key now includes the sorted FILE SET, and both shapes (new file joining an existing duplicate; brand-new duplicate of a unique path) exit 1 and name the winner. Test a ratchet against the regression it is meant to stop, not just against a clean tree.

userStories.title: Establish a runnable production smoke check against a deployed environment
userStories.description: The entire route-parity analysis is STATICALLY derived. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the prod-404 mechanism is proven but nothing has been executed against a live deploy, and asks for one curl per prefix before treating any of it as an incident. No claim in the gap analysis has been confirmed against a running production environment: npm run check:drift exits with "DATABASE_URL is not set", and npm run audit:pages needs a live app plus browser auth and a current anon key (CLAUDE.md notes the committed anon keys are rotated/stale — GoTrue /auth/v1/health returns 401). Until one authenticated request per domain is actually made, the 29 prod 404s remain high-confidence inference rather than measured fact.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed script issues one authenticated request per /api prefix against a deployed environment and reports status per domain
The 29 statically-derived prod 404s are confirmed or corrected against a real deploy
A current anon key is available to the check (documented as a reference, never a committed value)
Output is committed as a dated summary — audit-reports/ is gitignored, so an uncommitted report does not survive
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. This is the honesty gate on the whole analysis: static parity cannot distinguish "404" from "returns 200 with the wrong shape", and CLAUDE.md flags the latter as strictly worse.

STRENGTHENED 2026-07-30: the need for this is now demonstrated rather than theoretical. A purely static audit produced one confirmed false positive out of 29 (quote-templates — an api-shaped CACHE KEY, no network call). The architecture premise itself (getApiUrl -> functions.printyx.net with no Express fallback in PROD) has now been verified by reading the code, but still not by a single real request. Static parity also cannot distinguish a 404 from a 200 carrying the wrong shape, which is the more dangerous outcome.

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 — TOOL DELIVERED, NOT YET RUN. Story stays OPEN: 2 of 4 acceptance criteria require measuring a real deploy, and this session had no egress to one. Do not close it on the strength of the script alone.

DONE:
 * AC1 (committed script, one authenticated request per /api prefix, status per domain) — scripts/prod-smoke-check.mjs, wired as `npm run smoke:prod`. Domains come from computeParity() in scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs — the SAME source the gap analysis uses — so the check cannot drift from the claims it tests. 182 live domains by default; --all widens to orphaned callers too. Flags: --base/--out/--json/--strict/--all/--concurrency/--timeout.
 * AC3 (current anon key available to the check, documented as a reference and never a committed value) — .env.example gained a "Production smoke check" block naming PRINTYX_SMOKE_TOKEN / PRINTYX_SMOKE_ANON_KEY / PRINTYX_FUNCTIONS_URL, where each comes from, and the rotation caveat. No values committed.

NOT DONE (blocked, not deferred):
 * AC2 (confirm/correct the 28 static prod 404s against a real deploy) and AC4 (commit the dated output of an actual run) — the sandbox refuses egress by policy: every CONNECT to functions.printyx.net and api.printyx.net returns 403 at the agent proxy, and https://example.com is refused identically, so there is no general egress to compare against. Nothing about production was measured, and docs/prod-smoke-2026-08-01.md states that in its first line so the artifact cannot be mistaken for results.

KEY DESIGN — WHY IT NEEDS NO CREDENTIALS: requiring auth is exactly what kept this analysis unverified (the committed anon keys are rotated/stale, 401 from GoTrue /auth/v1/health). It does not need them, because the Coolify dispatcher resolves the function from URL segment 0 BEFORE any handler runs and enforces auth PER HANDLER. So: 404 carrying {"error":"Function not found"} proves the function is NOT deployed; 401/403/2xx proves it IS. Distinguishing that marker 404 from a handler's own 404 on an unhandled sub-path is what makes the verdicts trustworthy — a status-only check would report every function that simply does not serve GET / as missing. A token is still worth supplying: it upgrades 2xx responses into evidence about RESPONSE SHAPE, the failure mode static parity cannot see and that CLAUDE.md calls strictly worse than a 404. Bonus: the marker body carries available[], so ONE request to an impossible function name enumerates every deployed function (reported as corroboration only — server.ts aliases like accounts-payable->account-payable mean a prefix can resolve while its literal name is absent from that list).

TRAP FOUND AND FIXED — READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANY SMOKE OUTPUT: the first working version REPORTED A FABRICATED CLEAN BILL OF HEALTH against the blocked host, and the run looked completely normal. The proxy answers every path with 403; a status-only classifier reads 403 as "deployed, refused auth", so all 182 domains came back exists-auth — a confident report that production was healthy, produced without one packet reaching it. ANY uniform interceptor (proxy, WAF, CDN, captive portal, login wall) produces the same lie, and its natural answers (401/403) are precisely the ones that read as fine. Fix: a HANDSHAKE — before reporting anything, probe a function name that cannot exist and require the dispatcher's marker; only server.ts emits it, so receiving it proves the far end is the real dispatcher. Without it the run aborts (exit 1) saying plainly that nothing was measured. Deliberately NO override flag: every failure mode this catches produces plausible-looking output, and "wrong but confident" is the outcome this story exists to prevent. This is the story's own thesis reproduced in miniature — worth keeping in mind for PROD-010..014, where a wrong response SHAPE fails the same way.

VERIFIED: classifier exercised against a local mock reproducing all four dispatcher response shapes (marker 404 / 401 / 200 / bare sub-path 404) — all classified correctly, including the bare 404 that must NOT read as missing. Both failure paths confirmed: handshake refuses the blocked host with exit 1, --strict exits 2 on contradicted predictions. That verifies the classifier, not production. All five ratchets still pass (check:routes, check:nav, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides, check:migrations); eslint clean; prettier applied.

TO FINISH: from any host with egress, `npm run smoke:prod -- --out docs/prod-smoke-$(date +%F).md` (add PRINTYX_SMOKE_TOKEN to also exercise shapes), then COMMIT the generated file — audit-reports/ is gitignored, so a report written there does not survive. | NEW RATCHET 2026-08-19 (from the PROD-013 documents port): scripts/check-raw-api-fetch.mjs + docs/raw-api-fetch-baseline.json + npm run check:raw-fetch, wired into ci.yml next to check:nav. A bare fetch('/api/...') in client code is broken in PRODUCTION two independent ways and works fine in dev, so local testing never catches it: (1) the relative path skips getApiUrl (client/src/lib/config.ts), which in prod rewrites /api/x to the edge-function host - a relative path instead hits whatever origin serves the static bundle; (2) credentials:'include' sends COOKIES, but edge functions authenticate with a Bearer JWT, so even a correctly-addressed call 401s. COUNT: 120 LIVE call sites (file reachable from App.tsx, a user can trigger it) plus 22 on unreachable files. That is a far wider blast radius than the one page that surfaced it and is multi-session work, so it is BASELINED to stop new ones while the existing set is worked down - shrink it, never grow it. The fix per site is apiRequest() from lib/queryClient for JSON, or a helper modelled on lib/invoice-pdf.ts for blob downloads. Detection rule: the URL argument must be a RELATIVE /api literal with only whitespace between it and the paren, so fetch(getApiUrl('/api/x')) and fetch(url) correctly do NOT report (verified against invoice-pdf.ts, quote-pdf.ts, document-export.ts). MUTATION-TESTED: reintroducing the exact raw fetch this was written for exits 1 at the right line; restoring the apiRequest call passes. This is a good candidate for a smoke-check assertion too - a prod smoke test that exercises any of these 120 sites would have caught the class years ago. | RAW-FETCH BURN-DOWN 2026-08-19, ROUND 1: live call sites 128 -> 121, baseline (deduped by file:url) 120 -> 113. THE TRIAGE RULE THAT MATTERS, learned the hard way: converting a raw fetch to apiRequest only FIXES production if the edge function actually implements that path. Otherwise you trade a wrong-origin request for a 404 and the page is just as broken, but now it LOOKS fixed. So check two things per cluster before touching it: (a) does /api/<prefix> have a crmProxies entry, and (b) does the edge fn have a branch for the specific sub-path. MEASURED TABLE of the remaining live sites by prefix, n = live sites, with proxy status: seo 17 (no proxy), subscriptions 16 (no), platform-crm 16 (PROXIED), public 9 (no), knowledge-base 9 (PROXIED), customers 8 (no), oid-mappings 7 (no), import 6 (no), integrations 5 (no), rbac 5 (no), social-media 4 (no), device-monitoring 3 (no), manufacturer-integrations 3 (no), admin 2, validate 2, then singletons (equipment, tasks, content, auth, auto-supply-replenishment, contract-renewal, leads, devices, pricing). CONVERTED THIS ROUND, both fully covered: the 7 platform-deals mutations on PlatformDealDetail + PlatformDealsPipeline (PATCH /:id, POST /:id/{move-stage,close-won,close-lost} - all four branches exist in supabase/functions/platform-deals/index.ts and the prefix is proxied) and the 5 ratings/votes sites in ArticleRatingWidget (the knowledge-base engagement dispatch covers GET /ratings/:id, GET /ratings/user/:id, POST /ratings, GET /votes/user/:id, POST /votes). CAVEAT ON THAT SECOND ONE, do not count it as a user-facing fix: client/src/components/knowledge-base/ArticleRatingWidget.tsx is imported by NOTHING - it is an orphan, so those 5 were in the ratchet's DEAD bucket and the live count did not move for them. Belongs to AUDIT-016. DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED, each because the endpoints do not exist edge-side: useSubscription's 16 sites (the subscriptions fn implements only plans + usage -> EDGE-002c); SEODashboard's 17 (the seo fn implements settings/pages/analytics/redirects/sitemap, the dashboard calls audit/crawl/content-*/images/links/mobile/performance/security/semantic/structured-data -> EDGE-002e); the 11 platform-crm assignment-rules/scoring-rules/territories sites (prefix IS proxied but platform-crm has NO branch for any of them - it only handles business-records, leads, activities, stats); and tasks/ai-schedule (absent, and its caller already swallows the failure on purpose). ALSO NOTED: the knowledge-base call sites in ArticleEditor/KnowledgeBaseAdmin use an /articles/ path segment (/api/knowledge-base/articles/:id) but the edge fn treats parts[0] as the ARTICLE ID directly, with no 'articles' segment - so those are a path-shape mismatch, not just a call-site fix. Verify that contract before converting them. | RAW-FETCH BURN-DOWN ROUND 2 (2026-08-19): baseline 111 -> 102, by fixing the knowledge-base admin cluster. WORTH READING BEFORE THE NEXT ROUND, because the pattern generalises: converting a raw fetch to apiRequest was only step THREE of three here. The KB admin pages were broken in three independent ways and only one was production-specific. (1) DEV-AND-PROD BUG: publish + archive PATCHed /api/knowledge-base/articles/:id/publish and /archive. NEITHER endpoint exists on the canonical Express router (server/routes-knowledge-base.ts) NOR the edge fn - those buttons 404'd EVERYWHERE. Fixed by routing both through PUT /articles/:id, which already accepts a status change, with changeType/changeDescription so the revision history records why. The same dead /publish call was also in ArticleEditor's save-and-publish path. (2) PATH SHAPE: the edge fn addressed articles FLAT (/ and /:id) while every caller uses /articles and /articles/:id - all of them 404'd in prod. Fixed by stripping an OPTIONAL leading `articles` segment (the EDGE-005e signatures idiom for its optional `signature-` prefix), so both shapes resolve and no caller has to change. (3) RESPONSE SHAPE: the edge list returned { data, total, page, limit } while Express returns { articles, pagination } and KnowledgeBaseAdmin reads articlesData?.articles - the table would have rendered EMPTY against a 200, the same failure mode as the platform-crm pages. The edge response now carries BOTH shapes (`data` kept as an alias) rather than swapping one for the other. Verified nothing else consumes the flat list before changing it. ALSO ADDED: a /analytics branch, which the admin dashboard calls and the edge fn never had; PostgREST has no COUNT FILTER or AVG so the tenant's articles are read once and reduced in JS rather than issuing five counts. `analytics` had to be RESERVED alongside categories/popular/search or the :id branches would treat it as an article id - watch for that whenever adding a named route to a function with a flat /:id shape. DEAD FILE FOUND: server/routes/knowledge-base-routes.ts is imported by NOTHING (the mounted one is server/routes-knowledge-base.ts, registry line 348). Do not mistake it for the canonical implementation - it has its own /analytics and /articles routes that never execute. TAKEAWAY FOR THE REMAINING 102: check whether the endpoint exists on EITHER backend before converting a call site; a 404 in dev means the fix is a feature, not a call-site change.

userStories.title: Close prod 404s: AI, analytics & predictive surfaces
userStories.description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-30 via scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs: each domain below is called by a page REACHABLE from App.tsx/main.tsx and has NO edge function, so it works in dev (Express serves it) and returns 404 in production (which hits the edge function directly). 7 of these have an Express handler that is the port source; 1 have no handler on either side and are dead in dev AND prod.

  - /api/ai -> pages/GPT5Dashboard.tsx
  - /api/ai-analytics -> pages/AIAnalyticsDashboard.tsx
  - /api/predictive-analytics -> pages/PredictiveAnalytics.tsx  [NO Express handler either]
  - /api/predictive-failure -> pages/ServicePredictions.tsx
  - /api/business-process -> pages/BusinessProcessOptimization.tsx
  - /api/daily-briefing -> pages/DailyBriefings.tsx
  - /api/churn-risk -> pages/CustomerRisk.tsx
  - /api/qbr -> pages/CustomerQbrs.tsx

The no-handler domains (predictive-analytics) need a decision first: implement the endpoint, or remove the frontend call. Do not port a handler that does not exist.

Per CLAUDE.md, porting is not just route creation: use normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>') (an edge handler NEVER sees its own name in the path — the dispatcher strips segment 0), filter every query by tenant_id, and match the RESPONSE SHAPE the page actually reads. Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404, because pages fall back to mock data with || and silently render fabricated numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: An edge function exists for every domain listed, resolving under the URL prefix the frontend already calls
Routing uses normalizePath so it behaves identically whether or not the function-name segment is present
Every query filters by tenant_id, and auth is enforced per handler
Response shape matches what the consuming page reads, verified field by field against the real Drizzle columns (not an assumed/mock shape)
Each domain is removed from the missingEdge list in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json
npm run check:edge-paths stays at 0 offenders
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL. Fixed at the source by renaming the key to 'local:quote-templates' (also more honest: there is no quote_templates table in any schema/migration), so the tool no longer classifies it. Removed from the baseline; missingEdge 39 -> 38, live prod 404s 29 -> 28. Gotcha worth knowing: the first version of the explanatory comment SPELLED OUT the api path and re-triggered the same grep — the comment now deliberately avoids the literal string.

(c) I checked the OTHER 28 for the same no-network pattern (scripted scan for a queryFn resolving from localStorage/sessionStorage near each match). quote-templates was the ONLY one. The remaining 28 are real.

(d) predictive-analytics and technician-sessions are confirmed REAL but differ from the rest: they use the DEFAULT queryFn (queryClient.ts joins the queryKey into a URL and fetches it), so they issue genuine requests — and they have NO handler in Express either, so they are broken in DEV TOO, not just prod. technician-sessions also drives mutations (check-in), so the technician ticket workflow is non-functional everywhere. Neither has a backing table (no technician_sessions, no quote_templates in any schema or migration), so these two need an implement-with-schema decision, not a port.

(e) MEASURED EFFORT for the ports, so the remaining batches are honestly scoped: the four PROD-012 handlers alone are 3,950 lines of Express (routes-voice-ticket-close 860, routes-voice-agent 825, routes-chatbot 1200, routes-email-autopilot 1065), and each exposes 4-9 endpoints. Extrapolating, the full 26-domain port is roughly 20,000 lines of Express to re-express as Deno edge functions WITH field-by-field response-shape parity. This is multi-session work and must not be rushed: per CLAUDE.md these pages fall back to mock data with '|| [...]', so a shape mismatch silently renders fabricated numbers — strictly worse than the 404 it replaces.

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 — 1 of 8 domains DONE (qbr). Story stays OPEN for the remaining 7: ai, ai-analytics, predictive-analytics, predictive-failure, business-process, daily-briefing, churn-risk.

qbr PORTED — supabase/functions/qbr/{index.ts,content.ts}, proxied via '/api/qbr' in edge-function-proxy.ts, removed from missingEdge in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json (38 -> 37; bothDivergent unchanged at 70). route-parity now classifies qbr as 'proxied', i.e. dev and prod run the SAME code — verified: registerEdgeFunctionProxy(app) runs at routes-registry.ts:345, well before registerQbrRoutes at :654, so the proxy wins in dev.

All SEVEN Express endpoints are implemented, not just the four the page calls (list, generate, GET/POST suppressions, GET/PATCH /:id, /:id/send) — the full-parity bar the existing proxy entries are held to. Proxying a prefix forwards ALL of it and falls through only on a network error, never a 404, so a partial port would have taken the unported endpoints from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev.

SHAPE (the AC that matters most — a wrong shape is worse than a 404): CustomerQbrs.tsx types QbrReport in camelCase and reads list.data/list.total. PostgREST returns snake_case, so rows convert at the boundary with toCamelShallow — deliberately SHALLOW. `content` is a jsonb column whose inner keys are ALREADY camelCase; a deep toCamel would walk into the deck payload and rewrite keys inside it, including sectionOverrides, which the review dialog round-trips. Every column name was verified against shared/schema.ts rather than assumed from the Drizzle field name — meter_readings stores black_copies/color_copies, contracts stores monthly_base, equipment stores serial_number/model_number, business_records stores company_name/assigned_sales_rep. companyName is NOT a column on qbr_reports; it is joined from business_records (the canonical company table) exactly as Express does.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE — PDF, disclosed not silent: Express renders the deck PDF with Playwright/Chromium, which CANNOT run in the Deno edge runtime. The edge fn stores the HTML artifact and leaves pdf_url NULL. This is not a new failure mode — the Express generator already treats the PDF as best-effort and saves with a null pdf_url whenever Chromium is absent, and the page already renders "Not available" for a null pdfUrl. generate returns pdfAvailable:false so the gap is visible to callers rather than only inferable from a null column. Note the real tradeoff: because /api/qbr is now proxied, DEV loses PDF generation too. That is the deliberate choice — prod has no qbr function at all today, so leaving dev on Express would keep PDFs working on developer machines while prod silently lacked them, which is exactly the works-in-dev/broken-in-prod split this batch exists to close. Restoring PDFs means rendering outside the edge runtime, for both.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/qbr-content.test.ts (14 tests) pins the ported aggregation — quarter bucketing across a year boundary, the end-bound ticket exclusion, open/closed split, top-issue frequency, the supply-cost proxy tolerating numeric strings, forecast slope + year rollover, the empty-customer case, and HTML escaping + section-override replacement. This matters because there is NO Deno in CI, so nothing else in the suite can reach the edge function, and its arithmetic IS the product behavior now that it is the only implementation that runs. Follows the quote-math.test.ts precedent. The tests were MUTATION-CHECKED rather than trusted for passing first try: swapping black_copies/color_copies fails 2, and neutering the quarter end-bound filter fails 2.

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass (check:routes, check:nav, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides, check:migrations); check:edge-paths holds at 0 offenders/177 migrated; full suite 1521 passed + 1 skipped across 80 files; check-types holds at 1067 (baseline 1067); npm run build passes; eslint adds 0 errors (the 6 in edge-function-proxy.ts are pre-existing and identical before/after); prettier applied. NOT verified against a live deploy — there is no Deno in this sandbox to typecheck the function and no egress to production (see PROD-020); run npm run smoke:prod once qbr is deployed to confirm it resolves.

SCOPE NOTE for the remaining 7: they are NOT uniform. predictive-analytics has NO Express handler either (broken in dev too) and needs an implement-or-remove decision, not a port. The other six have handlers of 421-1037 lines each. Do them one at a time with the same shape discipline — the value is in field-by-field parity, not in closing domains quickly.

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 (2) — ai-analytics PORTED; business-process DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED. 2 of 8 domains done (qbr, ai-analytics); 1 reclassified out of scope (business-process); 5 remain: ai, predictive-analytics, predictive-failure, daily-briefing, churn-risk.

ai-analytics DONE — supabase/functions/ai-analytics/{index.ts,dashboard.ts}, proxied via '/api/ai-analytics', removed from missingEdge (37 -> 36; bothDivergent still 70). Full parity: /dashboard is the ONLY endpoint Express serves on the prefix and the only one the page calls. The page (AIAnalyticsDashboard.tsx) declares a complete AiAnalyticsResponse interface and, since CRMX-001, has NO mock fallback — so a shape mismatch shows as visibly empty sections rather than fabricated numbers, and every key is reproduced exactly.

TWO PORTING SUBTLETIES worth remembering for the remaining 5:
 (a) DISTINCT ON HAS NO POSTGREST EQUIVALENT. Express used `SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id) ... ORDER BY customer_id, calculated_at DESC` to get the latest churn score per customer. The port orders newest-first and keeps the FIRST row seen per customer. Get this wrong and the dashboard shows STALE scores that look completely plausible — no error, no empty state, just wrong numbers. Pinned by a test.
 (b) jsonb INNER KEYS ARE snake_case AND MUST NOT BE CONVERTED. `signals` holds ticket_delta / suggested_parts / reasons. Rows here are hand-built in camelCase and specific fields read out of the jsonb, rather than running the row through a key converter. (Same class of trap as the toCamelShallow decision on qbr, where `content` is jsonb.)

STRUCTURE NOTE (applies to every future port): the aggregation lives in a separate dashboard.ts that takes the Supabase client as a PARAMETER and imports only its TYPE. index.ts imports _shared/supabase.ts, which pulls @supabase/supabase-js from esm.sh at RUNTIME and therefore cannot be loaded by Node — so anything left in index.ts is untestable in CI. Splitting the pure logic out is what makes the vitest coverage possible at all. qbr/content.ts has the same arrangement; do this by default.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/ai-analytics-dashboard.test.ts (13 tests) — latest-score dedupe, value-weighted ordering, jsonb reasons/suggested_parts extraction, "Unknown account" fallback, malformed-signals tolerance, open-vs-monitored prediction counts, the 25-row caps with totals still reflecting everything, per-record_type counts, and the availability map. MUTATION-CHECKED: making the dedupe keep the last row instead of the first fails 1; removing the 5-outcome accuracy floor fails 1.

business-process NOT PORTED — DECISION, not an omission. BOTH of its Express dashboard handlers (routes-business-process-optimization.ts:24 and routes-sample-data.ts:1209 — the path is registered TWICE) return entirely hardcoded numbers with ZERO database access: totalProcesses 47, automationRate 68.1, costSavings 127890.5, plus static keyMetrics/workflowTemplates arrays. They also IGNORE the category/department query params the page sends (0 req.query reads in the handler). Verified by grepping the full handler bodies for any db./sql` usage — none, though the file does import db for its other routes.

Porting that would take fabricated business metrics and publish them to production, where the page currently 404s. That is strictly worse than the 404: an error is honest, a confident "$127,890.50 saved" is not. This is precisely the failure this story's own description warns about ("Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404 ... silently render fabricated numbers") — here the BACKEND itself is the mock, so no amount of shape fidelity helps. It belongs to PA-040 ("Wire or clearly flag the fully-mock dashboards that silently render fabricated data"), and stays in missingEdge with the rationale recorded in the edge-function-proxy.ts comment block so the next person does not "fix" it by porting.

GENERAL RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: before porting a PROD-010..014 domain, check whether the Express handler actually queries anything. A mock-backed domain is a PA-040 item, not a port — and the remaining batches were scoped by handler LINE COUNT, which does not distinguish 800 lines of real queries from 800 lines of hardcoded fixtures.

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1534 passed + 1 skipped across 81 files; check-types holds at 1067; npm run build passes; eslint clean on new files; prettier applied. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here to typecheck, no egress — see PROD-020).

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 (3) — churn-risk PORTED. 3 of 8 domains done (qbr, ai-analytics, churn-risk); 1 reclassified out of scope (business-process); 4 remain: ai, predictive-analytics, predictive-failure, daily-briefing.

MOCK SCREEN FIRST (the rule from the last pass, applied): counted real db calls per remaining handler — churn-risk 17, daily-briefing 28, predictive-failure 19, routes-ai-gpt5 ZERO. The three with queries are genuine ports; routes-ai-gpt5 has no DB access at all and needs the same look business-process got before anyone ports /api/ai (it may be an AI-service wrapper rather than a mock, but that has to be checked, not assumed).

churn-risk DONE — supabase/functions/churn-risk/{index.ts,scoring.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (36 -> 35; bothDivergent still 70). All SEVEN Express endpoints implemented, which is also everything CustomerRisk.tsx calls: POST /score, GET /scores?band=, GET /scores/:customerId/history, POST /save-plan, GET+PUT /settings, POST /digest/preview.

COLUMN TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING — meter_readings has TWO pairs of volume columns and they mean different things: bw_meter_reading/color_meter_reading are the cumulative E-Automate meter values, black_copies/color_copies are period copy counts. The churn scorer averages the FORMER; the qbr port (previous pass) uses the LATTER. Both are correct for their own purpose. Picking the wrong pair changes every score with nothing failing loudly — verified each against shared/schema.ts:1841-1851 rather than inferring from the Drizzle field name.

TWO MORE QUERIES WITH NO POSTGREST EQUIVALENT (this is now a recurring theme — third and fourth instances):
 - /scores used SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id) ORDER BY calculated_at DESC -> newest-first fetch, first row per customer wins.
 - /digest/preview used ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY calculated_at DESC) to pair each customer's latest score with the previous one for the week-over-week delta -> same newest-first ordering, take ranks 1 and 2 per customer.
Both are correct ONLY because of the descending order. Lose it and the page shows stale scores and nonsense deltas with nothing erroring.

DELIBERATE FIDELITY CALL: the POST /score loop keeps Express's per-customer query fan-out (tickets x2, invoices, equipment, meters x2, contracts per customer). It is genuinely N+1, but restructuring the aggregation risks changing the numbers, and this is a weekly cron-style batch rather than a request-path read. Recorded in the code as a separate, measurable change rather than folded into a port. The one place the port DOES diverge is the write: a single batch insert instead of Express's per-row insert loop — equivalent because the table is append-only history keyed by (customer, run).

Also carried over faithfully: weights MERGE on PUT /settings (a partial edit must not reset unmentioned signals), null-not-zero for a missing week-over-week delta ("no change" and "no history" render differently), and getOrCreateSettings tolerating a concurrent creator so two dashboards opening at once do not 500.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/churn-risk-scoring.test.ts (27 tests) covering every signal's saturation point and sign, weight normalization with unnormalized and all-zero weights, band boundary inclusivity, the 0.4 reason-chip threshold from both sides, NaN/Infinity containment, and every buildSavePlan branch including the empty-company-name and no-history cases. MUTATION-CHECKED with four mutations, all caught: dropping weight normalization (1 fail), reason threshold > instead of >= (1), meter-trend sign flipped so a volume RISE reads as risk (2), band boundary made exclusive (1).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1561 passed + 1 skipped across 82 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on new files. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 (4) — predictive-failure PORTED. 4 of 8 domains done (qbr, ai-analytics, churn-risk, predictive-failure); 1 reclassified out of scope (business-process); 1 BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT DECISION (ai); 2 remain (predictive-analytics, daily-briefing).

predictive-failure DONE — supabase/functions/predictive-failure/{index.ts,scoring.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (35 -> 34; bothDivergent still 70). All EIGHT Express endpoints implemented, covering everything ServicePredictions.tsx calls: POST /score, GET /predictions?status=, POST /predictions/:id/{approve,snooze,dismiss}, GET+PUT /settings, GET /accuracy.

KILL SWITCH PRESERVED: POST /score short-circuits with { skipped:true, reason:'agent_disabled' } BEFORE any scoring or ticket creation when predictive_dispatch_settings.agent_enabled is false. This endpoint DISPATCHES TECHNICIANS — a port that quietly ignored the pause would have turned the kill switch into a no-op in production, which is worse than the 404 it replaced.

TWO BEHAVIORS I GOT WRONG ON THE FIRST PASS AND CORRECTED BY RE-READING EXPRESS (worth noting as a method point — I had written both from a plausible assumption):
 1. dismiss does NOT set outcome='false_positive'. I invented that. Express sets status='dismissed' only; the accuracy report derives outcomes from closed tickets, so writing an outcome on dismissal would have corrupted the precision numbers the page displays.
 2. dismiss ALSO cancels the linked draft ticket — but ONLY where status='pending_review'. That status guard is load-bearing: without it, dismissing a prediction whose ticket was already approved and dispatched would cancel work a technician may already be doing.
Both were caught by reading the handler rather than trusting the shape of the code around it. Assume nothing about sibling actions in these ports.

ORDERING NOTE (fifth PostgREST gap in this batch): Express sorted /predictions by the SQL expression confidence * contract_value. PostgREST cannot ORDER BY an expression, so the sort is applied in JS after mapping. Same class of fix as the DISTINCT ON and ROW_NUMBER cases in the previous passes.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/predictive-failure-scoring.test.ts (30 tests) — every signal's saturation point and floor, the >=3-reading requirement, unordered-input sorting, the zero-mean guard in the toner CV, weight-share verification, the "unknown service date alone must stay below the dispatch threshold" case (0.12 vs 0.7 — a machine with no history must not summon a technician), all suggestParts thresholds including model_age's higher bar and cross-signal dedupe, and every computeAccuracy window edge. nowMs is injected because three of five signals move with wall-clock time. MUTATION-CHECKED, all four caught: accuracy window made direction-agnostic so earlier closures earn credit (1 fail), unknown-service-date risk zeroed (2), meter rows left unsorted before differencing (1), model_age part threshold lowered (1).

/api/ai — NOT PORTED, BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT DECISION, not on effort. Screened it first per the rule from the last pass. It is NOT a mock: server/routes-ai-gpt5.ts (9 endpoints, 6 used by GPT5Dashboard.tsx) is a real pass-through to server/services/gpt5-service.ts, which calls OpenAI's gpt-5 / gpt-5-mini / gpt-5-nano via the SDK. Zero db calls because it is a provider wrapper, which is legitimate.

The blocker is that supabase/functions/_shared/openai.ts states the edge convention explicitly: "Only the embeddings endpoint is wired; if you need chat/completion, use _shared/anthropic.ts (Claude is our default)." So porting this means choosing one of:
  (a) add OpenAI chat/completion to the edge tree via fetch — faithful to current behavior, but contradicts the stated convention AND requires OPENAI_API_KEY in the edge env, which cannot be verified from here (no egress);
  (b) re-point these endpoints at Claude through _shared/anthropic.ts — follows the convention, but the page is literally GPT5Dashboard.tsx and its /gpt5/configs endpoint renders OpenAI-specific model names, reasoning-effort and verbosity settings, so the dashboard would then display configs that do not describe what actually runs;
  (c) leave it 404ing in production until someone decides.
This is a provider choice with product-visible consequences, so it should be made deliberately rather than settled by whichever option is convenient mid-port. Also note /api/ai carries a SECOND router — routes/ai-routes-simple.ts mounts /health and /leads/analyze on the same prefix — so any proxy entry has to cover those too or they go from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev.

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1591 passed + 1 skipped across 83 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on new files. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 (5) — predictive-analytics RESOLVED BY REMOVAL. Status of the 8: 4 ported (qbr, ai-analytics, churn-risk, predictive-failure), 1 reclassified to PA-040 (business-process), 1 resolved by removal (predictive-analytics), 1 blocked on a provider decision (ai), 1 remaining (daily-briefing).

predictive-analytics — the story asked for a decision, "implement the endpoint, or remove the frontend call". The evidence made it a removal, not a judgment call:
 * NO handler exists in Express OR as an edge function, so this was broken in DEV as well as prod — unlike every other domain in this batch, which are prod-only 404s.
 * NOTHING EXISTS TO SERVE. Checked every table the three endpoints would need — ml_models, training_jobs, model_performance, data_sources, predictive_insights, prediction_models — and NONE appears in any schema file or any migration. The UI was written against an imagined API with no backing store anywhere in the system.
 * Implementing would mean designing a model registry, training-job history, a data-source registry and a predictions store, with schema + migrations, before a single endpoint could be written. That is a feature, not a 404 fix, and does not belong to a story scoped to closing prod 404s.

WHAT THE PAGE WAS ACTUALLY DOING: `analyticsData` was always undefined, so the ~965-line dashboard branch was UNREACHABLE and the only thing that ever rendered was the CRMX-001 "in preview" state. Meanwhile the three queries kept polling at 60s/30s/30s — roughly five failing requests a minute for as long as the page stayed open, forever, against endpoints that exist nowhere.

CHANGE: removed the three dead queries and the unreachable dashboard; PredictiveAnalytics.tsx goes 1160 lines -> 52. The preview state users actually saw is character-for-character unchanged, so there is NO user-visible behavior change — this deletes only code that could never execute. The built chunk is now 1.25 kB (0.68 kB gzipped). The scaffold is recoverable from git history if the platform is ever built, though it was written against an assumed response shape rather than a real one, so it is a sketch and not a spec.

RATCHET EFFECT: with no frontend call remaining, predictive-analytics is no longer a route-parity DOMAIN at all — it drops out of the classification entirely rather than moving between buckets. missingEdge 34 -> 33.

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1591 passed + 1 skipped across 83 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean (also fixed an unescaped apostrophe that the original page carried).

NOTE ON THE REMAINING TWO: daily-briefing (28 db calls, real data) is a straight port like the four already done. /api/ai stays blocked on the OpenAI-vs-Claude provider decision recorded in the previous entry — it is not effort-blocked, and porting it "whichever way is convenient" is exactly what should not happen.

ASSESSMENT 2026-08-01 (6) — daily-briefing SCOPED BUT NOT STARTED. This is the last unblocked domain and it is materially bigger than the four already ported. Recording the survey so the next attempt starts from facts instead of rediscovering them; deliberately NOT begun as a partial, because a half-port here is worse than none (see the all-or-nothing constraint below).

WHY IT IS ALL-OR-NOTHING: a crmProxies entry forwards the ENTIRE prefix and falls through only on a network error, never a 404. daily-briefing has six endpoints and the page calls all six, so shipping an edge fn without POST /generate would take that button from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev. There is no useful partial: either all six land or the proxy entry cannot be added, and without the proxy entry the domain stays a prod 404 AND the new edge fn would reclassify to both-divergent, which moves debt rather than resolving it.

SURFACE (all six page-called):
  POST /generate            { date?, force?, userId?, all? } -> { generated, skippedOff, emailed, inApp }
  GET  /                    ?userId= override -> { data, total }, newest first, limit 30
  GET  /preferences         getOrCreate for the caller
  PUT  /preferences         partial update
  GET  /stats               A/B open-rate by variant + overall
  POST /:id/open            open tracking

MEASURED SCOPE: routes-daily-briefing.ts is 1037 lines and touches TEN tables — businessRecords, contracts, dailyBriefingLog, equipmentFailurePredictions, inventoryItems, proposals, renewalAutoQuotes, serviceTickets, truckStockCallbacks, users. The bulk is three role-specific assemblers (assembleOwnerData ~116 lines, assembleServiceManagerData ~111, assembleSalesRepData ~111) plus generateBriefing/buildFallback and generateBriefingForUser's delivery path. For comparison the four completed ports were 130-990 Express lines each with 1-6 tables.

DEPENDENCIES ALL HAVE EDGE EQUIVALENTS (so this is size, not a blocker): ClaudeAIService -> _shared/anthropic.ts (and Claude is the stated edge default, unlike the /api/ai OpenAI problem); sendEmail -> _shared/sendgrid.ts, which already has the simulation-mode fallback pattern; the user_notifications insert is a plain table write and the Express version already wraps it in try/catch as best-effort.

SQL FEATURES NEEDING JS EQUIVALENTS (6 raw sql`` fragments, 2 GROUP BYs) — the sixth through ninth instances of this pattern in the batch:
  * GET /stats: GROUP BY variant with count(*) and count(opened_at). PostgREST cannot express count-of-non-nulls per group; fetch rows and fold. NOTE count(opened_at) counts NON-NULL only — a naive count() would report every briefing as opened and show a 100% open rate.
  * assembleOwnerData: DISTINCT ON (customer_id) over customer_churn_scores to take each customer's LATEST band before counting at_risk. Same trap as ai-analytics and churn-risk: get it wrong and the owner briefing counts stale bands.
  * assembleServiceManagerData: lower(status) NOT IN (...) predicates, a column-to-column comparison (quantity_on_hand <= reorder_point), and GROUP BY assigned_technician_id. PostgREST cannot compare two columns — that one needs the rows fetched and filtered in JS.

INTEGRITY DETAIL WORTH PRESERVING: POST /:id/open sets opened_at ONLY where it is still null (`is null` guard) and returns firstOpen from whether a row came back. Re-opening must not overwrite the first open time, or the A/B open-rate metric this whole feature is measured on becomes meaningless. PostgREST expresses this as .is('opened_at', null) in the filter.

RECOMMENDATION: treat daily-briefing as its own unit of work rather than the tail of a batch. The four completed ports establish the pattern (pure logic in a separate module importing only the client TYPE so CI can reach it; explicit camelCase mapping; never key-convert a jsonb column; mutation-check the tests), so the risk is volume, not novelty.

PROGRESS 2026-08-02 — daily-briefing PORTED. EVERY UNBLOCKED DOMAIN IN THIS STORY IS NOW RESOLVED. Final tally of the 8: 5 PORTED (qbr, ai-analytics, churn-risk, predictive-failure, daily-briefing), 1 RECLASSIFIED to PA-040 (business-process, mock-backed), 1 RESOLVED BY REMOVAL (predictive-analytics, no backing tables anywhere), 1 BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT DECISION (ai — OpenAI vs Claude, see the earlier entry). missingEdge went 38 -> 32 across these passes.

daily-briefing DONE — supabase/functions/daily-briefing/{index.ts,briefing.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (33 -> 32). All SIX Express endpoints shipped together as the assessment required.

TWO REAL BUGS CAUGHT BY VERIFYING THE SHARED HELPERS INSTEAD OF ASSUMING THEIR SHAPE — both would have been silent:
 1. _shared sendEmail returns { messageId, simulated? } and THROWS on failure. There is NO `success` field. A direct transcription of the Express line (`emailSent = !!result?.success`) reads undefined and would have recorded email_sent=false for EVERY briefing ever sent, quietly zeroing the delivery counts the page shows.
 2. That same SendArgs makes `from` REQUIRED. The Express signature did not, so the transcribed call was missing it. Added BRIEFING_FROM_EMAIL with the env-with-default idiom public-booking already uses.
Also corrected mid-port: a first pass at reading the proposals columns reported assigned_to and updated_at as ABSENT, which would have been alarming — it was my grep window truncating the table definition, not a real gap. Widening it confirmed both columns exist. Worth remembering that a "column not found" result from a bounded text search is not evidence of absence.

TWO DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES, disclosed in the file header rather than silent:
 * The briefing email now HTML-ESCAPES subject and bullets. Express interpolated them raw, and these strings carry user-controlled data — proposal TITLES flow into metric labels, which flow into bullets — so an apostrophe in a deal name breaks the markup and a crafted one injects into an outbound email. Escaping changes nothing about legitimate content.
 * email_sent is recorded only when the message actually left. `simulated: true` means SENDGRID_API_KEY is unset and nothing was sent; counting it as delivered would inflate the numbers the page displays.

FOUR CONSTRUCTS POSTGREST COULD NOT EXPRESS (running total for the batch: nine):
 * GROUP BY variant with count(*) and count(opened_at) for /stats. count(opened_at) is NON-NULLS ONLY — a naive count would report a 100% open rate on the exact metric this feature is judged by.
 * DISTINCT ON (customer_id) for the owner's at-risk count (latest band per customer).
 * lower(status) NOT IN (...) for open tickets — no lower() in PostgREST filters.
 * quantity_on_hand <= reorder_point — a COLUMN-TO-COLUMN comparison PostgREST cannot do at all; rows must be fetched and compared in JS.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/daily-briefing.test.ts (21 tests) covering all three role assemblers, the empty-tenant and empty-section paths, the renewals itemisation, both A/B prompt variants including the anti-hallucination instruction, and every parseAiBriefing rejection case (no JSON, malformed JSON, missing/empty bullets, wrong types, mixed-type arrays) — that parser is the seam where a bad model reply could put broken content into a customer email. MUTATION-CHECKED, all three PostgREST re-implementations caught: churn dedupe keeping the last row (1 fail), reorder comparison made strict-less (1), closed-status matching made case-sensitive (3). NOTE: the case-sensitivity mutation initially "passed" because the sed was a NO-OP; re-running it properly after checking whether the file actually changed is what surfaced the real result. A passing mutation test is only evidence if the mutation actually applied.

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1612 passed + 1 skipped across 84 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

TO CLOSE THIS STORY: only /api/ai remains, and it needs a provider decision (not effort). Once that is made and ported, every AC here is met except the live-deploy confirmation, which is PROD-020's job. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 - closed one live prod 404 and found it was hiding a second, worse bug. /api/universal-search (the command palette's global search) had NO edge function, so global search 404'd in production; check:routes had been FAILING ON MAIN for it. Added supabase/functions/universal-search/ (7 entity groups, same relevance scores and same flat sorted array the palette consumes) + a crmProxies entry so dev exercises the edge path. Dir name == URL segment, so no server.ts override was needed. WHAT THE 404 WAS HIDING: server/routes-universal-search.ts, the dev-side implementation, was written against table shapes that DO NOT EXIST - the deals branch selected deals.name/value/stage and joined deals.business_record_id, while the real columns (migration 0000) are title/amount/stage_id/customer_id. That branch is not try/caught, so it 500'd the WHOLE endpoint. Same drift in three more places: business_records.estimated_value is really estimated_deal_value (Drizzle prop estimatedAmount); business_record_activities has subject/activity_type/description, not title/type/notes, and has NO status column (outcome is the nearest real field); quotes joins through customer_id like its invoice and equipment siblings. So search was broken on BOTH backends - 500 in dev, 404 in prod - and the prod 404 masked the dev 500. Repairing it dropped 12 tsc errors (ratchet 1058 -> 1046). PostgREST caveat for the edge port: it cannot filter across an embed the way the Drizzle joins did, so entities hanging off customer_id match on account name via the ids the business_records query already returns, and the or-filter term is sanitized (PostgREST's or() grammar is comma/paren delimited and unescapable). Also fixed the CR-029 cache tests, which asserted 6 queries after COP-I05 added a 7th entity (contracts) - both had been failing. NOT VERIFIED: deno is not installed in this environment, so the edge function is not deno-checked and nothing was executed against a deploy; confirm with one curl before treating this as closed. 16 grandfathered missing-edge routes remain LIVE prod 404s per check:routes.

AI-001 (2026-08-19) - /api/ai IS CLOSED. 1 of the 8 domains done; live prod-404 domains repo-wide 7 -> 6.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN, in two independent ways:

(1) PROD 404 on every button of /gpt5-dashboard. The page calls /api/ai/gpt5/{analyze-lead,generate-proposal,analyze-service,classify-inquiry,custom-prompt,configs}. getApiUrl rewrites that to functions.printyx.net/ai/gpt5/..., the dispatcher resolves segment 0 = 'ai', and no 'ai' function directory exists. Fixed with supabase/functions/ai-gpt5/ + a server.ts alias (functionName === 'ai' && subPath[0] === 'gpt5' -> 'ai-gpt5', stripSegments stays 1) + a dev proxy entry '/api/ai/gpt5': { fn: 'ai-gpt5', pathPrefix: '/gpt5' } so dev and prod run one code path. Only the gpt5 sub-path is proxied; the rest of /api/ai (ai-routes-simple) stays on Express, which is safe because nothing in the frontend calls it.

(2) A DEV BUG THE PORT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE COPIED. server/services/gpt5-service.ts read the model output as `response.output?.content || ''`. In the OpenAI Responses API `output` is an ARRAY of output items (reasoning items included), not an object with a `.content` string - so that expression is ALWAYS undefined and every one of the 8 endpoints returned an empty analysis / proposal / classification even when the API call succeeded and was billed. Confirmed against the installed SDK types: node_modules/openai/resources/responses/responses.d.ts declares `output: Array<ResponseOutputItem>` and a separate flattened `output_text: string`. Replaced with extractResponseText(), which prefers output_text (the SDK adds it; the raw REST payload the edge function receives does NOT carry it) and otherwise walks the array, skipping reasoning items and concatenating text chunks. So the dashboard rendered blank in dev and 404'd in prod; both are fixed.

PARITY LOCK. server/tests/unit/gpt5-prompts-parity.test.ts (42 tests) imports the Node service and the Deno copies and asserts identical output for all 7 prompt builders, the model configs, the config descriptions, the request body and the response parser. supabase/functions/_shared/crisis-response.ts is a new Deno copy of server/lib/crisis-response.ts (the LEGAL-012 guardrail the support-response prompt carries) and is locked by the same suite. Mutation-tested three ways: a one-word prompt edit in one copy -> 1 failure; disabling a branch of the array walk -> 3 failures; changing 911 to 999 in the Node crisis directive -> 3 failures.

GUARD IMPROVEMENT, not just a baseline edit. scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs matched proxy prefixes with /'\/api\/([a-z0-9-]+)'/ - single segment only - so multi-segment entries ('/api/ai/gpt5', '/api/public/calculator') were invisible and their domains stayed classified missing-edge. Rather than hand-waving 'ai' into PROXY_REDIRECTS (which would have silently absolved a future unproxied /api/ai/<other> call), the script now captures multi-segment prefixes separately, records the full live frontend path per domain, and credits a domain as aligned ONLY when every path a REACHABLE page calls sits under a proxied sub-prefix. Mutation-tested: adding a live '/api/ai/not-proxied' string to GPT5Dashboard.tsx flips the live-404 count straight back from 6 to 7.

DEPLOY PREREQUISITE, and it is load-bearing: the edge function reads OPENAI_API_KEY from Deno.env. That variable exists in the Express .env; whether it is set in the edge environment was NOT verifiable from this container. If it is missing the endpoints return 500 {"error":"OpenAI API key not configured"} - and because dev now proxies to the same function, dev will say so too rather than quietly working. That is deliberate: a dev-only success would hide a prod-only failure. Set it before treating this as shipped.

STILL OPEN in PROD-010: ai-analytics, predictive-analytics (no handler on either side - still needs the implement-or-delete decision), predictive-failure, business-process, daily-briefing, churn-risk, qbr. business-process is one of the fabricated-data mock dashboards flagged for a delete-or-build decision; porting a mock to prod would ship fake numbers, so it is deliberately not in this pass.

userStories.title: Close prod 404s: service, field & inventory surfaces
userStories.description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-30 via scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs: each domain below is called by a page REACHABLE from App.tsx/main.tsx and has NO edge function, so it works in dev (Express serves it) and returns 404 in production (which hits the edge function directly). 6 of these have an Express handler that is the port source; 1 have no handler on either side and are dead in dev AND prod.

  - /api/service -> pages/KnowledgeSearch.tsx + pages/ProactiveServiceDashboard.tsx
  - /api/meter-reads -> pages/MeterReadReview.tsx
  - /api/technician-sessions -> components/service/TechnicianTicketWorkflow.tsx  [NO Express handler either]
  - /api/truck-stock -> pages/TruckStocking.tsx
  - /api/toner-replenish -> pages/TonerReplenish.tsx
  - /api/portal-service -> pages/CustomerPortalService.tsx
  - /api/incident-response -> pages/IncidentResponseSystem.tsx

The no-handler domains (technician-sessions) need a decision first: implement the endpoint, or remove the frontend call. Do not port a handler that does not exist.

Per CLAUDE.md, porting is not just route creation: use normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>') (an edge handler NEVER sees its own name in the path — the dispatcher strips segment 0), filter every query by tenant_id, and match the RESPONSE SHAPE the page actually reads. Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404, because pages fall back to mock data with || and silently render fabricated numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: An edge function exists for every domain listed, resolving under the URL prefix the frontend already calls
Routing uses normalizePath so it behaves identically whether or not the function-name segment is present
Every query filters by tenant_id, and auth is enforced per handler
Response shape matches what the consuming page reads, verified field by field against the real Drizzle columns (not an assumed/mock shape)
Each domain is removed from the missingEdge list in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json
npm run check:edge-paths stays at 0 offenders
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL. Fixed at the source by renaming the key to 'local:quote-templates' (also more honest: there is no quote_templates table in any schema/migration), so the tool no longer classifies it. Removed from the baseline; missingEdge 39 -> 38, live prod 404s 29 -> 28. Gotcha worth knowing: the first version of the explanatory comment SPELLED OUT the api path and re-triggered the same grep — the comment now deliberately avoids the literal string.

(c) I checked the OTHER 28 for the same no-network pattern (scripted scan for a queryFn resolving from localStorage/sessionStorage near each match). quote-templates was the ONLY one. The remaining 28 are real.

(d) predictive-analytics and technician-sessions are confirmed REAL but differ from the rest: they use the DEFAULT queryFn (queryClient.ts joins the queryKey into a URL and fetches it), so they issue genuine requests — and they have NO handler in Express either, so they are broken in DEV TOO, not just prod. technician-sessions also drives mutations (check-in), so the technician ticket workflow is non-functional everywhere. Neither has a backing table (no technician_sessions, no quote_templates in any schema or migration), so these two need an implement-with-schema decision, not a port.

(e) MEASURED EFFORT for the ports, so the remaining batches are honestly scoped: the four PROD-012 handlers alone are 3,950 lines of Express (routes-voice-ticket-close 860, routes-voice-agent 825, routes-chatbot 1200, routes-email-autopilot 1065), and each exposes 4-9 endpoints. Extrapolating, the full 26-domain port is roughly 20,000 lines of Express to re-express as Deno edge functions WITH field-by-field response-shape parity. This is multi-session work and must not be rushed: per CLAUDE.md these pages fall back to mock data with '|| [...]', so a shape mismatch silently renders fabricated numbers — strictly worse than the 404 it replaces.

PROGRESS 2026-08-02 — portal-service PORTED; incident-response RECLASSIFIED to PA-040. 1 of 7 ported, 1 reclassified out of scope, 1 needs an implement-or-remove decision, 4 remain.

MOCK SCREEN FIRST (the rule established in PROD-010 — count real db calls before porting anything). Results for all seven:
  routes-service-knowledge.ts          14 db calls / 719 lines   REAL
  routes-proactive-maintenance.ts       3 db calls / 255 lines   REAL   (also serves /api/service)
  routes-meter-read-vision.ts          19 db calls / 964 lines   REAL
  routes-truck-stock.ts                22 db calls / 812 lines   REAL
  routes-toner-replenish.ts            24 db calls / 899 lines   REAL
  routes-portal-service.ts             10 db calls / 713 lines   REAL  <- ported
  routes-incident-response.ts           0 db calls / 677 lines   MOCK  <- reclassified
NOTE /api/service has TWO Express handlers (service-knowledge + proactive-maintenance), so porting it means covering both — 25 endpoints across 12 frontend paths, the largest in this batch.

incident-response NOT PORTED — same call as business-process in PROD-010, and a sharper one. routes-incident-response.ts imports db but NEVER queries it: all three endpoints return hardcoded payloads (activeIncidents 7, criticalIncidents 1, avgResponseTime 12.5, mttr 3.8, slaCompliance 94.7, incident ids like 'INC-2025-007'). Verified zero db./sql`/storage. usage across all 677 lines. This is an INCIDENT RESPONSE dashboard: publishing fabricated incident counts and SLA compliance to production would let an operator believe they have 7 live incidents at 94.7% SLA when the system knows nothing at all. Strictly worse than the 404 it would replace. Belongs to PA-040 (wire or clearly flag the fully-mock dashboards).

portal-service DONE — supabase/functions/portal-service/{index.ts,classify.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (22 -> 21). All FOUR Express endpoints (classify, classifications/:requestId, rate, timeline/:requestId), which is everything CustomerPortalService.tsx calls.

A REAL DEFECT FOUND IN THE SHIPPED CLASSIFIER, ported faithfully and pinned by a test rather than silently fixed: print_quality's pattern contains the bare word `line`, and "offLINE" contains it. print_quality is checked BEFORE connectivity, so ANY text containing "offline" — the single most common way a customer reports a connectivity fault — is classified as a print-quality defect. Consequence: priority medium instead of high, and the technician is dispatched with a drum unit and transfer belt instead of a NIC. Confirmed by running the actual regex against four phrasings. NOT fixed here because this is a prod-404 port and changing which category a customer's issue lands in is a behavior change beyond that scope; the fix is a word-boundary pattern (\blines?\b) which needs review against the other rules. The test asserts the CURRENT (wrong) behavior with a KNOWN DEFECT banner, so a future fix shows up as an intentional test change rather than a surprise regression.

TWO DEGRADATION PATHS PRESERVED EXACTLY, because both are load-bearing:
 1. Classification ALWAYS returns — the AI call is best-effort and any failure falls through to the rule classifier. A customer describing a grinding noise must never get an empty playbook because a model was down.
 2. Dispatch is best-effort and SEPARATE — ticket creation, the status flip to 'assigned' and the history row are wrapped so a MISSING TABLE/COLUMN/ENUM (a partially-migrated tenant) degrades to dispatch:'skipped' while the customer still gets their classification. Any OTHER error still propagates: I deliberately kept isMissingTableOrTypeError narrow, because widening it to swallow e.g. a unique or FK violation would lose a service ticket with a successful-looking response. A mutation adding 23505 to that check fails a test.

ORDERING DETAIL: the timeline history query must be ASCENDING. reachedAtFromHistory keeps the FIRST timestamp per step, which is only the earliest if rows arrive oldest-first. Also preserved: a COMPLETED request marks its reached step 'done', not 'current' (otherwise "Resolved" renders as forever-in-progress), and a CANCELLED request leaves every step 'pending'.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/portal-service-classify.test.ts (25 tests) — every rule family, first-match ordering (which is behavior, not decoration: "grinding noise and the paper jams" must be mechanical_noise), the general fallthrough, all three coercers including the empty-playbook and 5-part cap cases, every parseAiClassification rejection and field-by-field fallback, confidence clamping and the 0.7-not-0.4 default, the enum priority mapping, the missing-table predicate INCLUDING the codes it must NOT swallow, and all four timeline behaviors. MUTATION-CHECKED, all four caught: completed-step marked current (1 fail), empty playbook steps accepted (1), 23505 added to the missing-table check (1), confidence default changed to 0.4 (1).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1637 passed + 1 skipped across 85 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on new files. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

REMAINING: technician-sessions still needs the implement-or-remove decision the story flags (no handler on either side, so it is broken in dev too — same situation as predictive-analytics in PROD-010, which resolved to removal once it turned out no backing tables existed). Then service (largest: 2 handlers, 25 endpoints), meter-reads, truck-stock, toner-replenish.

PROGRESS 2026-08-07 — technician-sessions PORTED, and the story's own diagnosis of it was wrong. 2 of 7 ported, 1 reclassified out of scope, 4 remain.
