THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES. docs/supabase-remediation.md and PRODUCTION-GAPS both record technician-sessions as "NO Express · NO edge fn · gate/remove", i.e. the predictive-analytics case: nothing behind it, so delete the caller. That is not what is there.
  - Express DOES serve it. server/routes-enhanced-service.ts (mounted at /api by routes-registry.ts:587) has GET /api/technician-sessions/:sessionId/workflow-steps and POST /api/technician-sessions/:sessionId/update-step.
  - The tables DO exist: technician_ticket_sessions and workflow_steps, both in shared/enhanced-service-schema.ts. This is the opposite of predictive-analytics, where the absence of any backing table is what settled the decision.
So the resolution is a PORT, not a removal. Worth stating plainly because "no handler on either side" was the premise the remove option rested on, and it does not hold.

WHY THE WORKFLOW WAS NON-FUNCTIONAL ANYWAY — and it was broken in DEV, not just prod. TechnicianTicketWorkflow.tsx calls four URLs; three of them had never existed on either side:
  GET  /api/technician-sessions/:ticketId                    no such Express route (Express spells this /api/service-tickets/:ticketId/session)
  GET  /api/technician-sessions/:sessionId/workflow-steps    the ONE that matched
  POST /api/technician-sessions/:sessionId/complete-step     Express calls it update-step
  POST /api/service-tickets/:ticketId/check-in               404 in prod (the service-tickets edge fn has no check-in branch) AND 500 in dev, because Express reads the technician from an x-user-id header the client never sends and technician_id is NOT NULL
That is why nobody noticed the prod 404: the feature could not start in dev either. Three further defects on top, each of which alone would have kept progress from persisting: the page read sessionData.sessionId from a response whose id is 'id' (so sessionId stayed null and every later POST went to .../null/complete-step); it typed workflow steps as {stepCompleted?: boolean} while Express returns raw snake_case rows, so the completed list was always empty; and Express's update-step, when a step had no row yet, INSERTED it with step_completed NULL — completing a step it had never started left it incomplete forever.

PORTED — supabase/functions/technician-sessions/{index.ts,sessions.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (21 -> 20). Four endpoints, serving the shape the PAGE calls rather than the shape Express happened to have (the EDGE-005a rule: the frontend's URLs are the contract):
  POST /:ticketId/check-in            start or RESUME a visit
  GET  /:ticketId                     the open session for this ticket + technician
  GET  /:sessionId/workflow-steps     Express parity
  POST /:sessionId/complete-step      advance the guided workflow

CHECK-IN MOVED PREFIX, deliberately. It is the first action of this workflow and /api/service-tickets is not proxied, so leaving it there would split one feature across two functions with different deploy paths. Nothing regresses — that URL was already dead in both environments (above). The alternative, adding a check-in branch to the service-tickets edge fn, was written and then backed out: it left dev on the broken Express handler while prod used the new one, i.e. the same two-implementations-one-feature problem this program exists to remove.

complete-step HAS NO SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR TO PRESERVE, so the insert-incomplete quirk is fixed rather than pinned. Express's update-step has ZERO callers anywhere in the repo (grepped client/, server/, supabase/, tests/) — no user has ever hit that path, so there is nothing to be faithful to and the endpoint's name is the only spec available. A step with no row is now inserted already completed. Called out because it is a deliberate divergence, and it is the opposite call from portal-service's offline-misclassification, which WAS pinned: that one had real traffic behind it.

TENANT SCOPING IS TIGHTER THAN EXPRESS. The Express session lookup and both step/session updates filter on serviceTicketId / technicianId / sessionId but NOT on tenantId. Every query in the edge fn is tenant-scoped per the repo rule. This can only narrow what a caller can reach.

REMOVED the Express update-step route (84 lines): zero callers, superseded by a differently-named endpoint, and shadowed by the proxy in dev — keeping it would be dead code under a misleading name. The workflow-steps route stays; it is genuine parity and the proxy simply takes precedence.

FRONTEND FIXES, all forced by the port: sessionData.sessionId -> .id; the check-in URL; stepCompleted retyped as the timestamp it actually is; and an existing session now counts as check_in complete, so a technician who reloads mid-visit is not sent back to a check-in they already did.

A TEST CAUGHT A BUG IN MY OWN CODE before it shipped: isKnownStepName used `stepName in STEP_TICKET_STATUS`, which is true for 'toString' and 'constructor' — a step by that name would have resolved to an inherited Object member and been written into service_tickets.status as a function. Now hasOwnProperty.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/technician-sessions.test.ts (28 tests) — the full step->status map with the completion=completed case called out on its own (a regression there leaves finished visits open forever and they never reach billing), the unknown-step fallback, prototype-pollution rejection, both camelCase mappers including total_duration_minutes -> totalDuration (a wrong key here bills every visit at 1 hour), the no-snake_case-keys invariant, jsonb pass-through on parts_used_ids and step_data, false-vs-null on the booleans, completedStepNames, and both input parsers including out-of-range coordinates and the keep-free-text-verbatim case. MUTATION-CHECKED, all five caught and each verified to have actually applied: completion->in-progress (2 fail), total_duration_minutes->total_duration (1), GPS range guard removed (1), hasOwnProperty->in (1), completedStepNames drops the timestamp check (1).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1665 passed + 1 skipped across 86 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint on the touched files went 31 -> 29 errors (all pre-existing, 2 removed with the dead route). NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

REMAINING: service (largest: 2 handlers, 25 endpoints across 12 frontend paths), meter-reads, truck-stock, toner-replenish.

PROGRESS 2026-08-07 (2) — service PORTED. 3 of 7 ported, 1 reclassified out of scope, 3 remain (meter-reads, truck-stock, toner-replenish).

CORRECTING MY OWN EARLIER COUNT: the previous two notes called service "25 endpoints across 12 frontend paths". That was wrong — it is EIGHT endpoints across TWO frontend pages. The inflated figure came from counting every route in routes-enhanced-service.ts, which is a different prefix (/api/service-tickets, /api/phone-in-tickets), not /api/service. Confirmed by grepping for handlers under the prefix: only routes-service-knowledge.ts (6) and routes-proactive-maintenance.ts (2) serve /api/service/*, and only KnowledgeSearch.tsx and ProactiveServiceDashboard.tsx call it. The "largest in the batch" framing I carried for two iterations was an artefact of that miscount.

PORTED — supabase/functions/service/{index.ts,knowledge.ts,maintenance.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (20 -> 19). All eight:
  POST /knowledge-search · /knowledge-search/backfill · /knowledge-search/embed/:ticketId
  GET  /knowledge-search/stats · /knowledge-search/settings · PUT /knowledge-search/settings
  GET  /proactive-maintenance · POST /proactive-maintenance/:equipmentId/schedule
Both routers had to ship together — one proxy entry forwards the whole prefix, so porting one router would have taken the other from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev. Verified nothing else serves /api/service/*, and that app.use('/api/service') matches on segment boundaries so /api/service-tickets keeps its own function.

THE EMBEDDING FALLBACK IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS CARRIED OVER BYTE-FOR-BYTE. _shared/openai.ts already exists and wraps text-embedding-3-small, but it returns NULL when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset, and passing that straight through would make every knowledge search return empty. Express's deterministic hash embedding (31-multiplier string hash -> 1536-bucket histogram -> L2 normalise) is reproduced exactly, for two reasons: keyless search keeps working, and — the one that would have been silent — vectors ALREADY STORED by the Express fallback path stay comparable to vectors produced here. A "cleaner" hash would have left every existing fallback embedding unmatchable with no error anywhere. Pinned by fixed hash values in the tests, and the Express cosineSimilarity is imported and compared against directly.

GET /proactive-maintenance IS A REPAIR, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION — it has NEVER run, in either environment. Its SELECT names equipment.current_meter_reading and equipment.status; the real columns are (nothing) and equipment_status, so the query throws and the endpoint 500s on every call. ProactiveServiceDashboard.tsx has therefore never displayed real data. Porting it verbatim would have shipped a 500 to production. Fixed the status column; matched 'active' case-insensitively since the column is free-text varchar with no enum behind it.

THE METER FACTOR IS DROPPED, NOT FAKED. The health formula penalised readings over a 50,000-page PM interval, but there is no meter column on equipment and no equivalent: meter_readings stores bw and colour separately, so "the" reading is bw, colour or their sum — three different health scores, and choosing is a product decision (the Express file's own comment says exactly this and declines it too). So health is computed from service dates alone and meterReading is reported as NULL, not 0. Zero would render as a brand-new machine; null says "not known". Cost of the omission: nil — the dashboard never renders meterReading or recommendedPages, they only existed in its TS interface, which is now corrected to match.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED: ProactiveServiceDashboard's "Schedule Service" button does NOT call the schedule endpoint. handleScheduleService awaits a setTimeout(1000), console.logs, and refetches — it shows a spinner and reports success while doing nothing. The POST endpoint is real and is ported, so the wiring exists on the server side; the button is not wired because doing it properly needs a date picker (the endpoint takes scheduledDate, and defaulting it would create dateless PM tickets). Logged here rather than half-done — a button that silently does nothing is a UX bug of the same family as the mock dashboards in PA-040.

POSTGREST GAPS (running count now 10+): the model-proxy INNER JOIN through equipment.model_number cannot be expressed, so it is two queries — the tenant's equipment ids for that model, then their tickets — which is equivalent and short-circuits when the model has no equipment. Stats switched from loading every row to count:'exact',head:true plus one ordered row for lastEmbeddedAt. sha256 moved from node:crypto to Web Crypto, which makes it async.

TESTED: 76 tests across server/tests/unit/service-knowledge.test.ts (50) and service-maintenance.test.ts (26) — the hash/embedding invariants (dimension, L2 norm, case-insensitivity, all-zero on empty, near-beats-far), cosine agreement with the Express export on five vector pairs including the degenerate ones, error-code extraction and dedup, content assembly and its 8000-cap, ranking (order, limit, and that unvectored rows are DROPPED not scored 0), relevance clamping, both proxy metrics including the denominator choice and negative-duration handling, full input validation, backfill clamping, opt-in strictness, and every maintenance boundary. MUTATION-CHECKED, 9 mutations, all caught after one round of strengthening: hash multiplier 31->33 (1 fail), unvectored rows kept (1), fixSuccessRate denominator -> timed subset (3), negative durations clamped instead of dropped (1), opt-in Boolean() instead of ===true (1), due-today reclassified urgent (1), overdue cap 50->500 (1), meterReading 0 instead of null (1), never-serviced sentinel 9999->0 (initially SURVIVED — the test asserted against the constant itself, which is circular; replaced with the literal value plus an assertion that it saturates the penalty, and it now fails 2).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1741 passed + 1 skipped across 88 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on the new files (the 3 remaining in ProactiveServiceDashboard.tsx are pre-existing, at lines I did not touch). NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

PROGRESS 2026-08-07 (3) — meter-reads PORTED. 4 of 7 ported, 1 reclassified out of scope, 2 remain (truck-stock, toner-replenish).

PORTED — supabase/functions/meter-reads/{index.ts,vision.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (19 -> 18). All EIGHT Express endpoints (inbound, submit, submissions list, submissions/:id, :id/approve, :id/reject, GET/PUT settings), which is everything MeterReadReview.tsx calls. Confirmed no other Express router serves /api/meter-reads/*.

THIS PIPELINE WRITES BILLING ROWS, so the failure modes carry more weight than the usual port and three are preserved exactly:
 1. A FALLBACK EXTRACTION IS NEVER AUTO-BILLED. With no ANTHROPIC key, or on any vision failure, the counters come back as zeros marked 'fallback', and computeValidation flags on that ALONE — independent of whether the numbers look plausible. Without that check a keyless deployment auto-bills every customer a meter read of 0. It is the single most load-bearing line in the file and has its own test plus its own mutation.
 2. THE BILLABLE INSERT IS TOLERATED SEPARATELY from the submission. If meter_readings rejects the row, auto-approve degrades to 'flagged' and reviewer-approve still records the approval with a note. The submission is never lost because billing was unavailable — losing it would send the reviewer back to re-review the same photo.
 3. IDENTICAL IMAGES REUSE THE PRIOR EXTRACTION, keyed on SHA-256 of the image. That is cost control, not caching: a customer re-sending the same photo must not trigger a second paid vision call.

TWO DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES, both argued rather than assumed:
 (a) TWILIO CREDENTIALS NOW GO THROUGH THE REAL VAULT. Express called obfuscateCredential() — base64 — and stored the result in a jsonb column named encryptedConfig, with its own TODO(vault) admitting the gap. Base64 is not encryption: an auth token stored that way is plaintext to anyone with row access. The edge tree has supabase/functions/_shared/credential-vault.ts (AES-256-GCM), which is the documented house pattern for edge functions, so the port uses it. Writing NEW code that stores a live auth token reversibly under a field named encrypted_config is not a port worth doing. Two consequences handled: the vault THROWS when its master key is unset (which is exactly why Express avoided it), so that is surfaced as a 503 naming PRINTYX_CREDENTIAL_VAULT_KEY as a reference — and only when a credential is actually supplied, so template/threshold edits still save on a keyless deployment; and credSetMarkers accepts BOTH the new envelope ({blob,v}) and the legacy base64 string, so already-configured tenants keep reporting "configured" across the format change.
 (b) AN AMBIGUOUS PHONE MATCH RESOLVES TO NOBODY. Express did candidates.find(...) and took the first hit on a last-10-digits match. Two business records sharing a number is ordinary in this data (a parent company and a site), and attributing a meter read to the wrong one bills the wrong company. Now: exactly one hit resolves, zero or many resolve to null, which routes the submission to the review queue with the clarification message — the outcome the queue exists for.

DATA-CONTRACT FIX (the EDGE-005a lesson again): MeterReadReview.tsx reads camelCase straight off the response — validationStatus, extractedValues.black, rawImageUrl, submittedAt, and data.submission.validationStatus from the submit mutation. Express returns Drizzle rows, which are already camelCase; PostgREST returns snake_case. Returning raw rows would have rendered an EMPTY review queue with no error. Added toCamelSubmission and applied it to every path that returns a submission (list, single, approve, reject, and the object nested inside inbound/submit). extracted_values and validation_detail are jsonb and pass through untouched.

PERFORMANCE FIX, incidental but real: Express's enrich() selected the tenant's ENTIRE equipment and business_records tables on every review-queue load and then filtered in JS — correct, but a 500-row queue read two whole tables. Now filtered by the ids actually referenced.

SHARED HELPER WIDENED: _shared/anthropic.ts typed ClaudeMessage.content as string, which cannot express an image block. Widened to string | ClaudeContentBlock[]; the helper already passes messages straight into the request body, so this is a type-only change with no runtime effect on the ~40 existing callers.

STILL STUBBED, as in Express and flagged as such: outbound SMS is recorded on the submission but not sent, and POST /inbound trusts the authenticated tenant instead of verifying a Twilio signature. Both are pre-existing TODOs, not new gaps.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/meter-reads-vision.test.ts (60 tests) — vision-reply parsing including negative/fractional/string counters and the confidence clamp, rolling stats including the newest-first ordering assumption and null handling, every validation branch with its boundary (delta exactly at the multiplier passes; the fallback check fires regardless of the numbers; a first-ever read auto-approves; zero rolling average does not divide), template rendering including unknown-token and prototype-pollution cases, phone matching including the ambiguity rule, credential markers in both storage formats and the invariant that they never leak a value, settings projection, the camelCase mapper, and all four input parsers including the empty-template-allowed / empty-credential-rejected asymmetry. MUTATION-CHECKED, 11 mutations, all caught: fallback no longer flags (1 fail), counters not floored at 0 (1), rollingStats takes the last row (3), nulls counted as 0 (2), ambiguous phone takes the first hit (1), delta bound inclusive (1), confidence default 0.5->1 (1), unknown tokens blanked (2), empty credential allowed (2), unknown status passed through (1), legacy base64 marker ignored (1).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1801 passed + 1 skipped across 89 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on the new files. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020).

PROGRESS 2026-08-07 (4) — truck-stock PORTED. 5 of 7 ported, 1 reclassified out of scope, 1 remains (toner-replenish).

PORTED — supabase/functions/truck-stock/{index.ts,optimizer.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (18 -> 17). All ELEVEN Express endpoints (generate, recommendations list, :id, :id/export.csv, :id/pick, :id/receive, inventory, GET/PUT settings, callbacks, stats), which is everything TruckStocking.tsx calls. Confirmed no other Express router serves /api/truck-stock/*.

A SECOND PROD-ONLY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, separate from the 404. The pick-list download was window.open(getApiUrl('.../export.csv')) — a plain browser navigation, which carries NO Authorization header. That works today because Express accepts a session cookie, but the moment the domain is served by an edge function it 401s and the warehouse gets a JSON error page where the pick list should be. This is the exact pattern CLAUDE.md records for invoice PDFs. New client/src/lib/truck-stock-csv.ts mirrors lib/invoice-pdf.ts: fetch with Bearer + x-tenant-id, then hand the browser a blob via the existing triggerBlobDownload; failures now surface as a toast instead of a blank tab. Worth noting the shape of this bug — it would NOT have been caught by porting alone, and it would have looked like "the export is broken in prod" long after the port was declared done.

ROUTING DETAIL: /recommendations/:id/export.csv must be matched BEFORE the bare /recommendations/:id, and 'export.csv' is an ACTION segment — the dot is part of the path segment, not an extension anything strips. Also the only endpoint in this tree that returns non-JSON, so its Response is built by hand rather than through createCorsResponse (which JSON-encodes), with the CORS headers set explicitly.

/receive IS THE ONLY WRITE THAT CHANGES PHYSICAL STOCK — it sets truck_inventory.quantity_on_truck for every recommended SKU. Ordering is deliberate: resolve-and-tenant-check the recommendation, THEN upsert the inventory, THEN flip the status. Reversing the last two would mark a truck restocked whose inventory was never written, and the tech would leave without the parts. Express looped one insert per item; this batches them into a single upsert on (tenant_id, tech_user_id, part_sku).

POSTGREST GAPS (running count now 12+): (1) no SELECT DISTINCT, so /generate's "every tech with tickets in the window" is built as a Set in JS from the ids; (2) the fuzzy SKU match (part_number = sku OR name = sku) becomes .or() of two .in() filters — one round trip, where Express scanned the whole inventory_items table per optimizer run and did the matching in JS; (3) the technicians lookup is likewise .or() of two .in() instead of a full-table scan.

DATA CONTRACT: TruckStocking.tsx reads camelCase (currentFillRate, projectedFillRate, recommendedItems, generatedAt, recommendedAdditions), so all three row shapes get explicit mappers. recommended_items stays untouched jsonb — its inner keys are data we wrote. Fill rates map null -> null rather than 0, because 0% coverage and "not measured" are different claims and the dashboard renders the former as a red number.

BEHAVIOURS PINNED BY TEST because they are judgement calls, not mechanics: fillRate gives NO partial credit (a job missing one of four parts still meant a trip back to base, so it is not 75% avoided); fillRate is 0 with no history, not 100 (an empty history is not evidence of coverage); tickets that used no parts are EXCLUDED from the denominator (including them would push a no-parts tech toward 100%); the greedy fit TRUNCATES the last SKU to the remaining capacity rather than dropping it; delta stays SIGNED so the CSV shows what to remove as well as what to add; and csvEscape quotes commas/quotes/newlines — an unescaped comma in a part description shifts every later column of the warehouse's pick list.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/truck-stock-optimizer.test.ts (64 tests) — usage tallying including the same-part-twice-in-one-job case, every fill-rate rule and boundary, the greedy fit with both caps and the truncation case, cost-map matching and first-wins precedence, latest-per-tech ordering, tech-name resolution by BOTH id and user_id, all three camelCase mappers, CSV escaping and formatting, stats including the null-not-zero rule and a negative lift, and all three input parsers. STORY STATUS — passes stays FALSE, and the reason is a judgement call for a human, not a gap in the work. Six of the seven domains meet every acceptance criterion. The seventh, incident-response, is NOT ported and is still in the missingEdge baseline, so AC1 ("an edge function exists for every domain listed") and AC5 ("each domain is removed from the missingEdge list") are literally unmet. That is deliberate: routes-incident-response.ts has ZERO db calls across 677 lines and returns hardcoded incident counts and SLA figures (activeIncidents 7, mttr 3.8, slaCompliance 94.7). Porting it would publish fabricated INCIDENT data to production, which is strictly worse than the 404 it replaces — an operator would believe they had 7 live incidents at 94.7% SLA when the system knows nothing at all. It is reclassified to PA-040 (wire or clearly flag the fully-mock dashboards). Whoever closes this story should decide whether that exception satisfies it or whether PA-040 has to land first; I am not flipping the flag on a criterion I knowingly did not meet.

  technician-sessions  PORTED (+ the story's own "no handler either side" diagnosis corrected)
  service              PORTED (+ an always-500 Express query repaired)

toner-replenish PORTED — supabase/functions/toner-replenish/{index.ts,replenish.ts}, proxied, removed from missingEdge (17 -> 16). All TWELVE Express endpoints (capture, evaluate, run, levels, orders, orders/:id/ship, orders/:id/cancel, machines/:id/ship-now, GET/PUT tenant settings, GET/PUT machine settings), which is everything TonerReplenish.tsx calls. Confirmed no other Express router serves /api/toner-replenish/*.

THIS IS THE ONLY DOMAIN IN THE BATCH THAT SPENDS MONEY WITH NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP — an auto_ship order becomes a cartridge on a truck and a line on an invoice — so the suppressions are the feature, not error handling, and every one is preserved and tested:
  - CUSTOMER-MANAGED machines never order unless their emergency override is set. That customer buys their own toner; shipping to them bills for something they did not ask for.
  - autoShipEnabled=false suppresses independently, on the operator side. The emergency override deliberately does NOT re-enable an operator-disabled machine — the two switches answer to different people.
  - a machine+color with an order already in flight never gets a second one, and the in-run set is updated as orders are queued so one evaluate pass cannot double-order either.
  - the cost gate is the MINIMUM of the tenant threshold and the per-machine ceiling, so the tighter limit always wins and a per-machine ceiling can only ever make approval MORE likely.
  - a flat or RISING level curve predicts nothing and orders nothing. A rising curve means someone just replaced the cartridge; ordering off it ships toner nobody needs. This is the subtlest of the five and has its own test.

REGRESSION DIRECTION IS THE EASY THING TO GET WRONG. x is DAYS AGO, so an older reading has a LARGER x, which makes the slope of a depleting cartridge POSITIVE — dailyDrop is the slope itself, not its negation. Inverting it would reject every depleting cartridge and order for every refilled one. Documented at the function and pinned by the rising-curve test.

POSTGREST GAP (running count 13+): the levels endpoint used SELECT DISTINCT ON (machine_id, color), which PostgREST cannot express. Replaced by an ordered fetch plus latestPerMachineColor, which keeps the first row per key — so the DESCENDING captured_at sort is load-bearing: reversed, the dashboard would show every machine's OLDEST toner level and nobody would notice until a machine ran dry. Pinned by test. Also: capture now batches its inserts into one call instead of one round trip per machine per color, and the levels/orders enrichment filters by the ids referenced rather than scanning whole tables.

DATA CONTRACT: TonerReplenish.tsx reads camelCase, so levels, orders and both settings shapes get explicit mappers. Two value-preservation rules worth naming: percentRemaining stays NULL when the column is null rather than becoming 0 (no reading and empty cartridge are opposite states, and the page paints the latter red), and money stays a STRING through unitCost/totalCost as the page types it — parsing to float would reintroduce rounding on a currency value.

STUBS carried over unchanged and still marked: vendor levels are deterministic synthetic readings written with source='injected' (the only thing distinguishing a fabricated reading from a real one once it is in the table — do not drop that marker), the per-color unit cost is a fixed proxy, and the tracking number is generated rather than obtained from a carrier.

TESTED: server/tests/unit/toner-replenish.test.ts (63 tests) — the regression including flat/rising/single/same-instant/already-empty cases and reading-order independence, all suppression combinations, the window boundary (strict), the cost gate including the min-not-max rule and a zero ceiling, color handling, reading grouping and latest-per-key ordering, the vendor stub's determinism and bounds, all four response mappers with their null-preservation rules, and all five input parsers including the null-means-clear vs omitted-means-leave distinction. MUTATION-CHECKED, 14 mutations, all caught: rising curve accepted (1 fail), customer-managed suppression removed (1), emergency override re-enabling an operator-disabled machine (1), cost gate max instead of min (3), window inclusive (1), latest-per-key keeps the last row (1), explicit zero lead time treated as unset (1), null percent coerced to 0 (1), money parsed to float (1), auto-ship defaulting to off (1), stored zero threshold replaced by the default (1), boolean flags coerced instead of rejected (1), unknown status filter passed through (1), unparseable timestamps kept (1).

VERIFIED: all five ratchets pass; suite 1928 passed + 1 skipped across 91 files; check-types holds at 1067; build passes; eslint clean on the new files. NOT verified against a live deploy (no Deno here, no egress — PROD-020 still needs one run from a host with egress). | BROKEN-FEATURE FINDING 2026-08-19 (the sole exclusion in the new check:throwing-types gate, recorded precisely because the CLAUDE.md note understated it): server/routes-predictive-service-dispatch.ts serves /api/predictive-dispatch/* - note the prefix DIFFERS from the filename, which is why a filename-based search misses it - and client/src/pages/PredictiveServiceDispatchDashboard.tsx is a LIVE ROUTE at /predictive-service-dispatch (App.tsx:771) whose four queries (dashboard, devices-at-risk, technician-performance, analyze/:serialNumber, analyze-all) all hit it. Its handlers reference serviceCallsEnhanced, equipmentMetrics and technicianResourcesEnhanced; I verified service_calls_enhanced / equipment_metrics / technician_resources_enhanced appear in ZERO migrations across the entire drizzle/migrations tree, not just 0000. So every panel on that page returns 500 today, in dev and prod alike - this is a BROKEN feature, distinct from the fabricated-data pages (which return plausible fiction) and from the missing-edge 404s (which work in dev). ~60 of the remaining 1009 tsc errors are in this one file. FIXING IT IS A PRODUCT DECISION, NOT AN IMPORT FIX: someone must design what those three tables hold (enhanced service-call history, per-equipment metric series, technician capacity/resource records), write the schema + migration, and only then wire the handlers. The alternative is deleting the page, the routes and the file, which would also remove the exclusion and drop the tsc baseline by ~60. Deliberately not chosen unilaterally - same open decision as the mock dashboards. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 - renewal-autoquote PORTED; live prod 404s 12 -> 10. supabase/functions/renewal-autoquote/ covers all 11 endpoints (generate, list, stats, settings GET/PUT, suppressions GET/POST/DELETE, :id detail, :id/mark-sent, :id/dismiss, :id/outcome). userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL. Fixed at the source by renaming the key to 'local:quote-templates' (also more honest: there is no quote_templates table in any schema/migration), so the tool no longer classifies it. Removed from the baseline; missingEdge 39 -> 38, live prod 404s 29 -> 28. Gotcha worth knowing: the first version of the explanatory comment SPELLED OUT the api path and re-triggered the same grep — the comment now deliberately avoids the literal string.

(c) I checked the OTHER 28 for the same no-network pattern (scripted scan for a queryFn resolving from localStorage/sessionStorage near each match). quote-templates was the ONLY one. The remaining 28 are real.

(d) predictive-analytics and technician-sessions are confirmed REAL but differ from the rest: they use the DEFAULT queryFn (queryClient.ts joins the queryKey into a URL and fetches it), so they issue genuine requests — and they have NO handler in Express either, so they are broken in DEV TOO, not just prod. technician-sessions also drives mutations (check-in), so the technician ticket workflow is non-functional everywhere. Neither has a backing table (no technician_sessions, no quote_templates in any schema or migration), so these two need an implement-with-schema decision, not a port.

(e) MEASURED EFFORT for the ports, so the remaining batches are honestly scoped: the four PROD-012 handlers alone are 3,950 lines of Express (routes-voice-ticket-close 860, routes-voice-agent 825, routes-chatbot 1200, routes-email-autopilot 1065), and each exposes 4-9 endpoints. Extrapolating, the full 26-domain port is roughly 20,000 lines of Express to re-express as Deno edge functions WITH field-by-field response-shape parity. This is multi-session work and must not be rushed: per CLAUDE.md these pages fall back to mock data with '|| [...]', so a shape mismatch silently renders fabricated numbers — strictly worse than the 404 it replaces. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 - voice-agent PORTED; live prod 404s 10 -> 9. supabase/functions/voice-agent/ covers all 7 endpoints (intake, calls list + :id, settings GET/PUT, cost, purge-recordings). Dir name == URL segment so a plain crmProxies entry sufficed. THE APPROACH THAT MATTERS HERE: the intake pipeline CREATES A SERVICE TICKET and PAGES THE ON-CALL TECH on P1, so the pure decision logic was EXTRACTED to supabase/functions/_shared/voice-agent-logic.ts (classifyPriority, redactPii, estimateCost, fallbackSummary, parseHHMM, isWithinBusinessHours, ticketPriority, last10Digits), exported from the Express route, and locked by server/tests/unit/voice-agent-logic-parity.test.ts running 72 cases through BOTH copies - a drift opens tickets at the wrong urgency or wakes someone at 2am who should not have been woken. MUTATION-TESTED by dropping 'down' from the P1 keyword list: 5 tests fail. This is the third parity lock built on the renewal-port pattern (renewal-retier, quote-math + print-cost-calculator, now voice-agent) and the pattern is now the default for any port where duplicated logic decides an outcome a human acts on. DECISION WORTH COPYING: summarizeIntake was PORTED, not stubbed to the offline fallback. Stubbing was easier and would have looked harmless, but Express calls Claude when CLAUDE_API_KEY is set - so prod would have quietly summarised WORSE than dev, changing what the technician reads on the ticket. The Deno version mirrors the model (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022), system prompt, temperature 0.2 and fallback-on-any-failure exactly. CARRIED OVER DELIBERATELY (do not 'fix' on one side only): credentials are base64-obfuscated NOT encrypted, matching the Express TODO(vault); GET returns only twilioSet/elevenLabsSet markers, never raw creds; the real-time Twilio Media Streams + ElevenLabs stack is unbuilt on BOTH sides, so v1 ingests a call-end summary. KNOWN COSMETIC QUIRK, recorded in the test rather than asserted around: the callback-number regex must start at a digit, so '(515) 242-7911' captures as '515) 242-7911'. Shared behaviour; fix belongs in both copies at once. REMAINING real missing-edge domains: chatbot, content, email-autopilot, voice-ticket-close. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 (part 2) - voice-ticket-close PORTED; live prod 404s 9 -> 8. supabase/functions/voice-ticket-close/ covers all 5 endpoints (:ticketId/transcribe, GET :ticketId, PATCH draft/:id, POST draft/:id/confirm, purge-audio), including the Whisper multipart call and the Claude extraction with the same prompt/temperature/fallback. THE MUTATION-TEST LESSON, the most transferable thing from this pass: my first parity suite for the SKU matcher PASSED when I moved SKU_AUTO_MATCH_THRESHOLD from 0.45 to 0.3. Every case I had chosen scored 0, 0.75 or 1 - nothing landed in the band the threshold actually governs, which is the entire auto-select-vs-ask-the-tech decision. Added cases scoring 0.300 ('maintenance kit for fuser unit') and 0.333 ('toner cartridge for the black one'); the same mutation now fails 3 tests. RULE: a parity/threshold suite must contain cases INSIDE the boundary band, not just clearly-above and clearly-below ones - otherwise it protects nothing at exactly the point that matters. Check the earlier locks (renewal-retier tier boundaries, quote-math guardrail) against this standard when they are next touched. TWO BEHAVIOURS RECORDED, NOT CHANGED (fix belongs in both copies at once): (1) a single common word scores 1 (0.5 substring + 0.5 full token overlap), so a tech saying just 'cartridge' AUTO-SELECTS the first toner rather than being asked to disambiguate - a real usability/stock-accuracy risk worth a follow-up; (2) the Express confirm runs inside db.transaction but each step is individually try/caught and the tx commits regardless - and because a failed statement ABORTS a Postgres transaction, that per-step 'degrade gracefully' cannot work past the first failure, whereas the sequential edge version can. NEITHER rolls back, so a partial close (inventory deducted, ticket still open) is possible on both; the response reports steps + stepWarnings. If atomicity is wanted, the drizzle/functions/ RPC convention (10 existing files + README, applied outside the migration journal) is the established place for it. PORTING NOTE: PostgREST cannot express `quantity_on_truck - qty` in an UPDATE, so the edge fn reads the row then writes the difference - not atomic, but the Express version does not lock the row either. REMAINING real missing-edge domains: chatbot, content, email-autopilot. | INVENTORY-ACCURACY FIX 2026-08-19 (part 3), enabled by the parity lock from part 2: the SKU matcher no longer auto-selects an AMBIGUOUS tie. A generic spoken word scores 1 against every part whose description contains it (0.5 substring + 0.5 full token overlap), so 'toner' and 'cartridge' both tied at 1.0 across TN-514K and TN-514C, and the code took candidates[0] - on confirm that silently deducted BLACK toner from the tech's truck when they may have fitted cyan. Wrong stock, no prompt, no warning. Now: when candidates[0].score === candidates[1].score, chosenSku is null and the tech disambiguates. Specific terms are unaffected ('black toner' 1 vs 0.25, 'TN-514K', 'drum unit' all still auto-select). CHANGED IN BOTH COPIES IN ONE COMMIT - that is the whole point of building the lock first; mutation-tested by disabling the tie-break in the Deno copy (6 tests fail). This is the pattern to follow for the other recorded-but-unfixed shared quirks (e.g. the voice-agent callback-number regex dropping a leading paren): lock first, then fix both sides together. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 (part 4) - email-autopilot PORTED; live prod 404s 8 -> 7. supabase/functions/email-autopilot/ covers all 12 endpoints (account, connect, settings, scan, drafts list + :id, accept, reject, suppressions GET/POST/DELETE, stats). Scoped by (tenant_id, user_id) throughout - a rep only ever sees their own mailbox/drafts/suppressions. NO SEND CAPABILITY on either side; accept records edits + edit-distance and leaves the draft in the rep's mailbox. EXTRACTED + LOCKED (4th parity lock this session): _shared/email-autopilot-logic.ts holds fallbackClassify (decides whether an email gets a drafted reply AT ALL) and levenshtein/editDistancePct (feeds avgEditDistancePct + toneMissRate, the numbers a rep uses to judge whether the autopilot is worth trusting), plus fallbackDraft and TONE_MISS_THRESHOLD. server/tests/unit/email-autopilot-logic-parity.test.ts = 32 cases through both copies. MUTATION-TESTED THREE WAYS, all caught: removing one spam keyword (1 fail), changing edit-distance rounding from 1 decimal to whole percent (3 fails), nudging fallback confidence 0.55 -> 0.5 (2 fails). APPLIED THE BOUNDARY-BAND LESSON from the voice-ticket-close pass: the suite includes edits either side of TONE_MISS_THRESHOLD, not just obviously-small and obviously-large ones. BOTH CLAUDE PATHS PORTED, not stubbed to the fallbacks - same model/prompts/failure behaviour - so prod does not quietly classify and draft worse than dev when CLAUDE_API_KEY is set (same reasoning as the voice-agent summarizeIntake decision). ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, recorded not invented: the Express createProviderDraft STUB returns a FAKE external draft id built from Date.now()+Math.random(); the port stores NULL, because an id that matches nothing in the rep's real mailbox is worse than recording that no provider draft was created. When the real create-draft API is wired, wire it on both sides. REMAINING real missing-edge domains: chatbot (needs the /query agent ported - see sizing note) and content (21 endpoints, 1 live beacon caller that is broken independently of any port).
