Both dir names == URL segment, so plain crmProxies entries, no server.ts override. SHAPE: both convert rows to camelCase on the way OUT (MeterBilling types its list as the Drizzle ContractTieredRate, and the compat dialog matches on `comp.modelId === model.id`) and map bodies to real migration-0000 columns on the way IN via an allowlist. STATUS-CODE PARITY MATTERS: the Express contract-tiered-rates POST answers 200, NOT 201 - the edge fn matches it deliberately; the accessories DELETE answers 204 with no body. FOUND WHILE PORTING - A DEAD DUPLICATE WITH AN RBAC GAP: /api/contract-tiered-rates was registered TWICE in Express, in routes-products-crud.ts AND routes-workflow-mobile.ts, with identical bodies EXCEPT that the products-crud POST gates on PERMISSIONS.FINANCE.BILLING.CONFIGURE and the workflow-mobile copy had NO permission check. registerProductsCrudRoutes(app) runs first (routes-registry.ts:364 vs :369) so Express always matched the GUARDED copy and the unguarded pair was dead - not a live hole, but any reordering of registration would have silently dropped the RBAC gate. Removed the duplicate + its now-unused insertContractTieredRateSchema import. WORTH A SWEEP: grep for other paths registered by two different route files; registration order is load-bearing and invisible. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 (part 2) - documents PORTED; live prod 404s 13 -> 12. supabase/functions/documents/ serves all four routes of server/routes-documents.ts (GET / list, POST / create, GET /:id, POST /:id/pdf), camelCase out (DocumentBuilder reads doc.agreementNumber / doc.includeServiceContract / doc.monthlyBase) and column-mapped in. TRIAGE CORRECTION - my own triage table in PROD-014 said 'documents -> routes-document-automation.ts (266 lines)'. WRONG on both counts: the file serving the frontend's calls is server/routes-documents.ts (266 lines, mounted at /api/documents by routes-registry.ts:468), while routes-document-automation.ts is 549 lines and owns entirely DIFFERENT paths (/api/documents/generate|batch-generate|generated|upload|uploads|ai-extract) that have ZERO callers in client/src. The proxy entry forwards the WHOLE /api/documents prefix, so those zero-caller paths now resolve to the edge fn in dev too - nothing regresses today, but a new caller for one of them needs an edge handler, not just the Express route. THE PORT ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED THE PAGE, and this is the important part: two of DocumentBuilder's three calls used a BARE fetch('/api/documents...', {credentials:'include'}), which breaks in prod TWICE - a relative path never passes through getApiUrl (so it hits the static origin, not functions.printyx.net) and cookies do not authenticate an edge function (it needs a Bearer JWT, per the CLAUDE.md invoice-pdf.ts note). Create now uses apiRequest; the export uses a new client/src/lib/document-export.ts modelled on lib/invoice-pdf.ts. ALSO: the /pdf endpoint returns HTML, not PDF (the Express handler always did - 'in production you would use puppeteer'); the edge fn reproduces that rather than diverging, but the download was named .pdf so users got an HTML file with the wrong extension - now .html, and generatePDFMutation renamed to downloadAgreementMutation. The renderer moved to supabase/functions/_shared/document-html.ts, copied VERBATIM (print-cost-calculator idiom) so the exported agreement is byte-identical on both backends. RECORDED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, needs a decision: that template hardcodes 'INFOMAX OFFICE SYSTEMS, INC.' as the seller, so in a multi-tenant product EVERY tenant's purchase agreement names that one company. white_label_config.company_name is the obvious source; the fix must land on both backends at once or the two will diverge. | SIZING FOR THE 3 REMAINING REAL MISSING-EDGE DOMAINS, measured 2026-08-19 rather than estimated (a filename/db-call heuristic mis-sized two domains earlier in this session, so these are counted from the file that actually defines the routes). (1) email-autopilot - server/routes-email-autopilot.ts, 1065 lines, 12 endpoints, 9 LIVE frontend paths, 13 helper fns. BEST NEXT TARGET: most live surface of the three. (2) chatbot - server/routes-chatbot.ts, 1210 lines, 9 endpoints, 7 live frontend paths. NOT a single-pass port: 8 of the 9 endpoints are simple CRUD over chatbot_* tables, but POST /query is a Claude agent that selects among ~700 lines of READ-ONLY query tools spanning many business tables, and re-expressing those SELECTs in PostgREST is where the risk and bulk are. Consider porting the 8 CRUD endpoints and treating /query separately, but note the prefix proxy is all-or-nothing so /query must be handled in the same function. (3) content - server/routes-content-marketing.ts, 863 lines, 21 endpoints, but only TWO live frontend paths and only ONE under /api/content: the fire-and-forget POST /api/content/analytics/view beacon in client/src/lib/seoUtils.tsx, which uses a RAW fetch and therefore never reaches the API in production regardless of any port (it is in the raw-fetch baseline). The other ~20 blog/guides/case-study endpoints have ZERO callers in client/src - the marketing blog pages are static React routes, not API-driven. LOWEST VALUE of the three despite being counted as a live prod-404 domain; porting 21 endpoints to fix one beacon is poor value, and the beacon needs its call site fixed either way. | SCHEMA COLLISION FOUND 2026-08-19 — blog_posts IS DECLARED TWICE WITH DIVERGENT SHAPES, and the US-BLOG system loses. Found while sizing the content-marketing port; recorded rather than fixed because choosing an owner and migrating data is an architecture decision. EVIDENCE, all verifiable: (1) shared/content-marketing-schema.ts:57 and shared/blog-schema.ts:344 BOTH declare pgTable('blog_posts', ...). 36 columns exist only in blog-schema, 35 only in content-marketing - divergent, not a copy. (2) shared/schema.ts re-exports BOTH (explicit named re-export at :8668 from content-marketing, `export * from './blog-schema'` at :9027). An explicit named re-export WINS over a later export *, so every consumer of `@shared/schema` silently receives the CONTENT-MARKETING definition - which is why server/routes-content-marketing.ts typechecks. (3) Only one shape can exist in the DB, and migration order decides it, not intent: migration 0000_fuzzy_blizzard.sql is JOURNALED and always applied, creating blog_posts with the content-marketing shape (content text NOT NULL, meta_title varchar(60), tenant_id uuid, focus_keyword, keyword_tier enum). drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_tables.sql:119 creates the blog-schema shape with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS - so it is SKIPPED IN SILENCE. No migration reconciles them (checked every ALTER TABLE "blog_posts" ADD COLUMN in the tree: only _backfill_blog_authors.sql adds author_id/reviewed_by_author_id/original_research_signal). CONSEQUENCE: the US-BLOG platform-admin blog system (28 tables, ~12 blog-* edge functions incl. blog-analytics-intel and blog-audience-variants, which query .from('blog_posts')) reads columns that DO NOT EXIST on the table it actually hits - body_markdown, body_html, brief_id, cms_target_key, cms_post_id, brand_voice_id, style_guide_id, canonical_url, featured_image_asset_id. And any INSERT from that system fails outright, because the physical table has content NOT NULL and the blog system never sets it. DECISION NEEDED: which system owns the name `blog_posts`? Renaming the US-BLOG one (e.g. to blog_system_posts) is the smaller change - the content-marketing table is the one that physically exists and is referenced by migration 0000 - but it touches 28 tables' FKs and every blog-* edge function. Do NOT 'fix' by dropping/recreating the table: whatever content-marketing rows exist would be lost. GUARD SHIPPED: scripts/check-duplicate-tables.mjs + docs/duplicate-tables-baseline.json + npm run check:dup-tables, wired into ci.yml, mutation-tested. It fails when a table name is newly declared by two different shared/*.ts schemas (a second declaration inside ONE file is ignored - the author can see that). THREE MORE COLLISIONS EXIST, all divergent and all baselined, each needing the same decision: client_activity_logs (client-monitor-schema vs printyx-client-schema, 31/46 unique columns), location_history (gps-tracking-schema vs mobile-service-schema, 48/3), dashboard_layouts (reporting-schema vs schema-dashboard, 10/32). CONTENT PORT NOT DONE and should not start until this is settled: porting routes-content-marketing means committing to the content-marketing blog_posts shape in a second place.

userStories.title: Close prod 404s: platform, integration & compliance surfaces
userStories.description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-30 via scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs: each domain below is called by a page REACHABLE from App.tsx/main.tsx and has NO edge function, so it works in dev (Express serves it) and returns 404 in production (which hits the edge function directly). 4 of these have an Express handler that is the port source; 0 have no handler on either side and are dead in dev AND prod.

  - /api/erp-integration -> pages/ERPIntegration.tsx
  - /api/security-compliance -> pages/SecurityComplianceManagement.tsx
  - /api/white-label -> pages/WhiteLabelDashboard.tsx
  - /api/workflow-automation -> pages/AutopilotDashboard.tsx + pages/WorkflowAutomation.tsx

Per CLAUDE.md, porting is not just route creation: use normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>') (an edge handler NEVER sees its own name in the path — the dispatcher strips segment 0), filter every query by tenant_id, and match the RESPONSE SHAPE the page actually reads. Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404, because pages fall back to mock data with || and silently render fabricated numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: An edge function exists for every domain listed, resolving under the URL prefix the frontend already calls
Routing uses normalizePath so it behaves identically whether or not the function-name segment is present
Every query filters by tenant_id, and auth is enforced per handler
Response shape matches what the consuming page reads, verified field by field against the real Drizzle columns (not an assumed/mock shape)
Each domain is removed from the missingEdge list in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json
npm run check:edge-paths stays at 0 offenders
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL. Fixed at the source by renaming the key to 'local:quote-templates' (also more honest: there is no quote_templates table in any schema/migration), so the tool no longer classifies it. Removed from the baseline; missingEdge 39 -> 38, live prod 404s 29 -> 28. Gotcha worth knowing: the first version of the explanatory comment SPELLED OUT the api path and re-triggered the same grep — the comment now deliberately avoids the literal string.

(c) I checked the OTHER 28 for the same no-network pattern (scripted scan for a queryFn resolving from localStorage/sessionStorage near each match). quote-templates was the ONLY one. The remaining 28 are real.

(d) predictive-analytics and technician-sessions are confirmed REAL but differ from the rest: they use the DEFAULT queryFn (queryClient.ts joins the queryKey into a URL and fetches it), so they issue genuine requests — and they have NO handler in Express either, so they are broken in DEV TOO, not just prod. technician-sessions also drives mutations (check-in), so the technician ticket workflow is non-functional everywhere. Neither has a backing table (no technician_sessions, no quote_templates in any schema or migration), so these two need an implement-with-schema decision, not a port.

(e) MEASURED EFFORT for the ports, so the remaining batches are honestly scoped: the four PROD-012 handlers alone are 3,950 lines of Express (routes-voice-ticket-close 860, routes-voice-agent 825, routes-chatbot 1200, routes-email-autopilot 1065), and each exposes 4-9 endpoints. Extrapolating, the full 26-domain port is roughly 20,000 lines of Express to re-express as Deno edge functions WITH field-by-field response-shape parity. This is multi-session work and must not be rushed: per CLAUDE.md these pages fall back to mock data with '|| [...]', so a shape mismatch silently renders fabricated numbers — strictly worse than the 404 it replaces. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 - white-label PORTED; live prod 404s in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json 16 -> 15. supabase/functions/white-label/ covers all twelve endpoints (config GET/PUT, verify-domain, email-template list/get/upsert/delete/preview, presets, apply-preset, css, config-by-domain) over the real migration-0000 tables white_label_config / white_label_email_templates / white_label_presets. Dir name == URL segment so a PLAIN crmProxies entry was enough - no server.ts override (the EDGE-004 decision rule, not EDGE-005a's). THREE THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT PORT IN THIS BATCH: (1) SHAPE - WhiteLabelDashboard.tsx reads camelCase (companyName/colorPrimary/customDomainVerified) but PostgREST returns snake_case, so every row is converted on the way OUT and every request body is mapped to real columns on the way IN via an explicit allowlist (an unmapped key is a PGRST204, per EDGE-005a). Returning raw snake_case here would have rendered the entire branding form blank while still returning 200. (2) SEEDING - creating a config seeds 5 default email templates in the Express path (WhiteLabelService.getDefaultTemplates, ~216 lines of literal template HTML). Rather than let dev and prod diverge on first create, those defaults plus generateCssVariables and renderEmailTemplate were duplicated into supabase/functions/_shared/white-label.ts, following the _shared/print-cost-calculator.ts duplicate-and-note idiom. KEEP THE TWO IN SYNC. (3) The /css endpoint returns text/css, NOT JSON - it is consumed as a stylesheet, so it bypasses createCorsResponse and sets its own Content-Type on top of getCorsHeaders. ALSO FIXED ON THE EXPRESS SIDE: all 10 handlers read req.headers['x-tenant-id'] directly instead of the resolved tenant. NOT an IDOR - resolveTenant (server/middleware/tenancy.ts:132) 403s a header that disagrees with the JWT before any handler runs - but it 400'd on any request that did not happen to send the header, and it is the pattern CLAUDE.md forbids; now getTenantId. PARITY GAP KEPT DELIBERATELY: verify-domain marks a domain verified WITHOUT any DNS lookup on both sides (the Express service has a TODO for real TXT/CNAME verification); the edge fn reproduces that rather than silently diverging, and both now say so. TRIAGE NOTE FOR THE REST OF THIS BATCH - erp-integration is NOT worth porting as-is: server/routes-erp-integration.ts /dashboard is 100% hardcoded mock (integrationOverview counts, an 'SAP Business One' system with invented sync stats, etc), so porting it would only move fabricated numbers into prod. Check each remaining domain for a real data source FIRST; security-compliance and incident-response are the same page archetype and likely the same. NOT VERIFIED: deno is not installed in this environment, so the function is not deno-checked and nothing was executed against a deploy - confirm with one curl per endpoint before treating this as closed. | TRIAGE TABLE 2026-08-19 - measured all 15 remaining missing-edge domains for whether the Express handler has a REAL data source, so no one spends a session porting fabricated numbers. Method: find the file that actually serves the prefix (NOT the file whose name matches - several disagree), then count db.select/insert/update/delete/query calls in it. PURE MOCK, DO NOT PORT AS-IS (0 db calls): erp-integration (740 lines, invented SAP sync stats), incident-response (677), workflow-automation (server/routes-workflow-automation.ts, 730 - and CLAUDE.md already flags this file as an UNREGISTERED dead mock; the REAL runtime is server/routes/workflow-automation-routes.ts, so check which file actually answers before porting this one). REAL, PORTABLE (db calls in parens): documents/routes-document-automation.ts (266 lines, 1) is the smallest remaining; security-compliance (597, 4); voice-agent (825, 3); chatbot (1210, 4); email-autopilot (1065, 4); renewal-autoquote (762, 6); voice-ticket-close (860, 6). FILENAME TRAP - these five have NO server/routes-<domain>.ts and are served from a differently-named file: accessories + contract-tiered-rates -> routes-products-crud.ts (both now ported), ai -> routes-registry/routes-sample-data, business-process -> routes-business-process-optimization.ts, content -> routes-content-marketing.ts. A `ls server/routes-<domain>.ts` returning nothing does NOT mean the domain is unserved. | TRIAGE TABLE CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (round 2) - MY OWN EARLIER TABLE WAS WRONG TWICE, both times from the same mistake: counting db calls in the file whose NAME matches the domain instead of the file that DEFINES the route. Corrected method: grep for the file containing (app|router).(get|post|...)('/api/<domain>...) and read the SPECIFIC handler - even a per-file db-call count misleads, because routes-operations-extended.ts has 11 db calls overall while its security-compliance/dashboard handler is 100% hardcoded mock (invented threat ids, a fake john.smith@printyx.com, fabricated scores). CORRECTED RESULTS. PURE MOCK, do not port as-is: erp-integration, incident-response, workflow-automation (routes-workflow-automation.ts), ai, business-process, and security-compliance (whose handler lives in routes-operations-extended.ts, NOT the similarly-named server/security-compliance.ts, which is an audit-logging module with no routes at all - that is the file that fooled my first count). REAL, with db-call counts in the file that actually defines the routes: content/routes-content-marketing.ts 35, chatbot/routes-chatbot.ts 30, renewal-autoquote/routes-renewal-autoquote.ts 23 (my earlier '6' was wrong), email-autopilot/routes-email-autopilot.ts 19, voice-agent/routes-voice-agent.ts 13, voice-ticket-close/routes-voice-ticket-close.ts 10. NOTE routes-sample-data.ts matches many domains and is NOISE - it is a seeder that merely mentions the paths. SIZING NOTE for whoever takes renewal-autoquote: it is the best-documented of the real ones (dedicated shared/renewal-autoquote-schema.ts, a header listing all 11 endpoints, frontend already on apiRequest) but POST /generate is a ~260-line generation engine that is also cron-callable, so the port is not just CRUD and interacts with EDGE-009. | FABRICATED-COMPLIANCE FINDING + REMOVAL 2026-08-19. While triaging the mock domains I found that security-compliance was not merely 'a mock dashboard' but a LEGAL-010-class problem stated inside the product: SecurityComplianceManagement.tsx rendered, to any authenticated user, an overall security score of 94.7, '6 certifications active', and a GDPR entry with status 'compliant', complianceScore 96.8, certificationStatus 'active', auditor 'EU Compliance Solutions' and audit/expiry dates - all a hardcoded object literal. Sibling endpoints returned audit logs SYNTHESISED WITH Math.random(), which is worse than returning nothing, since that is the record you consult during an incident. REMOVED the page, its 3 routes (note /security-compliance had NO guard at all) and all 7 endpoints, faking nothing in its place per the CLAUDE.md rule. Navigation now points at the REAL stack: 'Audit & Compliance' in the sidebar, the mobile drawer and AdminHub all target /admin/audit-logs (AuditLogViewer -> /api/audit-logs -> services/audit-log-service.ts -> the audit_logs table, unit-tested and already written to by logAuditEvent). gdpr_requests and security_sessions are likewise REAL tables in shared/security-schema.ts, so a genuine compliance dashboard has sources - build on those, and never restate a certification the company does not hold. TWO REUSABLE LESSONS. (1) DUPLICATE REGISTRATION DECIDES WHICH MOCK YOU ARE LOOKING AT: /api/security-compliance/dashboard was defined IDENTICALLY in routes-operations-extended.ts AND routes-sample-data.ts, and sample-data registers FIRST (routes-registry.ts:360 vs :368), so the copy Express actually matched was the sample-data one - deleting only the 'obvious' file would have left the fiction live. server/routes-sample-data.ts defines 29 routes and shadows real route modules on at least customer-success/health-scores, integration-hub/dashboard, remote-monitoring/fleet-overview and document-management/library; in each of those the shadowed handler is ALSO a mock today, so nothing real is hidden yet, but that stops being true the moment one of them is implemented. This is the second registration-order trap this session (the first was contract-tiered-rates losing an RBAC gate) - a check for doubly-registered paths is worth writing. (2) THE NAV RATCHET PAID FOR ITSELF: deleting the page left 5 stale references (navigation-permissions.ts x3, MobileNavigationDrawer, AdminHub) that check:nav caught immediately; grepping the component name alone would have missed all of them because they reference the PATH, not the component. STILL MOCK, same decision pending, all routed and reachable: erp-integration (/erp-integration), incident-response (/incident-response, /incident-response-system), business-process, ai-analytics, integration-hub, document-management, customer-success, maintenance, remote-monitoring. None of these makes a compliance claim, so none is as urgent - but each renders invented numbers as fact.

userStories.title: Resolve the canonical-table contradiction: production CRM runs on `companies`, not `business_records`
userStories.description: As an architect, I need one decided direction of travel for the account model, because docs/crm-canonical-model.md declares `business_records` canonical and `companies` deprecated, while the deployed edge functions do the exact opposite — they read and write `companies` and treat `business_records` as the legacy fallback. Until this is settled, every downstream CRM story risks being built against the wrong table.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm the finding in a running environment before deciding anything: supabase/functions/business-records/index.ts lists FROM `companies`, creates INTO `companies`, maps rows through mapCompanyToBusinessRecord(), and its own comment on the by-id branch reads 'Fallback: try business_records table for unmigrated records'. Express server/routes-business-records.ts meanwhile queries the real `businessRecords` table. Both are reachable: edge-function-proxy.ts maps '/api/business-records' -> the business-records edge fn.

Quantify the split per tenant: row counts in `companies` vs `business_records`, how many rows exist in only one, and whether any record ids appear in both. This determines whether the tables are a fork or a completed migration.

Record the dev/prod divergence explicitly: in dev Express serves the canonical table, in prod the edge fn serves `companies`, so the SAME page shows different data depending on environment. This is the CLAUDE.md 'both-divergent' class and must be stated in the decision.

Pick ONE canonical account table and write the decision into docs/crm-canonical-model.md, superseding the CRMX-002 ruling if the evidence goes the other way. Do not leave the doc and the runtime disagreeing.
Re-scope COP-E06 to match the chosen direction — it currently assumes folding `companies` INTO `business_records`, which is backwards if production has already migrated the other way.
State the blast radius for the consuming pages before any migration: LeadsPage, Contacts.tsx, and CustomersPage all read /api/companies, while CrmLeadsPage reads /api/business-records.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 0 / BLOCKER] Found 2026-08-11 while implementing COP-M01; not visible in the original audit, which read the Express routes and the Drizzle schema but not the deployed edge functions. This BLOCKS COP-M01 (nav repoint), COP-M03 (lifecycle views), COP-E03 (retiring the legacy index pages) and re-scopes COP-E06 / CRMX-007. Nothing that moves account data should ship until this is decided. Evidence is static (file reads); acceptance criterion 1 requires confirming against a real deployment before acting. [RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE 2026-08-11 — the DIRECTION is settled; what remains is a data migration, not an architecture decision. Written up as an addendum in docs/crm-canonical-model.md. I originally framed this as 'production migrated the other way, so the canonical choice is unsettled'. The dates disprove that. mapCompanyToBusinessRecord() and scripts/migrate-business-records-to-companies.ts both date to 2026-06-26 (the business_records -> companies direction). CRMX-002 — the canonical doc AND the @deprecated banner on `companies` — landed 2026-07-14 and reversed it. The edge function's `companies` binding therefore PREDATES the decision by ~3 weeks and was simply never updated; CRMX-007, the implementation, was never started. So `business_records` stands as canonical: the most recent authority says so and every artefact contradicting it is older than it. WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS (needs DB access, no decision required): (1) repoint the business-records edge fn at business_records and retire mapCompanyToBusinessRecord — until then Express reads business_records in dev while the edge fn reads companies in prod, and THAT dev/prod split is the real thing blocking COP-M01, not any ambiguity about which table wins; (2) migrate the rows (CRMX-007 / COP-E06) — count both tables per tenant, find rows in only one, check for id overlap; (3) ORDER MATTERS — repointing the edge fn before migrating rows would hide records that currently live only in `companies`.]

userStories.title: Repoint the sidebar at the CrmIndexShell pages for leads, contacts, and companies
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the CRM list pages to have saved views, a board/table toggle, inline editing, and bulk operations, because those were already built in CRM-001..010 but the sidebar still points at the older hand-rolled pages so nobody can reach them.
acceptanceCriteria: RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx 'Sales Hub' children point Leads at /crm/leads (CrmLeadsPage), Contacts at /crm/contacts (CrmContactsPage), and Companies/Customers at /crm/companies (CrmCompaniesPage) — replacing /leads-management (LeadsPage), /contacts (Contacts.tsx), and /customers (CustomersPage).

Before switching, confirm each shell page has parity on the capabilities the legacy page provided (create dialog, CSV export, the filters reps actually use); file any true parity gap as a follow-up rather than silently dropping it.

Each shell page renders saved-view tabs, the table/board toggle where the object supports a board, advanced filters, the column picker, bulk selection, and inline cell editing — i.e. the CrmIndexShell feature set is live for all four object types, not just deals.
matchPatterns on the Sales Hub nav entry still highlight the hub for every legacy path so deep links keep the correct section expanded.
Legacy pages are left routed (not deleted) in this story — COP-E03 retires them once parity is confirmed in a running environment.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes:
[PHASE 0 / NAV] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Highest ratio of impact to effort in the whole report: a one-line-per-object nav change that instantly upgrades three object types. Audit evidence: CrmLeadsPage (261 lines) / CrmContactsPage (176) / CrmCompaniesPage (174) are routed under /crm/* but absent from the sidebar, while nav points at LeadsPage (661), Contacts.tsx (1959), CustomersPage (877). Only deals reaches the shell, via /opportunities. [BLOCKED 2026-08-11 — investigated while starting this story. The repoint is NOT a one-line nav change; four defects gate it. (1) PARITY: the shell had no bulk operations, no CSV export, and hardcoded View/Edit row actions, while the legacy pages have convert / deactivate / assign-owner / delete + export. CLOSED by commit 'feat(crm): add row actions, bulk operations, and CSV export to the CRM shell'. (2) DEAD ROW CLICKS: crm-object-registry detailPath is '/contacts' and '/companies', but App.tsx has NO /contacts/:id and NO /companies/:id route (only /companies/:companyId/contacts), so every row click on the contacts and companies shell pages lands on NotFound. Leads ('/leads/:slug') and deals ('/deals/:id') are fine. (3) COMPANIES BINDING: CrmCompaniesPage + the registry point at /api/companies, the table CRMX-002 marked @deprecated. (4) THE BIG ONE — see COP-B00. NEXT: leads is the only object clear to repoint once COP-B00 is resolved; contacts and companies additionally need detail routes.] [DEFECT (1) REOPENED AND CLOSED PROPERLY 2026-08-19 - the 'PARITY' item was recorded as closed by the row-actions/bulk/export commit, but the page underneath it did not work at all. Three separate faults, all on CrmContactsPage:

(a) THE LIST RETURNED NOTHING, ANYWHERE. CrmDataTable calls GET /api/company-contacts?limit=&offset=&sortBy=&sortOrder= with NO companyId. The company-contacts edge function required companyId and answered 400 'companyId query parameter is required'; Express, for its own part, returned EVERY contact in the tenant as a bare array and ignored limit/offset/search/sortBy entirely. And /api/company-contacts is in crmProxies, so dev hits the edge function too - the page rendered its COP-I04 error state in dev AND prod, not just prod. companyId is now an optional filter on both sides and both return { data, total, page, limit }.

(b) CREATE COULD NEVER SUCCEED. The dialog posted jobTitle, which no column is called (the real one is title) and which neither backend maps, so the title was silently dropped - and company_contacts.company_id is NOT NULL while the form left companyId optional with no way to pick a company, so the insert had to fail. Note the server was never wrong here: contactCreateSchema in server/lib/crm-validation.ts already declared title. The form was the only thing built against the wrong name. Fixed both: field renamed to title, company is now required and chosen from a companies picker that reads companyName ?? businessName ?? business_name (the two backends genuinely label it differently - Express/Drizzle returns businessName, the companies edge fn spreads the raw row and adds companyName).

(c) THREE OF NINE COLUMNS WERE PHANTOM. The contacts registry config named jobTitle, isPrimary and isActive. Against shared/schema.ts:1255 the first two are title and isPrimaryContact, and there is NO isActive column on company_contacts at all - so those columns rendered blank, and sorting or inline-editing them addressed a column the database does not have. Rebound to the real names; isActive DELETED rather than faked (the CLAUDE.md BATCH 7 rule) and replaced with leadStatus, which is real. The statusConfigs block described active/inactive - i.e. the column that does not exist - and now carries the real lead_status values (new/contacted/qualified/unqualified/customer). The edge function's row mapper also invented companyName, ownerName and preferredChannels as hardcoded empties; the first two are gone and preferredChannels, which IS a real column, is now parsed instead of thrown away.

PARITY LOCK: server/lib/contact-list-query.ts + supabase/functions/_shared/contact-list-query.ts hold the query semantics (sort whitelist, limit/offset/page, filters, search) and server/tests/unit/contact-list-query-parity.test.ts (52 tests) fails on drift. Mutation-tested four ways: a sort-mapping change in one copy -> 2 failures, a narrowed search sanitizer -> 6, flipped null ordering -> 1, a raised limit clamp -> 2.

WORTH KNOWING: sortBy is a WHITELIST, not a translation - an unknown value falls back to createdAt rather than reaching either database as an identifier. And the search term is stripped of ,()%*\\"' before it is used: a PostgREST or() filter is comma/paren-delimited with no escape sequence, so searching for 'Smith, Jane' did not return zero rows, it produced a malformed filter. The old contacts fn has the same unescaped pattern and was left alone.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE LEFT IN PLACE: companyQuerySchema caps limit at 500 and the shared parser clamps at 200, so Express 400s on limit=1000 where the edge function would clamp. The frontend never sends more than 100. Not worth loosening the validator for.

STILL BLOCKING THE ACTUAL REPOINT: defect (2) is HALF resolved - App.tsx now has /companies/:id (CompanyDetail), which it did not on 2026-08-11, so company row clicks land. Contacts still have no detail route: the registry's detailPath is '/contacts' and there is no /contacts/:id route and no ContactDetail page, so every row click on the contacts table still lands on NotFound. There is also no single-contact GET on either backend (Express /api/company-contacts/:companyId is a list-by-company, and the edge fn has no GET-with-id branch), so a detail page is a page AND an endpoint, not a route line. Defect (4)/COP-B00 is untouched. ALSO SPOTTED, NOT FIXED: the companies registry config binds a 'name' field while the companies table column is businessName - the same phantom-shape fault as (c), one object over. [DEFECT (2) CLOSED 2026-08-19. Contacts now have a record page and both backends can serve one.

WHAT WAS MISSING WAS AN ENDPOINT, NOT A ROUTE LINE. GET /api/company-contacts/:id did not resolve to a single contact anywhere: Express served a list-by-company on that path, and the company-contacts edge function had no GET-with-id branch at all, so production answered 405. Both now return one contact (404 when it is not in the tenant). The Express list-by-company it replaced was DEAD in both environments and could not have had a caller - /api/company-contacts is proxied to the edge function in dev so Express never saw the request, and prod had no handler; the list-by-company case is served by GET /api/company-contacts?companyId=, which the previous pass added to both sides.

CANONICAL PATH, NOT THE LEGACY ONE. detailPath was '/contacts', which is the legacy Contacts.tsx INDEX page - there is no /contacts/:id route, so a row click landed on NotFound. It is now '/crm/contacts' with a /crm/contacts/:id route, following the deals precedent (dealsConfig already uses /crm/deals) rather than adding a second meaning to a legacy path COP-E04 wants to collapse anyway.

client/src/pages/ContactDetail.tsx renders only real company_contacts columns (shared/schema.ts:1255): the phone/mobile/other/home/fax set, assistant + assistantPhone, reportsTo, ownerId, contactRoles, preferredChannels, favoriteContentType, the mailing and other address groups, birthdate, lastContactDate, nextFollowUpDate, and a link through to the company. The status badge reads its label from the registry's statusConfigs, so the wording cannot drift from the table's.

DEDUP RATHER THAN A SECOND COPY: CompanyDetail.tsx had grown its own pick/pickBool/pickList/formatAddress helpers and ContactDetail needed the same four. Both now import client/src/lib/crm/record-fields.ts, covered by record-fields.test.ts (28 tests). Writing those tests caught a real defect in my own first implementation: a null entry inside a contact_roles JSON array came out as the literal string 'null' in the UI, because String(null) survives filter(Boolean). Fixed in the helper, and the case is pinned.

STILL OPEN ON THIS STORY: the sidebar repoint itself, which is defect (4)/COP-B00. Also noted while wiring this - CrmDataTable's edit action navigates to `${detailPath}/${id}?edit=true` and NO detail page in the codebase reads that query param, so the pencil and the row click do the same thing on deals, companies and now contacts. Pre-existing and repo-wide, not introduced here. [COMPANIES PASS 2026-08-19 - the third object type, same class of fault as contacts, plus one that was breaking the quote builder.

COMPANY SEARCH RETURNED 500, EVERYWHERE. The companies edge function's search filter was or=(business_name.ilike,phone.ilike,EMAIL.ilike,customer_number.ilike,industry.ilike,billing_city.ilike,billing_state.ilike). There is no email column on companies - migration 0000 creates phone, fax and website and no ALTER TABLE ever adds one - so PostgREST answered 42703 and the handler returned 500 'Failed to fetch companies'. /api/companies is in crmProxies, so this was dev as well as production, and it was not confined to the CRM page: client/src/components/quote-builder/CompanyContactSelector.tsx searches this endpoint, so you could not look up a customer while building a quote. The same read appeared in primaryContactEmail's fallback (company.email), which was always undefined; removed.

FOUR OF NINE COMPANY COLUMNS WERE PHANTOM. The registry named name, city, state and employeeCount; the real columns are businessName, billingCity, billingState and employees. Company Name is the FIRST column of the table and rendered blank against both backends. Rebound to the real names. The 'My Companies' default view filtered ownerId, which companies does not have in any form that a user id could match (the nearest column is businessOwner, a free-text person's name), so the view was guaranteed empty - DELETED rather than repointed.

SORTING DID NOTHING. The edge function hardcoded ORDER BY created_at DESC and Express ignored sortBy/sortOrder entirely, so every column header on the companies table was inert. Both now sort through the shared whitelist.

TWO EXPRESS FILTERS NEVER MATCHED. routes-companies.ts filtered c.recordType and c.status; the Drizzle columns are businessRecordType and activity, which is what the edge function had always matched on. So ?status= and ?recordType= silently returned zero rows on Express.

CASING CONTRACT. The companies edge function spreads the raw PostgREST row, so it emitted business_name/billing_city while Express/Drizzle emits businessName/billingCity - whichever names the registry chose would be blank against one backend. The handler now adds camelCase aliases ALONGSIDE the existing keys (added, not swapped, so every current reader keeps working).

REFACTOR: contact-list-query.ts became crm-list-query.ts with a spec per object (sort whitelist, default limit, search columns, filter keys). The contacts call sites moved over unchanged in behaviour; the parity suite is now crm-list-query-parity.test.ts at 62 tests.

NEW GUARD, and this is the part worth keeping: server/tests/unit/crm-list-spec-columns.test.ts (15 tests) asserts every column a list spec names actually exists, read from the Drizzle table definitions via getTableColumns rather than a hand-written list - so it cannot go stale, and renaming a column in shared/schema.ts fails it until the spec follows. Mutation-tested: putting 'email' back into the company search columns fails 5 tests; pointing businessName at a 'name' column fails 2. This is the first automated check in the repo for the phantom-column class of defect that CLAUDE.md's BATCH 7-11 notes keep describing by hand.

NOT VERIFIED, worth a look with data: the companies quickFilter offers lowercase industry values (technology, healthcare, ...) and filters by exact match, so it returns nothing if the stored values are capitalised. No way to check that from here. [DEALS PASS 2026-08-19 - the fourth object type, and the worst of the four. The deals edge function was written against a table that does not exist.

Real columns (migration 0000): title, amount, stage_id, owner_id, created_by_id, company_name, primary_contact_*. The handler used deal_name, deal_value, stage, next_step, business_record_id, created_by, closed_date. /api/deals is in crmProxies, so all of this was dev as well as production.

CREATING A DEAL COULD NOT SUCCEED. The insert wrote six columns that do not exist and omitted stage_id and created_by_id, both NOT NULL. CrmDealsPage's create dialog and LeadDeals' both post here.

EDITING A DEAL FAILED ON THE FIELDS PEOPLE EDIT. The PATCH map and the bulk map both wrote deal_name, deal_value, stage and next_step, so renaming a deal, changing its amount or moving its stage all came back 42703. Fields that happened to be spelled correctly (description, probability, expectedCloseDate, ownerId, source) worked, which is why this was survivable enough to ship.

SEARCHING DEALS RETURNED 500. or=(deal_name.ilike.%term%,description.ilike.%term%) - deal_name is not a column. Same defect as the companies email column found in the previous pass, on a different table.

FILTERING BY STAGE RETURNED 500, and sortBy/sortOrder were ignored (hardcoded ORDER BY expected_close_date ASC), so the deals table's column headers were inert.

SIX COLUMNS WERE BLANK. The handler selects '*' and returned raw snake keys, so expectedCloseDate and createdAt never resolved; the registry additionally named value, customerName and assignedToName, none of which are columns. Rebound to amount and companyName; assignedToName is DELETED rather than faked - the handler avoids FK embeds on purpose (the deals FKs are not reliably in the schema cache) so it cannot resolve owner_id to a name, and primaryContactName, which IS stored on the deal, takes that column. The quick filter and the My Deals view moved from assignedToId to ownerId.

THE STAGE PROBLEM, and what I did NOT do about it. deals.stage_id is NOT NULL and keyed on the legacy deal_stages id space (CRMX-005), but every create surface sends a SLUG from a hardcoded four-item select. New _shared/deal-stage.ts resolves a slug against the tenant's own deal_stages rows at request time. That is a LOOKUP, not a schema change: COP-M07 warns that repointing a writer to the pipeline_stages id space without verifying every existing deal orphans them, and nothing here repoints anything. Two functions on purpose - findStageId never falls back (filtering) and resolveStageId falls back to the front of the pipeline (creating, because stage_id is NOT NULL and the deal has to land somewhere). A tenant with no stages now gets a 400 naming the missing setup instead of a 500. The Stage COLUMN renders again because the handler maps stage_id to the stage name in memory rather than through an FK embed.

TESTS: deal-stage.test.ts (26) mutation-tested three ways - making the filter fall back like create fails 1, treating a missing sort_order as 0 fails 1, dropping punctuation normalization fails 5. crm-list-spec-columns.test.ts now covers deals too (23 total) and pins that deal_name/deal_value/stage/next_step/business_record_id/created_by/closed_date are not columns while stage_id and created_by_id are NOT NULL. The parity suite gained DEAL_LIST_SPEC and a defaultAscending flag so the deals list keeps its soonest-close-date-first default.

ALL FOUR CRM OBJECTS NOW BIND TO REAL COLUMNS. The registry audit that found this is worth repeating whenever a config is touched: read every field name in crm-object-registry.ts against getTableColumns of the backing table. leads was already clean; contacts, companies and deals were not. [THE AUDIT BECAME A GUARD 2026-08-19, and it found that this defect class is repo-wide.

Three passes in a row turned up the same fault by hand - companies.email in a search or(), deals.deal_name in another, deals.deal_value/stage in an insert and two update maps - each one breaking a page that looked finished. Edge functions name columns in STRINGS, so a wrong name is a runtime 42703 that tsc, lint and every non-DB test are blind to.

npm run check:phantom-cols (scripts/check-phantom-columns.ts, wired into CI) reads all 671 Drizzle tables and checks every column literal an edge function hands to PostgREST - .eq/.neq/.gt/.gte/.lt/.lte/.like/.ilike/.is/.in/.contains/.overlaps/.order, the clauses inside .or(), plain .select() lists, and INLINE .insert/.update object literals - against the table its call chain is on. Baseline docs/phantom-columns-baseline.json: 384.

384 is a WORKLIST, not a score. Sampled and confirmed true, straight off the Drizzle definitions: `users` has first_name/last_name and is_active, and NO name, full_name, status, phone or job_title (12 references); `roles` has NO tenant_id, so four handlers filter roles by a tenant column that does not exist; `audit_logs` has `timestamp`, not created_at (though CLAUDE.md separately records that the LIVE audit_logs is a different shape again, so that one may be drift rather than a code bug). And `deals` is still queried as deal_value/stage/value/name/closed_at/weighted_value/assigned_to_id by EIGHT more edge functions beyond the one fixed in the previous pass - commission, crm-goals, dashboards, pipeline, sales-reports, today-dashboard, user-assignments, pipeline-config.

THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENCE. PostgREST leaves .data null on error and this code says `|| 0`, so /pipeline/stats returns a pipeline of zeroes rather than an error - the same fabricated-data symptom the mock dashboards have, from a completely different cause. (That endpoint has no frontend caller and /api/pipeline is unproxied, so it was not worth fixing in this pass; the ones with live callers are.)

BLIND SPOTS, stated so nobody reads a green run as proof of correctness: payloads built as a named variable rather than an inline literal - the deals insert was exactly that, and this tool would NOT have caught it; names assembled at runtime; camel->snake field maps; the 107 tables in no Drizzle schema (skipped, and that count independently reproduces COP-M00's own figure of 107 db:push-created tables); and 15 tables declared twice with different shapes, skipped as ambiguous because there is no way to tell from code which one is live - reporting those would be reporting the check:dup-tables schema collision as a query bug. Filtering the ambiguous ones dropped the raw count from 522 to 384, so about a quarter of the first run was the blog_posts collision rather than new bugs.

Mutation-tested: renaming one .eq('tenant_id') to a typo makes it exit 1 naming the file, line, table, column and the call that introduced it. [BURN-DOWN ROUND 1, 2026-08-19: 384 -> 373. Took the phantom-column worklist by blast radius, starting with the handlers a routed page actually calls.

DASHBOARDS (/api/dashboards/sales, /overview, /today - TodayDashboard.tsx, routed at /today and /dashboard/today). Selected deal_value and stage; the columns are amount and stage_id. `stage` was selected and never read, so it is gone. Not proxied, so this was prod-only: dev goes to Express and works, production got 42703, undefined data and every figure through `|| 0`. The page showed a pipeline of zeroes rather than an error. Now returns 500 with the PostgREST message on the sales branch instead of pretending.

COMMISSION (/api/commission/calculations, /my-earnings - CommissionManagement.tsx, routed). Same shape: deal_value and closed_at, where the columns are amount and actual_close_date. Every rep's calculated commission was silently zero.

A SECOND BUG INSIDE THE FIRST, and it would have survived a naive rename: deals.amount is numeric(12,2) and PostgREST returns numeric as a STRING. `sum + row.amount` CONCATENATES - a commission total of "01500.002400.00" rather than 3900. Both handlers now coerce through the already-tested toNumber from _shared/quote-math.ts rather than growing a third copy.

REPORTS (25 client files - the widest blast radius in the list). Four query modules selected users.name. There is no name column; the table has first_name and last_name. Those queries THROW on error rather than degrading, so every report needing a rep or technician name 500'd. New reports/_queries/user-names.ts holds the column list and the composition so the four call sites cannot drift on what 'Unknown' means; 7 tests, one of which asserts USER_NAME_COLUMNS against getTableColumns(users) so the fix cannot rot.

REPORTS pipeline-funnel: asked deal_stages for stage_name and order_index; the columns are name and sort_order. stages came back empty and the handler fell through to its no-stages-configured fallback, so every tenant's funnel was three status buckets rather than their pipeline - a silent wrong answer, not an error.

REPORTS team: selected business_records.lead_status, which does not exist. The lifecycle column IS `status` and was already in the same select. That query throws, so the whole team report 500'd.

DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED THIS ROUND: the leads edge function's seven refs (business_records.assigned_to / lead_status / qualified_at / qualified_by / qualification_score / qualification_notes / converted_at). assigned_to is a rename (assigned_sales_rep) but the five qualification columns are a FEATURE WITH NO SCHEMA - there is nowhere to write a qualification score. That is a decision about whether to add the columns or drop the workflow, not a rename, and it wants its own pass. [BURN-DOWN ROUND 2, 2026-08-19: 373 -> 365, and the checker got sharper.

SCANNER BLIND SPOT CLOSED FIRST. The checker only read .select('...') in single quotes, so it could not see BACKTICK selects - which is exactly where the long multi-line column lists live. /user/profile named seven phantom columns inside one and the tool had reported none of them. It now reads both quoting styles and STRIPS embedded relations (`alias:relation(...)`) rather than skipping any list containing a paren, so top-level columns around an embed are checked too. That surfaced 7 more real defects immediately, with no false positives left after fixing the aliased-embed case.

THE users TABLE IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE CLUSTER: 27 references across 10 edge functions to name, full_name, status, phone, job_title, department, timezone, locale, avatar_url, activated_at and deactivated_at. The real shape is first_name/last_name, profile_image_url, is_active, and a metadata jsonb.

FIXED THIS ROUND:
  - /user/profile (Settings.tsx, routed). GET selected seven phantom columns, so the error branch fired on EVERY request and the page rendered whatever the JWT carried; PUT wrote the same seven, so saving a profile could not work. Also /user/settings, which composed firstName by splitting a `name` column that does not exist.
  - /users/team - selected full_name, job_title, department and status, and filtered .eq('status','active'). 500 for every tenant.
  - /admin users list - selected phone, job_title and department inside a backtick list.
  - customer-portal service requests - selected created_at on customer_service_requests, which has submitted_at (already in the same select, and what the ORDER BY uses). One column nobody read took the whole list down.

THE DESIGN CALL, and why it is not new columns: phone, jobTitle, department, timezone and locale have nowhere to go. Adding columns means a migration, and COP-M00 records migration generation as currently broken (meta snapshots 22 behind the journal, so db:generate emits ~151 statements of drift and collides on the filename). users.metadata is a real jsonb column that exists today, so _shared/user-profile.ts puts them there. The API shape is unchanged, so promoting them to real columns later is a storage change and not an interface change.

THE SUBTLE PART, pinned by tests: metadata is a SINGLE jsonb column, so a partial profile update has to MERGE or it silently deletes the fields it did not mention - data loss with no error. buildUserProfileUpdate merges, emits nothing at all for an empty body, and one test asserts every key it can emit is a real users column. 28 tests, mutation-tested three ways: replacing instead of merging fails 2, writing blanks for absent fields fails 5, writing avatar_url instead of profile_image_url fails 2.

STILL OPEN in the users cluster, and they are not renames: predictive-dispatch reads users.skills and users.current_location (a technician-dispatch feature with no schema at all - CLAUDE.md already flags that file for phantom TABLES), user-management reads activated_at/deactivated_at (an audit trail that does not exist), and role-management/team-reports/crm-goals/root-admin/quotes/locations still read full_name/status/phone/name/location_id. Those last six are mechanical and are the obvious next slice. [BURN-DOWN ROUND 3, 2026-08-19: 365 -> 352. Three of these were doing real damage beyond a blank field.

SUSPENDING A TENANT REPORTED SUCCESS AND DID NOTHING. root-admin's suspend and activate wrote `{ status: 'suspended' }` to `tenants`, which has no status column (the flag is is_active). PostgREST accepts an update naming no known column as a no-op, the handler saw no error, and returned 'Tenant suspended'. Both now write is_active. The tenant LIST selected status too, so it 500'd outright for every root admin; it now selects is_active and returns a derived `status` string, since the console reads that. Audit logs ordered by created_at, where the column is `timestamp`.

DELETING A LOCATION LOST ITS GUARD. locations counted users at a location with .eq('location_id'), where the column is primary_location_id. The count 42703'd to undefined and fell through `|| 0`, so the 'this location still has users' check never saw anyone and the delete went through.

QUOTES SHOWED NO CUSTOMER. Both the list and the detail path selected `email` from `companies`, which has no email column, so the whole select failed and every quote came back with customer: null. The address book is company_contacts, so the contact email and phone now come from an embedded primary contact.

Also fixed: team-reports, which addressed business_records as deal_value / assigned_to / pipeline_stage (the columns are estimated_deal_value, assigned_sales_rep, sales_stage) - every team report returned zeroes; and crm-goals, which selected full_name and job_title from users and `value` from deals. estimated_deal_value and amount are both numeric, so the sums coerce through toNumber or they concatenate.

DECISION-BLOCKED, DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED: role-management is built on a `roles` table with tenant_id, hierarchy_level, is_system and updated_at. The real roles table is GLOBAL - no tenant_id at all - with level and is_system_role and no updated_at. Renaming the two that exist is trivial, but dropping the tenant filter would make every tenant's custom roles visible to every other tenant, and creating a per-tenant role has nowhere to store the tenant. That is an RBAC visibility decision, not a rename, and it is not mine to make silently. Same class as the leads qualification columns and root-admin's security-alerts endpoint, which queries activity_reports (a sales-activity rollup) for `type = 'security_alert'` - there is no security-alerts table in any schema. [BURN-DOWN ROUND 4, 2026-08-19: 352 -> 336. This one was the worst single defect the checker has found.

NOBODY COULD SIGN UP. supabase/functions/signup/index.ts inserted THIRTEEN columns into `tenants` that the table does not have - industry, company_size, website, address, city, state, zip, country, timezone, plan_slug, billing_cycle, status, trial_ends_at. The real shape is name, slug, is_active, plan, subscription, billing_status, metadata. The insert failed, and the handler returned 'Failed to create organization' for every attempt. client/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx:60 posts straight to this function, and it is unauthenticated, so this is the front door.

Then it got worse: step 2 looked for a role with tenant_id = <new tenant> and, finding none, INSERTED one carrying tenant_id, is_system and updated_at. `roles` has none of those - it is a GLOBAL table seeded by npm run seed:rbac. So even past the tenant insert, signup would have rolled itself back.

FIXES. The company profile goes into tenants.metadata, exactly as the users insert in the SAME FILE already carries phone and status (PA-001 did that fix and the tenants insert next to it was never revisited). plan_slug -> plan; status:'trial' -> billing_status:'trial' plus is_active:true; trial_ends_at -> metadata.trialEndsAt. No migration needed, which matters because COP-M00 records migration generation as broken.

For the role, signup now RESOLVES the seeded COMPANY_ADMIN role instead of inventing a per-tenant one, and returns a named MISSING_ADMIN_ROLE error (rolling the tenant back) if the environment has not been seeded. Roles being global is a real design decision rather than something to route around here - role-management assumes the opposite and is still parked on that call.

TEST: server/tests/unit/signup-tenant-shape.test.ts (30) parses the handler's insert objects and asserts every TOP-LEVEL key is a real column, while allowing nested metadata keys. Mutation-tested: putting `status` back on the tenants insert fails 2, restoring the roles insert fails 1. It also covers the users insert, so the PA-001 fix cannot regress either.

WORTH NOTING FOR THE PATTERN: PA-001 fixed the users insert in this file with the metadata approach and left the tenants insert three steps above it untouched. A fix applied to one insert in a file is not evidence about the others - which is exactly the argument for the static check rather than another careful read.

userStories.title: Restructure the Sales Hub navigation into Work / Sell / Manage groups
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the Sales Hub menu to be grouped by what I am doing, because today it is 17 ungrouped children mixing CRM objects, selling tools, dashboards, and admin settings in one flat list.
acceptanceCriteria: Sales Hub children are grouped under three headings: Work (My Day, Deals, Leads/Contacts/Companies, Tasks), Sell (Quotes, Proposals, Deal Desk, Meetings, Sequences, Web Forms), and Manage (Forecast, Goals, Territories, Commission, Customer Success).
Admin/config entries move out of Sales Hub into Settings: Custom Fields (/settings/custom-fields), Proposal Branding (/proposals/branding), and Pipeline Configuration (/pipeline-config).
Meeting Transcription moves from the Productivity hub into Sell — it is a selling tool, not a productivity utility.
The sidebar component supports a group heading within a hub section (non-navigable label) without breaking collapse, keyboard navigation, or the active-path highlight.
Every moved item keeps its existing route; this story changes grouping and placement only, not destinations.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 0 / NAV] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Audit evidence: RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx 'crm' section has 17 flat children mixing objects, tools, dashboards, and settings; Meeting Transcription sits under Productivity.

userStories.title: Delete the nine unrouted CRM/sales pages (~10,065 lines of dead code)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need dead CRM pages removed, because nine sizeable page components are not routed anywhere in App.tsx yet still appear in every search, creating constant "which page is the real one?" confusion.
acceptanceCriteria: Delete client/src/pages/{DealsManagement,LeadsManagement,customers,TaskManagement,BasicTaskManagement,AITaskScheduling,my-tasks,TaskManagementPage}.tsx after re-confirming each has no lazy() import in App.tsx and no import from any other module.

TerritoryManagement.tsx is NOT simply deleted — first move its reusable logic/components somewhere COP-B09 can revive them (or record in that story exactly what was removed and where to find it in git history), then delete the page.

Re-verify emptiness mechanically before deleting: for each candidate, grep the whole client/src tree for the component name and for the @/pages/<name> path, and confirm zero hits outside the file itself.
Delete any components/hooks that become orphaned as a result and are referenced by nothing else.
Update the ProtectedRoute.tsx doc comment that references LeadsManagement as an example.
npm run check && npm run build && npm run lint pass, and the app boots with no missing-module errors.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 0 / CLEANUP] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Line counts at audit time: DealsManagement 2851, LeadsManagement 1733, customers 1419, TaskManagement 1072, BasicTaskManagement 855, TerritoryManagement 700, AITaskScheduling 629, my-tasks 464, TaskManagementPage 342 = 10,065. Tasks are served by TaskHub at /tasks. CAVEAT: the audit was static (read App.tsx + grep), so re-verify each file is truly unreachable before deleting. [DONE 2026-08-11: all 9 pages re-verified as having ZERO ES imports before deletion (10,065 lines, matching the audit exactly). userStories.title: Repair drizzle migration generation — meta snapshots are 22 behind the journal
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `npm run db:generate` to emit a migration containing only my change, because today it emits 151 statements of already-applied drift and numbers the file into a collision — so no story that needs a schema change can ship.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce first: `DATABASE_URL=<any> npm run db:generate` after any schema edit emits ~2,281 lines / ~151 statements and writes 0040_<name>.sql, which collides with the existing 0040_auto_orders.sql and fails `npm run check:migrations`.

Root cause is the snapshot set, not the journal: drizzle/migrations/meta holds only 15 snapshots (highest 0018_snapshot.json) against 40 journal entries (highest tag 0056_email_sequence_enrollments). drizzle-kit diffs the schema against the LATEST snapshot, so every change made after 0018 is invisible to the differ and gets re-emitted.
The journal itself is healthy — check:migrations passes on a clean tree, all 40 files are journaled, prefixes unique, idx contiguous. Do not 'fix' the journal.

Second defect to fix in the same pass: drizzle-kit names the new file from the journal LENGTH (0040) while the files on disk are numbered up to 0056, so a fresh generate always collides. Reconcile the two numbering schemes.
Rebuild or backfill the meta snapshots so a no-op `db:generate` (schema unchanged) produces an EMPTY migration. That is the pass/fail test.
Then verify the real case: add one nullable column and confirm the generated SQL contains only that column.
Do not hand-author migrations as the fix — CLAUDE.md forbids dropping a .sql into drizzle/migrations, and the journal guard exists to enforce it.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 1 / BLOCKER] Found 2026-08-11 while implementing COP-M04. BLOCKS every story that needs a schema change: COP-M04, COP-M05, and through them the whole Phase 3 copier wedge (COP-B04 Opportunity Radar, COP-B05 Fleet Assessment, COP-B06 installed-base quoting). Related to the SUPA-005 journal-integrity work, but distinct: that guard checks the JOURNAL, which is currently healthy — this is the SNAPSHOT set, which the guard does not check. Consider extending check-migration-journal.mjs to also assert snapshots == journal entries, so this cannot silently regress again. [DIAGNOSED + GUARDED 2026-08-11; RECONCILIATION NEEDS DB ACCESS. Full write-up: docs/COP-M00-migration-tooling.md. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: 15 snapshots (highest 0018) vs 40 journal entries; drizzle-kit diffs against the LAST entry's snapshot, finds none, and falls back to 0018. Missing idx 10-13 and 19-39. MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the correction matters: I assumed the 141-statement drift was already-applied noise, which would have made 'install a current-schema snapshot at idx 39' the fix. It is not. Analysis of the drift shows 107 TABLES IN shared/* THAT HAVE NO MIGRATION AT ALL (71 blog_*, 4 truck_*, plus renewal_*, voice_*, booking_*, chatbot_*, email_autopilot_*, qbr_*, machine_*, meter_*, daily_*, service_*, and 9 singletons including customer_churn_scores and equipment_failure_predictions) — almost certainly created by db:push straight against the DB. Absorbing them into a snapshot would make the drift PERMANENT AND INVISIBLE and leave any migration-built environment missing 107 tables. That trap is documented explicitly so the next person does not fall into it. ALSO IMPORTANT: the non-contiguous file numbering is DELIBERATE — SUPA-002 renumbered 21 orphans to 0036-0056 so their `when` sorts after everything applied (drizzle only applies when lastDbMigration.created_at < folderMillis). Do NOT tidy it; I nearly did. COMMITTED: check-migration-journal.mjs gained check (e) — every journal entry must have a snapshot — as a RATCHET at the known gap of 25 rather than a hard gate, since failing outright would break CI on a pre-existing condition. NOT COMMITTED: any schema or migration change; the generated drift file was inspected and discarded and drizzle/ is byte-identical. REMAINING WORK needs a DB: introspect which of the 107 exist, apply the 21 pending journaled migrations, generate ONE reconciliation migration renamed to 0057+ with idempotent DDL, baseline it, then prove a no-op generate emits an EMPTY migration and drop SNAPSHOT_GAP_BASELINE to 0.]

Dismissing or converting a play records the outcome so play-to-deal and play-to-won conversion can be reported later.
The scan is idempotent — re-running does not duplicate plays for the same trigger.
Every query tenant-scoped; the scan is chunked so a large installed base does not block.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.

userStories.title: Enforce cookie consent: gate Sentry Session Replay and all non-essential telemetry
userStories.description: As a visitor, when I decline non-essential cookies I need that choice to actually take effect, because today the consent banner records a decision that nothing reads: hasConsent() in client/src/lib/cookie-consent.ts:128 is never called anywhere in the codebase, while Sentry Session Replay initializes unconditionally at boot in client/src/main.tsx:24 and records 10% of all sessions plus 100% of error sessions before any consent is given.
acceptanceCriteria: Sentry Session Replay is NOT initialized until hasConsent('analytics') returns true; error reporting without replay may remain if it is justified as strictly necessary and that justification is written into the Cookie Policy.
Sentry replay starts on consent grant (listen for CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT) and stops/flushes on consent withdrawal, without requiring a page reload.
Every other non-essential script, pixel, or SDK added anywhere in client/ is routed through hasConsent(); a repo-wide grep confirms no ungated non-essential telemetry remains.
Global Privacy Control is honored at runtime, not just in the stored record: a GPC signal suppresses analytics and marketing categories before any script loads.
A CI guard (script + npm script, wired like scripts/check-edge-paths) fails when a known telemetry SDK is initialized outside a consent gate, so the pattern cannot be reintroduced.
A unit test asserts hasConsent() default-denies for analytics/preferences/marketing when no record exists and when the stored record version is stale.
Sentry is named in Privacy Policy section 2, in the Cookie Policy category table, and in Subprocessors.tsx (this overlaps LEGAL-007; whichever story lands first satisfies it).

The Cookie Policy claim 'Non-essential cookies are not set until you agree to them' is true as shipped, verified by loading the marketing site with a clean profile and confirming no Sentry replay request fires before consent.
npm run check && npm run lint && npm run build pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P0] Highest-exposure finding of the compliance audit. A consent banner that records a choice and ignores it is worse than no banner: it documents that the obligation was known. This is the fact pattern behind the CIPA session-replay litigation wave (Cal. Penal Code 631/632, $5,000 statutory per violation) and EU ePrivacy/GDPR Art. 6(1)(a) enforcement. Evidence: hasConsent defined at client/src/lib/cookie-consent.ts:128, zero call sites (grep -rn hasConsent client/src excluding the lib itself returns nothing). Sentry.init at client/src/main.tsx:24 with replayIntegration, replaysSessionSampleRate 0.1, replaysOnErrorSampleRate 1.0. Banner IS mounted (client/src/App.tsx:1272) and the consent model itself (GPC handling, versioning, default-deny) is well built; only the enforcement layer is missing. Note the module's own header comment already states the requirement it violates. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. client/src/lib/telemetry.ts is now the single owner of the Sentry lifecycle; main.tsx calls initTelemetry(). Error capture starts at boot (declared strictly necessary in the Cookie Policy); BrowserTracing, Replay AND BrowserSession release-health all wait for hasConsent(analytics) and are attached via Sentry.addIntegration on CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT, stopped on withdrawal without a reload. BrowserSession had to be filtered out of Sentry defaults because it pinged once per page load pre-consent (caught by the browser probe, not by reading the code). GPC made authoritative in hasConsent(): a live signal overrides a stored accept-all for analytics+marketing. Removed replit-dev-banner.js, a cross-origin script client/index.html loaded on every production page view, which a client/src-only scan could never have seen. Guard scripts/check-telemetry-consent.mjs (npm run check:telemetry, wired into ci.yml) enforces three rules and was proven to fail on each. 7 unit tests in client/src/lib/cookie-consent.test.ts. End-to-end proof scripts/verify-telemetry-consent.mjs (npm run verify:telemetry) drives the real production bundle in Chromium: 8/8 PASS, including 0 Sentry requests before consent and tracesSampleRate returning to 0 on withdrawal. Typecheck holds at baseline 1058, build passes.
